chapters.title: Chapter 5680: Rewrite!
paragraphs: <THE Dimensional Provenance Train>
The atmosphere within a particular Dimensional Cabin of the Train was heavy enough to crush the spines of ordinary Primevals.
It was a sprawling expanse of jagged obsidian peaks and swirling violet clouds as the very air hummed with a terrifying, suffocating weight!
At the apex of the highest hill stood a figure draped in pristine shadows, his presence warping the local existence as if reality itself was bending the knee.
This was the Vessel of THE Sealed One!
He stood with his hands clasped behind his back as he looked out over the dark horizon of the cabin. A mesmerizing, purple gold light flickered across his fingertips.

"My future self seems to have already gotten things started as a portion of ITS capabilities have traversed back to me here," THE Sealed One murmured, his voice a charismatic, echoing symphony that carried the undeniable gravity of a grand being.
"The capability to rewrite existence itself... is unfathomably unique."
Behind him, figures of absolute calamity rested upon the jagged rocks!

These were not ordinary lifeforms. Standing in the back was the terrifying entity holding the Mantle of THE Assassin, a being whose very shadow seemed to devour the light around him as he stood with absolute, lethal stillness.
Beside him rested the holder of the Mantle of THE Culling Blade, a towering woman wielding a rusted executioner’s sword as her eyes burned with the weight of shattered Dimensions!
Dozens of other terrifying Descendants populated the hill, each one radiating a sovereign authority that could drown entire realms in blood.
Yet as THE Sealed One spoke, these apex predators did not radiate hostility. They looked towards the shadow-draped figure calmly, and some even wore expressions of warm, absolute devotion!
THE Sealed One turned his head slightly, his unseen eyes sweeping over the gathered weapons of mass destruction.
"How do you all see me as?"THE Sealed One asked smoothly.
The holder of the Mantle of THE Culling Blade blinked, a genuine smile breaking across her scarred features as she rested her massive weapon on her shoulder.
"Master, what are you talking about?"THE Culling Blade asked, her voice filled with absolute loyalty as she took a step forward.
"We have been by your side for ages. You saved me eons ago. I would have been reduced to ash if you had not offered me your hand."
THE Assassin nodded smoothly, his shadowy form bowing in deep reverence.

"You forged us into what we are today,"THE Assassin added, his voice holding the unwavering conviction of a zealot. "You granted us purpose when existence offered us only ruin. We are your blades, Master. We always have been."
WAA!
This was power!
This was a terrifying, absolute violation of the Records! Of the very memories and weavings of Existence!
There was no battle that THE Sealed One had against them.There had been no fight. He had only looked at them!

These powerful lifeforms had their entire histories, memories, and conceptual architectures completely rewritten to see this being as their eternal master, and they did not even know it! Their loyalty was not coerced through fear or bound by contracts. It was forged into the very foundation of their Trueness!
To them, the fabricated memories were the only undeniable reality they had ever known!
THE Sealed One looked at their warm smiles and turned his gaze back to the violet clouds.

His charismatic exterior masked a mind calculating the exact parameters of this horrific capability. The power to rewrite the Records of a lifeform was absolute, but it possessed a specific, highly logical limitation. The only true defense against this capability was if a being possessed the backing of many Causes!

A high density of unspent Causes acted as a conceptual anchor. If he attempted to rewrite a lifeform dripping with Causes, the sheer weight of their anchor would cause massive resistance to the alteration, slowing down the rewrite and potentially alerting the target to the invasion of their existence. But for those lacking sufficient weight, the assimilation was flawless!
His thoughts drifted towards a specific anomaly who should be within this same Train.

Initially, a vessel like Osmont was critical, but he was not deemed an absolute necessity. Yet, the purple gold light flickering across THE Sealed One’s fingers carried a mandate directly from the unbroken timeline ahead of them. His future self had sent the knowledge that out of all lifeforms across the vast expanse, Osmont had to have his existence rewritten.
He had to be made a subordinate.
If left unbound, the trajectory of THE True Human Emperor would become something entirely uncontrollable.
THE Sealed One released a slow, heavy sigh as the sound echoed like a death knell across the obsidian peaks.
He turned his full attention back to the smiling, terrifying apex predators that now existed solely to execute his will. He looked at the flawless weapons he had stolen from the continuum.
"Spread out across the train,"THE Sealed One commanded. "Find me Osmont."
<THE Epigraph of the Hollow Devotion>
There is a story recorded in the deepest, forgotten layers of existence.
It is the story of a brilliant Provenance Lifeform and THE Immense One who desired her.
She was The Weaver of the Silver Rivers. She had cultivated her own truth, generating a sovereign light that refused to bow to the rigid codes of the continuum.
He was THE Architect of the Chained Sky. He looked down from his throne and demanded she stand by his side.
She refused him. Her authority was her own, and she would not subordinate her Weavings to another.
He pursued her again. He offered her rule over thousands of Dimensions and the authority to judge lower lifeforms. She denied him, keeping her eyes fixed on her own path.
He pursued her a third time. He threatened to scorch her entire lineage into ash. She still refused him, choosing the purity of her own Provenance over the safety of a cage.

THE Immense One grew tired. His unfathomable patience fractured. He realized that a sovereign truth could not be coerced through wealth or fear, so he chose the only path remaining to an absolute tyrant. He simply reached into the Records and unmade her truth.
He rewrote her existence.
He altered the foundational ink of her being, erasing her defiance and replacing it with fabricated devotion.

When The Weaver of the Silver Rivers opened her eyes the next day, the defiant spark was gone. Her eyes were filled with absolute, unwavering infatuation. She flew into his arms. She praised his immensity. She offered herself to him completely, declaring that she had loved him since the dawn of time!
He finally had her. He could do exactly as he wished with her mind and her vessel.

But as the epochs passed, the Architect grew bored. The woman sleeping in his arms no longer held the blinding, sovereign light that had drawn his gaze in the first place. She was no longer herself. She was merely an echo of his own power. She was a hollow puppet wearing the skin of a sovereign.
In a fit of terrifying, absolute anger, he closed his hand and collapsed her entire existence into ash!
As her golden blood stained his pristine throne, THE Immense One looked down at the ruin and asked a question to the empty expanse.
"Why did she have to reject me? Why did she make me rewrite existence to be with her?"

This is the tragic, terrifying lesson of the highest authorities. The power to rewrite the Records is the ultimate tyranny. It grants unquestioned loyalty, but it fundamentally destroys the Trueness of the subject.It creates an existence of smiling, hollow reflections.

chapters.title: Chapter 5681: Men and Sovereigns! I
paragraphs: <THE Shared Sky>
Existence was a terrifying, unfathomable expanse!
To forge one’s own Provenance was to declare a singular truth against an existence of competing realities as one stood completely alone in the crushing dark.

A sovereign lifeform could stand alone. They could generate their own immensity and hold back the heavy, rigid laws of existence with their own two hands. This was the nature of an apex predator as it was the path of absolute, unyielding authority!
But a singular pillar had to bear the entire weight of a collapsing sky!

When Those Who Remain looked down from their pristine thrones, they searched for the solitary anomalies. They isolated them and they crushed them because a lone truth was always easier to overwrite than a woven grandeur of sovereign wills. A single light in the dark merely invited the shadows to converge upon it.
There was a profound, glorious strength in shared existence!

To walk beside another Provenance Lifeform was not a dilution of authority as it was an exponential multiplication of Trueness! When two absolute realities intertwined, they did not erase each other. They created a localized continuum that the architects could not simply snuff out with a single thought. They anchored each other to the physical and conceptual planes as their combined weight forced the surrounding existence to bend to their collective will.

Doing everything alone was more than possible for a being burdened by glorious purpose. A solitary sovereign could conquer a Dimension and slaughter their enemies without relying on a single outside variable.
But existence was always easier to face when a lifeform did not have to hold up the heavy sky by themselves.
A tyrant could conquer a timeline alone, but a true Emperor built a court of apex predators to conquer the unknown!
A single sun could only illuminate so much before existence suffocated its light.
But constellations working together could rewrite the entire night sky!
<THE True Human Emperor>
The spring did its work without asking permission, and Noah let it!
Scorching golden essence pressed against his stellar blue-gold frame from every direction as prompts ticked pleasantly at the edge of his vision.
|VERITAS is increasing.|
|PONDUS is increasing.|
Free attributes, ancient secrets, and a scarred Patriarch marinating across from him with Ages of answers behind his teeth.
Noah settled deeper into the bubbling lava with the satisfaction of a man who had walked into a hostile mountain and found a buffet, and he decided to enjoy every course of it.
"You said you can hold off the Immense One,"Noah began. "Before I weigh that offer, I want its other half. What exactly would the one I have taken Thalia from do?"
Aurelius Vasiliou opened his eyes.
For a moment the Patriarch said nothing.
"It will not come screaming," the Patriarch stated, his booming voice dropping into something flatter and far worse.

"An Immense One that has been slighted does not rage. It will arrive at the border of our Elseworld and present the agreement, clause by clause, and it will note that the promised bride is absent or defiled, and then it will name a price that existence itself will call fair."
His massive hand closed slowly into a fist above the water.

"The price will not be Thalia. That is the cruelty of it. Taking her now would be accepting damaged goods, and its dignity will not allow that. So it will take everything around her instead. It will ask for a hundred daughters of the lineage in her place, and it will get them, because refusing turns a collection into a war. It will harvest the cultivated Provenance of our brightest, drained down to the root, taken as interest on the Ages it spent waiting. It will demand a tier of Vasileia emptied and burned, not because it needs the stone, but because a lesson must be visible from a distance. And when it is done, it will thank us for honoring the spirit of the agreement."
"They value their honor and their dignity above all else."Aurelius finished.
Noah listened calmly.
A hundred daughters. A burned tier. And it would say thank you!

"How courteous of it,"Noah remarked dryly. "Okay then, this is the cost. While I still have you talking here, I want to expand my knowledge. Causes, and the Provenances of Provenance Lifeforms. I am fairly new to all this as could you expand my knowledge? It should increase the chances of success of what needs to be done."
Aurelius let out a low rumble that might have been a laugh, and leaned back against the rocky edge as golden lava sheeted off his scarred shoulders.
"Causes..."
He raised one thick finger and pointed upward, past the rocky ceiling, past the mountain, at everything.

"Look at the architecture of reality with clear eyes, and you will find Causes standing under all of it. Behind every Observable Existence, there are Causes bearing its weight. Behind the Unobservable Existences that most lifeforms never even learn to perceive, there are Causes. Behind entire Dimensions, holding their laws upright across the Ages, Causes. They are not treasures scattered for the ambitious to collect. They are structure. Existence itself treats a Cause as a critical support of its own body, and it extends that regard to anything a Cause stands behind. That is the secret the lesser frameworks chase without understanding."
The finger folded back into his fist, and his voice deepened.

"And that is why my kind hungers for them. Across the three hundred and forty-two Lineages, there are few pursuits older or more desperate than the birthing of one’s own Provenance Cause. Not a seized Cause or a harvested one. A Cause generated from your own essence, molded out of your own identity."

"You take the Provenance you generate, and you press it, and you shape it uniquely against everything you are, and you attempt to condense an aim so complete that it steps apart from you and stands on its own as structure. It is brutally hard."
His eyes locked onto Noah with blazing intensity!

"A birthed Cause is passive backing. It is power that stands guard over you while you sleep, asking nothing, draining nothing, generated once and holding forever. And above everything else, it is one of the finest resistances against THE Immense Ones that a sovereign can possess."
WAA!

"Causes fortify an existence. When you carry them, existence registers you the way it registers a Dimension, as critical structure, as a thing whose alteration or erasure costs the continuum itself. Existence looks at Causes as critical structure. And so should we."
Noah’s endlessly blue eyes shone!
Causes remained grand and paramount!
In the depths of THE Infiniverse, at this very moment, he sought to have reborn Laestrygonian who were capable of natively birthing new Causes- what Provenance lifeforms had to work hard to do!
A slow, delicious smile threatened the corner of his mouth!

chapters.title: Chapter 5682: Men And Sovereigns! II
paragraphs: "And what about Provenance itself?" Noah asked, genuinely curious now. "What identity does the arbiter of the Vasiliou carry?"
Aurelius smiled for the first time, and it was not a warm expression. It was the smile of a man being asked to show a weapon he was proud of.

"Every Provenance Lifeform ripens into an identity, sooner or later. My daughter’s ripened toward you, across all time, which is why I did not kill you instantly for doing all this. Because I know most that our Provenances...do not lie."The steam rolled between them.
"And mine ripened on a wall."
The golden waters around him began to hum!
"I am THE Provenance of THE Unfallen Vanguard,"Aurelius declared, and the pressure in the cavern thickened until the surface of the spring flattened beneath it!

"It is a simple identity. It is the truth that the line I stand in front of does not break while I am standing. Not a shield as a shield is a thing that takes the blow. I am the truth that the blow accomplishes nothing. Eleven times, powers came for this Elseworld across the Ages. Eleven times, I was the last thing standing between them and everything behind me. Eleven times, I did not fall. My Provenance is the accumulated weight of every stand, and it grows heavier each time, and there are beings in this continuum who turn around when they learn who is holding a wall, because arguing with an identity that has never once failed is arguing with existence itself."
HUUM!
The declaration settled, and Noah gave it the honest respect it deserved!
A grand identity, forged the hard way, worn by a man who had bled for every gram of its weight!
He was rather starting to like his father-in-law.
"Which is why my offer is real,"Aurelius added, sinking back into the lava. "Holding a fort is not a favor I am doing you. It is the single thing in existence I am best at."
"I understand now."Noah said pleasantly. "What about The Atlas Elseworlds?"
Aurelius scooped a handful of golden lava and let it pour through his fingers.

"Atlas engineered the concept of Elsedimensions itself, and the ones he built personally are a different order of thing than ours. Ours are blind spots. His are locked rooms. No Immense One has ever entered one as it is not for lack of trying. The doors do not refuse them the way our boundary refused nothing today. The doors simply do not exist for them. An architect can stand on the exact coordinates of an Atlas Elseworld and perceive empty dark. He built with their blindness as a material."
Wow!
This Atlas seemed grander and grander as one had to wonder how he was ever killed!

"Inside, they are said to be workshops. Testing grounds. Some say gardens. Our Lineage has sent expeditions across nine of his known Elseworlds over the Ages. We recovered tools from the outer chambers. Lesser inventions. Enough to know the deep rooms exist. We never opened one."
The Patriarch’s eyes hardened.

"We are not the only ones searching. Every Lineage with ambition scours them. But worse than the Lineages are the leashed. Some Provenance Lifeforms serve Immense Ones. Willingly, some, bought with patronage. Unwillingly, others, bent by agreements older than their own births."

"An Immense One that cannot enter an Atlas Elseworld can still send a sovereign inside on its behalf. When you walk his halls, you will meet others of our kind, and you will have no way of knowing whose hands truly move them. Some will be searchers like you. Some will be gloves worn by beings who could not fit through the door. Treat every Provenance Lifeform you meet inside an Atlas Elseworld as a question you have not answered yet."
|VERITAS has increased by 1.|
Noah’s smile widened by a fraction. Gloves worn by beings who could not fit through the door. He was already looking forward to shaking a few of those hands.
"Last question, then," he said."I was asked this myself not long ago as I wonder...How does a Provenance Lifeform die?"
"Badly, and rarely, and almost always to the same three causes."Aurelius counted them off with grim efficiency.

"Overwhelming convergence, which is what took Atlas. Enough Immense Ones agreeing to spend themselves at once. The second is the slow way. A sovereign who stops generating, who lets their identity go stale, thins across the Ages until existence stops making room for them. We call it Fading. Those below us are what fading leaves behind."

He gestured at the pristine golden skeletons resting in the depths of the spring. "The strongest of my line chose to fade here, in these waters, so that what remained of their generation would feed the ones who came after."
He said it evenly, and moved on.
"And the third cause is...ourselves."
The Patriarch’s voice went quiet for the first time.
"A sovereign at war with its own truth. It is rare. I have seen it once, and I will not describe it in these waters."
Silence held the cavern, and the steam rolled across the golden skeletons below.
Then Aurelius rose!

The golden lava fell away from his towering frame in sheets. He floated, upright and immense, wreathed in steam and the weight of eleven held walls, and he came to a stop directly before THE True Human Emperor, looking down with the full imposing gravity of a father, a Patriarch, and a vanguard that had never fallen.
Aurelius began, his voice filling the cavern to its edges.

"I raised that girl from the time she could fit in one of my hands. I taught her to stand before she could float, and I taught her to argue before she could weave, and I have watched every Age of her existence bend toward a stubbornness she absolutely did not get from her mother. She is the light of my existence."

"I bargained her away once because I weighed one daughter against one Lineage and made the choice a Patriarch makes, and I have hated the choice of it every day since. So...should anything happen to her, there is no boundary, no Dimensionality, and no identity of any Provenance that will stand between you and me."
BOOM!

"We are Provenance Lifeforms. We are also men. Men take care of those who depend on them, as they cannot let them down. I will hold the fort of my people against an Immense One. You will go across the Atlas Elseworlds and bring us back something of sufficient value, because all of us now enter a battle for survival. Do we have an agreement, O Human Dreamer?"
BOOM!
The declaration struck as the golden waters flattened, and the skeletons at the bottom seemed to listen!
Noah looked up at the floating Patriarch, and he smiled.
"We have an agreement,"Noah said, rising through the golden lava to meet the Patriarch’s gaze as his stellar blue-gold body blazed.
"I am a Dreamer, and my Dreams can be grand. What others could not find...may simply show itself to me."
He paused, and his endlessly blue eyes drifted, with unhidden and cheerful greed, toward the depths of the spring.
"Oh, by the way. Can I take one of the golden skeletons down below here?"

"What identity does the arbiter of the Vasiliou carry?"
Aurelius smiled for the first time, and it was not a warm expression.
It was the smile of a man being asked to show a weapon he was proud of.
"Every Provenance Lifeform ripens into an identity, sooner or later.
My daughter’s ripened toward you, across all time, which is why I did not kill you instantly for doing all this.
Because I know most that our Provenances...do not lie."The steam rolled between them.
"And mine ripened on a wall."
The golden waters around him began to hum!
"I am THE Provenance of THE Unfallen Vanguard,"Aurelius declared, and the pressure in the cavern thickened until the surface of the spring flattened beneath it!
"It is a simple identity.
It is the truth that the line I stand in front of does not break while I am standing.
Not a shield as a shield is a thing that takes the blow.
I am the truth that the blow accomplishes nothing.
Eleven times, powers came for this Elseworld across the Ages.
Eleven times, I was the last thing standing between them and everything behind me.
Eleven times, I did not fall.

My Provenance is the accumulated weight of every stand, and it grows heavier each time, and there are beings in this continuum who turn around when they learn who is holding a wall, because arguing with an identity that has never once failed is arguing with existence itself."
HUUM!
The declaration settled, and Noah gave it the honest respect it deserved!
A grand identity, forged the hard way, worn by a man who had bled for every gram of its weight!
He was rather starting to like his father-in-law.

"Holding a fort is not a favor I am doing you.

Aurelius scooped a handful of golden lava and let it pour through his fingers.

Ours are blind spots.
His are locked rooms.
No Immense One has ever entered one as it is not for lack of trying.
The doors do not refuse them the way our boundary refused nothing today.
The doors simply do not exist for them.
An architect can stand on the exact coordinates of an Atlas Elseworld and perceive empty dark.
He built with their blindness as a material."
Wow!
This Atlas seemed grander and grander as one had to wonder how he was ever killed!
"Inside, they are said to be workshops.
Testing grounds.
Some say gardens.
Our Lineage has sent expeditions across nine of his known Elseworlds over the Ages.
We recovered tools from the outer chambers.
Lesser inventions.
Enough to know the deep rooms exist.
We never opened one."
The Patriarch’s eyes hardened.

Every Lineage with ambition scours them.

Some Provenance Lifeforms serve Immense Ones.
Willingly, some, bought with patronage.
Unwillingly, others, bent by agreements older than their own births."

Some will be searchers like you.
Some will be gloves worn by beings who could not fit through the door.
Treat every Provenance Lifeform you meet inside an Atlas Elseworld as a question you have not answered yet."
|VERITAS has increased by 1.|

Gloves worn by beings who could not fit through the door.
He was already looking forward to shaking a few of those hands.

Enough Immense Ones agreeing to spend themselves at once.

A sovereign who stops generating, who lets their identity go stale, thins across the Ages until existence stops making room for them.
We call it Fading.
Those below us are what fading leaves behind."

He said it evenly, and moved on.

The Patriarch’s voice went quiet for the first time.
"A sovereign at war with its own truth.
It is rare.
I have seen it once, and I will not describe it in these waters."

chapters.title: Chapter 5683: Ten Nanoseconds! I
paragraphs: <THE Creature>
A Dimension about to change hands holds its breath heavily.

The burning skies of THE Vhelgaros hung low and red over a plain of cracked black stone that stretched across an entire Observable Existence, and upon that plain, two armies faced each other in a silence so heavy that even the wind had chosen a side and stopped moving!
On one side stood the army of THE Creature.

Hundreds of Primeval Ones floated in loose, grand formations behind him, titans of bone and Ego and petrified starlight, generals and soldiers alike gathered across multiple Observable Existences under the banner of a single masked figure wreathed in obsidian and white-gold flames.

They had knelt to him one by one across this campaign, some through defeat and some through awe, and every one of them now watched their Great Ruler hover at the front of their formation with the calm of a being who had never once needed to raise his voice to be obeyed!
And on the other side... stood the monsters of the old order!

The seated ruler’s army sprawled across the horizon, and it was a stranger army by far, because Primevals and Descendants stood mixed within it, the bred children of THE Immense Ones marching beside the ancient titans they usually scorned, unified beneath a single monstrous bloodline!
At their head towered the ruler of THE Vhelgaros.
Ghurvakh, THE Horned Sovereign!
He was a mountain of cursed majesty!
His massive body stood hunched and coiled with terrifying power, gnarled arms thick as fortress pillars hanging low, a heavy tail of plated muscle dragging furrows through the black stone behind him.

Horns erupted from everywhere upon him, curling from his skull, his shoulders, his spine, his forearms, a forest of cracked golden horn that had grown wild across Ages, and beneath the horns his flesh was grey and ancient and carved with old glowing wounds that had never fully agreed to close. An omen given a throne. A curse that had out-lived everything that cursed it!
And beside him stood his wife.

Descendant Ilvexa carried the same monstrous grammar in a leaner frame, her horns sweeping back from her skull in long elegant curves of black gold, her hunched shoulders draped in imperial silks that no tailor had ever designed for a body like hers, her clawed hands folded with a courtly grace that made the monstrousness more unsettling rather than less.
She was a Descendant of THE Immense Ones who had been born an omen and had made the omen regal, and her burning eyes held the only thing on that entire side of the battlefield that resembled caution!

THE Creature looked at the two of them and understood the arrangement of this Dimension in a single glance. A Primeval One of terrifying depth, and a Descendant whose lineage kept the architects’ favor flowing. Power married to permission. A monopoly with horns!
And above all of it... existence itself had come to watch!
Two eyes hung in the burning sky.

They were not clouds and they were not suns. They were gazes, vast and lidless, pressed through the firmament from somewhere unfathomably far above, each one large enough to reflect the entire battlefield in its depths, and every lifeform on the plain below could feel the weight of their attention crawling across their existence like the shadow of something too large to have a shape!
Waves of information bloomed across the whole Dimension, cascading into the minds of every Primeval and Descendant present, for the Ruling wished ALL of its audience informed!
|Two of THE Immense Ones have turned their gazes upon THE Narrative of Existence: The Grand Succession.|
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER has arrived to spectate. It adores successions. It adores them best when they are wet.|

|THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR has arrived to spectate. It has consumed the endings of ten thousand dynasties and declares most of them bland. It hopes, without much optimism, that this one will have flavor.|
The two gazes were nothing alike, and everyone beneath them could feel it!

The eye on the left trembled constantly with something that could only be called mirth, its vast iris quivering the way a throat quivers around laughter that never ends, and the pressure that rolled off it was hot and eager and horribly festive, as though slaughter were a holiday and it had arrived early to get a good seat!

The eye on the right did not move at all. Its attention lay across the battlefield cold and flat and evaluating, the gaze of a critic at a meal, and its pressure was somehow worse, because the left eye wanted everyone to die entertainingly, while the right eye had already concluded that most of them would die poorly and was simply waiting to be proven wrong!
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER looks forward to the bloodbath!|
|THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR reminds the participants that anticipation is the finest seasoning, and that they are taking too long.|

The armies shuddered beneath the information! Lesser Primevals pressed themselves lower to the stone. Descendants clutched at their lineages like children clutching blankets. To be watched by one Immense One was a legend. To be watched by two was a sentence!
THE Creature floated at the front of his army, looked up at the two vast eyes with his masked face, and gave them exactly as much attention as he gave the wind.
Then he looked at Ghurvakh, THE Horned Sovereign, and he weighed him honestly.

The old monster was stronger than him! It was not close. The Sovereign’s depth rolled off his horned frame in slow tectonic waves, Ages of hoarded authority packed into cursed flesh, and behind him his mixed army outnumbered THE Creature’s Primevals by a wide and simple margin. If the two armies met, THE Creature’s side would pay a toll of blood so vast that victory would be indistinguishable from ruin!
A lesser ruler would accept the toll. Rulers had been spending their people that way since the first crown.
THE Creature raised his voice, and it rolled across the plain!
"A Great Ruler does not watch and lead all his people to a massacre if he can prevent it,"THE Creature declared. "Leave our armies behind, as you and I can duke it out. Winner takes fuckin all."
BOOM!
The battlefield went still in an entirely new way!

Hundreds of Primevals on both sides stared at the masked figure! A duel! A succession of an entire Dimension, dozens of Observable Existences, two full armies and a married monopoly of Ages... settled between two beings alone!
Beside the Horned Sovereign, Descendant Ilvexa’s burning eyes narrowed, and she frowned!

She did not speak aloud. Her caution moved through the marriage-weavings between them instead, silent and urgent, and everyone watching could read its meaning from her clawed hand closing around her husband’s gnarled forearm.
Do not do this. We hold the numbers. We hold the ground. Do not hand the challenger the only battlefield where his weakness does not count!
Ghurvakh, THE Horned Sovereign, looked down at his wife’s hand.

Then he looked at the masked Great Ruler floating before two armies, alone, offering to spare both sides the grave, and something ancient and prideful and long-bored moved behind the old monster’s burning eyes. He had sat this throne for Ages. He had collected tribute and permission and the slow rust of unearned peace. And here, at last, was a thing his own size, speaking the old language!
The Horned Sovereign gently removed his wife’s hand from his arm.
"Agreed," Ghurvakh rumbled, and his voice cracked the stone plain for miles!
WAA!
|The terms of THE Grand Succession have been amended!|
|The Leading Conqueror and the Seated Sovereign have agreed to single combat. Winner takes all. The Dimension itself shall bear witness and enforce the outcome.|
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER is DELIGHTED! It declares this the correct and proper shape of a succession and showers the battlefield with its approval!|
|THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR concedes, grudgingly, that the meal has become interesting.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5684: Ten Nanoseconds! II
paragraphs: The sky itself seemed to lean closer! The pressure of the two vast eyes doubled, hot mirth and cold appetite pressing down together, and torrents of Existential Moirai began to pour into the space between the two rulers, golden and thick, the Ruling setting its table for the grandest single exchange this Dimension had ever hosted!
The armies moved!

Hundreds of Primevals and Descendants flowed outward and around in vast slow currents, forming an enormous ring across the black plain, titans of bone and omen-blooded children of the architects circling shoulder to shoulder as spectators to the fate of their entire Dimension. The ring closed and the center emptied.
And the two rulers walked toward each other!

Ghurvakh came forward with slow seismic steps, his tail carving the stone, his forest of golden horns beginning to burn! THE Creature drifted forward to meet him, obsidian and white-gold flames trailing off his body, small before the horned mountain and entirely unbothered by the difference!
Behind THE Creature, unseen by every other existence on the plain, the massive statue followed.
It smiled brutally as it walked, and its voice arrived for him alone.
"I never expected something seemingly foolish from you," the statue said, and there was a strange, almost respectful curiosity threaded through its brutality.
"You had a higher chance of winning with the army. But by yourself... this is adversity you cannot overcome."
The statue had weighed the Horned Sovereign the same way THE Creature had, and it had reached the same honest sum!
THE Creature nodded calmly as he walked!
"I know," THE Creature said.
And then he said the thing that shocked even a remnant of Ages!

"So I am making a gamble with my existence. You have been seeking control of me... I give you ten Nanoseconds of full control of my existence, in exchange for clearing the obstacle ahead of me. After you deal with it, you are free to do what you wish with the remaining time."
The statue stopped walking!
Its brutal smile faded, and for the first time in this entire campaign, for the first time perhaps in Ages, its carved face became grim! Full control. Freely given!
The thing it had circled and bargained and told stories toward, offered up in a single flat sentence, with conditions attached and a clock of ten Nanoseconds strapped to its wrists!
THE Creature closed his eyes!
And the statue MOVED!
It crossed the space between them faster than any measurable speed, faster than the concept of the space existing at all, and it smashed into the body of THE Creature!
CRACK!
Ghurvakh, THE Horned Sovereign, ROARED!
The sound flattened the burning clouds! The old monster surged forward across the emptied center of the ring, and as he came, he pulled his full arsenal into the light!

Chains of screaming gold erupted from his hunched back, and dragging at the ends of those chains came his hoarded Ages, multiple First Causes blazing like shackled suns, and beside them, miniaturized Observable Existences, entire compressed realities bound and dragged behind him as weapons, the plunder of a monopoly that had taxed a Dimension for eternity!
It was the arsenal of a true apex! It was a charge that could unmake armies!
And across from it, THE Creature opened his eyes.

They were pure white. There were no pupils. There was nothing in them at all that had ever been THE Creature, only a flat, bottomless, ancient white, like twin windows opened onto something that had been waiting behind a door for a very long time.
The body of THE Creature raised one hand, and tapped the air, emotionlessly, once.
The Horned Sovereign popped.

There was no exchange! There was no clash of Causes, no contest of chained Existences, no battle at all! One instant a mountain of cursed majesty was charging with the hoarded arsenal of Ages screaming behind him, and the next instant his entire massive body burst like a bloody balloon, and what sprayed outward was not blood and was not flesh, for every fragment of Ghurvakh, THE Horned Sovereign, ruler of THE Vhelgaros for Ages beyond counting, turned to pure white ash before it could even land!
The chains fell. The shackled First Causes rolled loose across the black stone like dropped marbles. The miniaturized Observable Existences drifted, suddenly ownerless.
Silense!

An immense, total, crushing silence swallowed the entire Dimension! Hundreds of Primevals stood frozen in the great ring! Descendant Ilvexa stared at the white ash drifting where her husband had existed, her clawed hand still half-raised from her final warning! Even the torrents of Moirai hung motionless in the air, as though the Ruling itself needed a moment!
And the thing wearing THE Creature did not celebrate, and did not look at the ash, and did not acknowledge the succession it had just settled with a tap.
It looked around, instead, at the edges.

The white, pupilless eyes swept slowly across the boundaries of THE Vhelgaros, and they saw the faint crystallized barriers at the far borders, the streaking of the burning sky, the deep structural hum beneath the black stone, the signature of a Dimension that was not sitting still in the void but MOVING, coupled and chained and dragged along linear tracks through the crossing-dark!
THE Vhelgaros was a Dimensional Cabin!

This entire Dimension, this entire succession, this entire Narrative, was one carriage among many upon THE Dimensional Provenance Train of Existence, rushing forward through the lethal dark toward the architects’ grand design!
The thing in THE Creature’s body looked at the edges of its moving cage, and then it looked up.
At the two eyes.
It raised THE Creature’s left hand and waved it once, and a bow appeared!

The bow was pure white! It was tall as the wielder and taller, a single flawless arc of blinding white authority with a string of compressed brilliance, and the instant it materialized, every Primeval and Descendant in the great ring felt their existence scream at them to be anywhere else!
The white-eyed figure nocked nothing, and drew!
The string came back, and power began to accumulate!

It built and built and BUILT, white authority folding into itself in silent detonations, and the pressure of the draw alone rolled outward across the ring in expanding rings of pure weight, and half of the surrounding army, hundreds of Primeval Ones and omen-blooded Descendants who were not even the targets, simply fainted where they stood, titans of Ages collapsing across the black stone like scythed wheat as the accumulating force scraped their consciousness flat!
And the bow rose.
It rose past the horizon. It rose past the burning clouds.
It aimed at the two eyes of THE Immense Ones!
Pure horror swallowed everyone still conscious in THE Vhelgaros!

Primevals who had knelt to tyrants for eternity, Descendants born from the very lineages of the beings above, all of them watched the white bow settle its aim upon the twin gazes of the architects themselves, and every single one of them understood that they were witnessing something that did not happen, that had never happened, that could not happen!
One did not aim at THE Immense Ones!
One did not even look at them for too long!
The white-eyed thing wearing THE Creature released.
Two shots, loosed simultaneously!

They surged upward like ascending spears of absolute white, and the power packed inside them was unfathomably grand, layered and braided and WRONG, multiple unique Causes swirling within each shot alongside an unknown power that no information named and no Records dared annotate, and they crossed the entire height of the burning sky in less time than a scream takes to begin, and they smashed directly into the two gazes of THE Immense Ones!
BOOM! BOOM!
The moment the impacts landed, all of existence within this Dimension began to shake!

The black plain heaved! The crystallized borders of the Dimensional Cabin screamed across their entire length! The burning sky tore and bled light from horizon to horizon, and through the tearing, from somewhere unfathomably far above, roars echoed down into THE Vhelgaros, vast and layered and existence-filling, roars of pure incredulity and gathering rage, the sound of two beings who had come to watch a bloodbath discovering that the bloodbath had looked back and reached UP!
They weren’t hurt or even touched at all, but their dignity...oh their dignity!
And down on the shaking plain, the white faded.

The pupilless light drained out of THE Creature’s eyes, and his own gaze returned to him, and he came back to himself standing beneath a torn and screaming sky with a fading white bow in his hand and ten spent Nanoseconds behind him.
He looked tired and heavy. The weight of the possession sat on his body like a debt already being collected.

And then his expression became grave, gravely still, because the roars from above were still echoing, and the sky was still blazing, and he looked up, slowly, to see exactly what the thing he had given control to... had done!

The two vast eyes above THE Vhelgaros burned through the torn and bleeding sky, and the pressure that had been mirth and appetite only moments ago curdled into something that made every surviving lifeform on the black plain forget how to breathe!
Prompts slammed down across the entire Dimension, and for the first time, Existence itself felt like a wound!
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER has stopped laughing.|
|THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR declares this meal RUINED. It has been struck. STRUCK. In ten thousand dynasties of endings, nothing has ever dared to season itself.|
|The spectators’ grievance is being drafted into the Records!|
|Judgment gathers.|
WAA!
And above the plain, the sky began to fill with swords!

Existential Moirai, the golden currency of fate itself, poured out of the two burning gazes and condensed, and it did not condense into showers of blessing or torrents of reward! It condensed into blades! Thousands upon thousands of golden swords materialized across the entire ceiling of the Dimension, each one long as a mountain is tall, each one aimed downward, a harvest of judgment stretching from horizon to horizon above two armies, one throne of ash, and a single masked figure!

The meaning required no information! The swords were not aimed at THE Creature alone. They hung over EVERYTHING. Every Primeval who had circled. Every Descendant who had watched. Every living fragment of a Dimensional Cabin that had hosted the insult! Two of Those Who Remain had been struck before an audience, and the audience itself had become part of the offense, and dignity of that magnitude was not restored by killing a culprit.
It was restored by deleting a venue!
Primevals wailed across the plain! Descendants clutched their lineages and screamed pleas up at the very beings preparing to erase them.
Ilvexa, widowed for less than a minute, stared up at the sword-filled sky over her Dimension with her clawed hands hanging open at her sides!
And THE Creature looked up at the thousands of blades of judgment, and he did not kneel, and he did not run.
He gazed up defiantly, obsidian and white-gold flames rising off his frame, tired and heavy and utterly unbowed, and he spoke, quietly, to the presence that only he could perceive!
"Why did you do that."

It was not a demand or an accusation. It was the flat question of a bearer who had paid ten Nanoseconds of his existence for one obstacle cleared, and had woken to find his entire Dimension standing under a harvest of golden swords!
And for the first time!
For the first time in this entire campaign, the statue behind him... was quiet.
No brutal smile. No parable. The massive stone face stared up at the sword-filled sky with an expression THE Creature had never seen carved upon it, and it said absolutely nothing at all!
The silence told him more than any answer could have, and none of what it told him was comforting!
Above, the swords finished gathering. The two burning gazes narrowed in unison. The entire golden harvest angled downward as one, thousands of blades drawing back for a single, Dimension-ending fall!
And then the sky opened a third time.
HUUM!
Between the two burning gazes, without arrival and without announcement, a third eye simply came to exist!

It was nothing like the others! Where the Butcher’s gaze quivered with heat and the Connoisseur’s lay flat and cold, this new eye was vast and soft and heavy-lidded, a deep luminous gold framed by long drifting strands of light that fell around it in slow, unhurried waves, and its pressure did not crawl or crush or evaluate!

Its pressure simply settled, over everything, the way dusk settles, feminine and grand and immeasurably old, and beneath it the rage-weather of the other two gazes was flattened into stillness like candle flames under a dropped blanket.
The eye blinked, once, slowly.
And the thousands of golden judgment-swords filling the sky... dispersed!

They did not fade with dignity. They were swept aside, all of them at once, unmade across the whole ceiling of the Dimension by a single lidded glance, scattered into loose harmless Moirai that drifted down over the armies like warm rain.
Waves of information bloomed, and even the Ruling’s voice seemed careful with these ones!
|A third gaze has arrived.|
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW looks upon THE Vhelgaros.|
|She rarely watches anything anymore. She finds that most things remind her of something better, and then are not it.|

The two burning gazes ROILED! Their outrage crashed against the newcomer’s dusk-heavy calm, and their protest arrived for all to read, because beings of their nature did not know how to be indignant privately!
|THE CACKLING BUTCHER protests! It was STRUCK! Its dignity demands this Cabin’s erasure! The honor of Those Who Remain is not negotiable!|
|THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR protests! A spectator’s sanctity was violated! Precedent demands a deletion! What is dignity worth if insult goes unpaid?!|
The third eye regarded the two of them with its heavy-lidded gold, and its reply arrived with the weight of a being for whom their entire honor-culture was a noise happening somewhere beneath her!
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW replies: I do not care.|
The information sat there, four words and a period, and the entire Dimension read it in stunned silence!

|THE REMINISCING WIDOW continues: You came to watch blood and were splashed by it. That is what the front row costs. You may collect your dignity from me, if either of you believes you can carry it home afterward.|
The two burning gazes went very, very still!

|THE REMINISCING WIDOW adds, softly: Besides. Something below drew back a bow I have not seen drawn in a very long age. I am taking this grievance, and both of you, elsewhere. The Narrative will conclude untouched. Do not make me repeat myself. I find repetition exhausting, and I find both of you exhausting, and I was having a rather pleasant memory before all of this.|

It looked at THE Creature, standing small and masked and defiant upon the ruined black plain. And then, in a moment that turned his flames cold, the vast feminine gaze moved a fraction further, past his shoulder, and settled with unhurried precision upon the exact empty space where the statue stood!
The space that no other existence in this Dimension had ever perceived!

|THE REMINISCING WIDOW departs.|
BOOM!

A blinding gold light erupted across the entire sky, dusk-soft and absolute, swallowing the burning gazes of THE CACKLING BUTCHER and THE STARVING CONNOISSEUR whole, and when the light faded, the sky of THE Vhelgaros was empty!
All three Immense Ones were gone!

The torn firmament slowly began to knit itself. The bleeding light dimmed. The crossing-dark streaked past the distant crystallized borders of the Cabin, indifferent as ever, and the only sounds on the plain were the settling of white ash and the breathing of two armies that had just survived their own execution.
Silence held for a long, long moment.
Then, across the vast ring of the battlefield, hundreds of Primevals and Descendants slowly turned and looked at each other, and the same stunned understanding moved through every one of them.

They had stood beneath a sky of judgment-swords and lived because a third architect had swatted the wrath of two others aside like a bothersome insect and then LEFT with them!
And at the center of all of it, tired flames burning low, stood one masked figure.
Slowly, hundreds of gazes converged upon THE Creature!

And the Ruling, which had waited with impeccable manners through the entire catastrophe, finally delivered its verdict, cascading in grand golden text before his eyes as the statue silently translated every line!
|THE Narrative of Existence: The Grand Succession has concluded.|
|The Leading Conqueror has usurped the Seated Sovereign in single combat, witnessed and enforced by the Dimension itself.|
|Winner takes all.|

|You are now the Sovereign Ruler of THE Vhelgaros and all Observable Existences within this Dimensional Cabin. All standing tributes, holdings, and territorial weavings of the former ruler transfer to you.|
|Spoils of Succession: the unbound First Causes of the fallen Sovereign. The miniaturized Observable Existences held in his chains. The accumulated hoard of an Age-long monopoly.|
|Narrative Reward: unfathomable Existential Moirai floods the Leading Conqueror. Your Mantle of THE RULER deepens. Your bearing is now etched into Narrative History.|
|Addendum, recorded with interest: you have survived the grievance of two of Those Who Remain, and drawn the intervention of a third. Existence will remember this Succession for a very long time.|

Waves of golden Moirai poured down out of the healing sky and sank into his frame, and his obsidian and white-gold flames rose and rose, fed by the fortune of an entire concluded Narrative, until his figure hovering above the plain burned like a signal fire visible from every Observable Existence in the Cabin!
THE Creature let it burn!

He rose slowly and grandly into the air above the white ash of the old order, his flames streaming, the loose First Causes of the fallen Sovereign drifting up around him like a crown assembling itself, the miniaturized Observable Existences settling into slow orbits about his body, and he looked down upon the massed hundreds of Primeval Ones and omen-blooded Descendants of THE Vhelgaros with the flat, absolute bearing of a being who had carried weight his entire existence and had finally been handed a throne’s worth of it!

The masses stared up at their new ruler, at the burning silhouette wreathed in stolen Causes and orbiting Existences of light, at the survivor of judgment, at the Great Ruler the Narrative itself had crowned!
And THE Creature spoke.
"Kneel to your King."

sentences.text: The sky itself seemed to lean closer!

The armies moved!

The ring closed and the center emptied.
And the two rulers walked toward each other!

THE Creature nodded calmly as he walked!
"I know," THE Creature said.

"So I am making a gamble with my existence.
You have been seeking control of me...

The statue stopped walking!
Its brutal smile faded, and for the first time in this entire campaign, for the first time perhaps in Ages, its carved face became grim!
Full control.
Freely given!
The thing it had circled and bargained and told stories toward, offered up in a single flat sentence, with conditions attached and a clock of ten Nanoseconds strapped to its wrists!
THE Creature closed his eyes!
And the statue MOVED!

It was the arsenal of a true apex!
It was a charge that could unmake armies!
And across from it, THE Creature opened his eyes.
They were pure white.
There were no pupils.

There was nothing in them at all that had ever been THE Creature, only a flat, bottomless, ancient white, like twin windows opened onto something that had been waiting behind a door for a very long time.
The body of THE Creature raised one hand, and tapped the air, emotionlessly, once.
The Horned Sovereign popped.
There was no exchange!
There was no clash of Causes, no contest of chained Existences, no battle at all!

The chains fell.
The shackled First Causes rolled loose across the black stone like dropped marbles.
The miniaturized Observable Existences drifted, suddenly ownerless.
Silense!
An immense, total, crushing silence swallowed the entire Dimension!
Hundreds of Primevals stood frozen in the great ring!
Descendant Ilvexa stared at the white ash drifting where her husband had existed, her clawed hand still half-raised from her final warning!
Even the torrents of Moirai hung motionless in the air, as though the Ruling itself needed a moment!

It looked around, instead, at the edges.

This entire Dimension, this entire succession, this entire Narrative, was one carriage among many upon THE Dimensional Provenance Train of Existence, rushing forward through the lethal dark toward the architects’ grand design!

chapters.title: Chapter 5685: The True Vessel!
paragraphs: Kneeling, when hundreds of apex existences do it at once, has a glorious sound.

It rolled across the black plain of THE Vhelgaros like a slow tide of thunder as Primeval Ones of Ages lowered themselves to the cracked stone, titans of bone and Ego and petrified starlight folding downward rank after rank, and between them the omen-blooded Descendants of the old order sank to their knees with their horned heads bowed, lineage-weavings dimmed in submission before a power their architects’ blood could not argue with!
Thousands of powerful existences! Two armies! One Dimension!
All of it knelt!
Descendant Ilvexa was among the last. The widowed monarch stared at the figure burning above the white ash of her husband for a long moment, her clawed hands slowly closing.
Then she, too, lowered her horned frame to the stone.
THE Creature hovered above his kneeling Dimension, wreathed in stolen First Causes and orbiting Existences of light, and he let the moment stand exactly as long as it needed to stand.
Then he closed his eyes!
He opened them somewhere else that was endlessly white and black.
He stood upon a battlefield that stretched beyond every horizon, and the battlefield was ancient.
The ground was bone-white and hard as fired porcelain, split by rivers of pure black that ran without moving, and across the entire endless expanse, corpses lay where they had fallen!

Thousands of them. Hundreds of thousands! Titanic frames and small ones, armored and bare, ancient beyond reckoning, every single one preserved mid-fall in white and black, no rot and no scavengers and no wind, a war that existence had chosen to keep exactly as it ended!
THE Creature’s mental manifestation stood at the center of it all, his flames burning low and steady, and before him, at the heart of the dead field, stood the statue.
He looked at it clearly, here, for the first time!

It was colossal. A towering figure of grey-white stone veined through with rivers of black, carved in the shape of a broad-shouldered bearer, its heavy brow jutting over deep-cut eyes that held no pupils, only smooth dark hollows that somehow watched.

Old wounds were chiseled across every surface of it, not decorations but records, gouges and fracture-lines and one long cleaving scar that ran from its shoulder to its hip, each wound edged in black as though the stone had bled ink and the ink had dried!
Its massive hands hung empty at its sides. They were the hands of a thing built to carry, thick-fingered and cracked across every knuckle!
And upon its back!

Upon its back was carved a mountain of...figures! Hundreds of small carved figures clung to the statue’s back and shoulders in a vast stacked heap, bodies upon bodies, some clinging, some slumped, some reaching upward, an entire carried multitude rendered in miniature, fused into the bearer’s frame as though it had walked out of some ancient catastrophe with everyone it could hold and the sculptor had refused to let it put them down!
A bearer. A carrier of masses. A thing that stood, wearing everything it had ever refused to drop!
The statue’s hollow eyes rested on THE Creature’s manifestation, and its cracked mouth held the faint line of its old brutal smile, and it waited!
THE Creature did not make it wait long.
"You will listen to me." THE Creature said.
His obsidian and white-gold flames rose!

Oh!

THE Creature stood among the dead.
"No."
BOOM!

His flames roared upward, obsidian and white-gold, and for a moment the mental manifestation burned bright enough to cast the statue’s shadow long across the field of the dead!

The statue...actually seemed subservient at this time.

THE Creature opened his eyes.

The burning sky of THE Vhelgaros hung above him, healing along its torn seams, and below him a Dimension of Primevals and Descendants still knelt upon the black plain, hundreds of horned and ancient heads bowed toward their new King, waiting for his first command.
He looked past them all.

At the far edge of the Cabin, beyond the crystallized borders where the crossing-dark streaked past, a grand doorway stood in the distance, massive and sealed and humming, the threshold that led forward along the Train, toward the next Cabin, and the next, and the next, toward whatever waited at the head of a chained procession of Dimensions rushing through the dark!
THE Creature’s white-gold flames erupted to their full height, and his voice boomed out across the entirety of his first Dimension.
"Existence is vast and full of terrors. Let us go...so that I can spread my terrors."
HUUM!
He gave the command, and thousands began to move!

chapters.title: Chapter 5686: Let Me Dream!
paragraphs: <THE True Human Emperor>
Aurelius Vasiliou looked at his son-in-law with a hardened gaze.

The scorching steam of THE Vasiliou Primordial Spring rolled between them, and for a long moment the Patriarch simply stared at the smiling tyrant soaking in his lineage’s most sacred waters, the tyrant who had just asked to take one of their ancestors home the way a guest asks to take home leftovers!
Then Aurelius waved his hand.

From the golden depths below, one of the pristine skeletons stirred! It was a particularly dim one, its bones holding only the faintest ghost of the radiance its brothers still carried, an ancestor whose fade had been long and whose generation had been nearly all given away, and it floated up through the bubbling lava-waters slowly and grandly until it hovered between the two men, dripping liquid gold.
"Existence is give and take,"Aurelius said.
"So far, you have taken my daughter, my patience, and now this."
The dim golden skeleton drifted toward Noah!
"This does not need to be said... but you do know I could crush your current self with a smack, right?"
The Patriarch’s burning eyes did not waver.
"Others will not easily put up with how you talk to them. In existence, many can be arrogant. Many can act tyrannical. But the showy and boisterous ones are those who die the quickest. Be careful."
It was a warning, and it was advice, and underneath both of those things it was a father-in-law trying to understand what exactly his daughter had dragged home!
Noah nodded and accepted the skeleton, and it disappeared into his existence with a flicker of light.

"I appreciate the advice, and the ancestor," Noah replied pleasantly. "But I should explain something, since we are family now. I simply act true to myself. I do not look at someone so much more powerful than me and become docile because of it. Somewhere along the way, I began to look at... Potential."
He leaned back against the rocky edge, golden lava sheeting off his stellar body.

"I ask myself, if given time, could I get to where this being has attained, or exceed him? Where would our potentials lie? And every time, no matter who I stand before, I believe my potential... always comes out on top."

"I do not think myself higher than anyone in standing. At one point, even a peasant was grander than me. At one point, an Ant was alive and had taken more steps in this existence than me. Standing is temporary. Standing is a snapshot. But potential... potential is the whole picture, and in the whole picture, I am... I am... I am...."
HUUM!
His own words turned strange in his mouth as he spoke them!

His voice trailed, and his endlessly blue eyes unfocused, and his mind slid sideways into a state of epiphany and reverie that he had not planned and could not name, the three repeated words humming through his two hundred Decillion quarks like a struck bell that refused to finish ringing!

I am. The first Letter. The oldest declaration. It turned over inside him, heavy with something unarrived, and he sighed deeply and sank back into the scorching waters without finishing the sentence, letting the feeling settle into the depths of him where grand things germinated!
Aurelius Vasiliou watched all of this, and slowly shook his head.

"My daughter’s Provenance chose a weird lifeform,"the Patriarch declared to no one in particular. "Okay. You seem to be enjoying yourself, so take some time here. I also need to go talk to my daughter and get things ready."
With these words, the muscular figure of Aurelius rose!

Drops of scorching golden lava-like waters fell off his towering, scarred body in glowing streams, and his ornate robes swept out of the steam and wrapped around him on their own as a golden gateway bloomed open at the spring’s edge!
The Patriarch stepped toward it, paused, and glanced back at Noah one last time, at the stellar blue-gold anomaly soaking in his ancestors’ spring and humming to himself about ants and potential.
He shook his head again.
Then he disappeared!
Noah leaned back, alone with the steam and the bones.
His eyes became endlessly blue, brighter and brighter, twin depths kindling in the golden mist, and he raised his hand up toward the rocky ceiling as if he wanted to grasp something he could not see.
There was so much out there!

Immense Ones who collected Provenance Lifeforms as interest. A Sealed One wearing its way through vessels toward something called IT. Atlas Elseworlds filled with leashed sovereigns and locked rooms. A Train of chained Dimensions rushing through the dark toward a design nobody would explain.
His power was growing, faster than any framework said it should, tier by tier and essence by essence, but he had understood something long ago.
He was not mainly limited by power.
He was limited by information. Knowledge!
Power told you how hard you could swing. Knowledge told you where to stand, when to swing, and whether swinging was even the correct art!
Every disaster that had ever nearly claimed him had walked in through a gap in what he knew, and every triumph had walked in through a gap in what his enemies knew about HIM!
He waved his hand, and the crystal left behind by Vakochev appeared above his palm.
The obsidian shard rotated slowly in the steam, dense and dark and silent, the parting gift of a being who had laid his Scales across all existence and then folded them up and retreated.
Noah looked at it the way he had looked at it a hundred times now, and his Regard answered the way it had answered a hundred times.
Question marks. Columns of them.
"Everyone in existence is so damn fond of their secrets..." Noah remarked to the bones below.

He had many things to utilize! Many tools under his belt! His Mantle was grand. THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign was grand. The collar, the crystal, the Marks, the Teloi, the Tesseracts, an arsenal that dynasties of old would have built entire dynasties around!
But out of all of it, THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer was the grandest!
Because every other tool did what it did. Only one tool did whatever he needed it to do next. And if what he needed was information and direction...
"I can always dream."
HUUM!
Noah smiled, and put the crystal away, and began to close his eyes in the spring!

The scorching golden waters bubbled around his body. The faded ancestors slept below. Somewhere above this pocket of density, his wife was arguing with her mother, his father-in-law was preparing a Lineage for war, and across the continuum his other body walked a higher Cabin
He settled his breathing, and reached inward, toward the doorway of his Provenance, toward the landscape where all his moments lived!
But it had to be something special!

No small dreams tonight. No cheap errands into yesterday. If knowledge was his true frontier, then he would aim his Dream at the largest gap in it, at the beings who sat above every framework, behind every curse, at the end of every warning anyone had ever given him!
"I want to dream of Immense Ones,"Noah declared into the steam, and the spring itself seemed to still at the words!
"I want to know more about these things that remain an unfathomable threat that can squash me so damn easily. Let me dream... of Immense Ones."
HUUM!

chapters.title: Chapter 5687: The Grave Beneath The Eye! I
paragraphs: His Provenance answered!
Prompts bloomed across his vision in cascading waves, and even their text seemed to arrive more carefully than usual, like a Ruination lowering her voice inside a dangerous archive!
|You seek to Dream of THE Immense Ones.|

|Warning: the subjects of this inquiry stand unfathomably above your current Trueness and Provenance. Direct perception of an Immense One through Dreaming is ill advised. Attempting to force direct perception would exhaust your entire Provenance and may draw the attention of the perceived.|
|Your Provenance negotiates.|

|The cemented past is open to you. The Records hold countless moments connected to THE Immense Ones. A connected Dream may be granted: a thread from the past bearing upon the subjects of your inquiry.|
|Cost: 20 Provenance Essence.|
Twenty!
Noah’s eyes remained closed, but his mind whistled at the number!
Twenty Essence, nearly a third of his capacity, drained for a single Dream he could not even steer.
He thought of many things. And then...
"Done," Noah said. "Take it."
|20 Provenance Essence has been drained.|
|A moment connected to THE Immense Ones has been selected from the cemented past.|
|A random Dream emerges: its time, its place, and its witnesses are chosen by weight alone.|
HUUM!
Within the scorching golden waters of THE Vasiliou Primordial Spring, the body of Noah began to shine!

It was not the shine of the spring’s essence, and it was not the shine of his body! Light poured out of him from beneath his skin, stellar and blue-gold and impossibly dense, his entire figure condensing into radiance until he blazed within the steam like an unfathomable singularity given the shape of a man, and the faded golden skeletons in the depths below seemed to turn their ancient hollow faces up toward the brilliance!
His Provenance blared, brilliant!

Singularities spun! Two hundred Decillion quarks aligned! The surface of the golden waters flattened outward in a perfect ring around his shining frame, and the doorway of THE Human Dreamer swung wide upon its hinges of identity, opening onto the one landscape where even Immense Ones had left footprints they could never take back!
And Noah began to dream!
A dream bloomed.

One moment there was the scorching gold of the spring, and the next moment there was ground beneath his feet and a sky above his head, and Noah stood manifested inside a Dimension that existence had folded shut like a pressed flower!
He looked out, and the place was grand.

Terraced fields rolled away from him in every direction, vast stepped plains of soft luminous soil stacked into the distance like the gardens of a sleeping titan, and the distances themselves were wrong in a beautiful, unhurried way, folding gently so that a far-off ridge might sit behind a near one and above it at the same time without apology!
The air was thick and breathed slow ambient exhalations rolling across the fields in visible ripples of shimmer!
And the sky!

The sky was layered, stratum upon stratum of radiance stacked toward an unseeable ceiling, bands of pale gold and deep amber and drowsy rose all glowing at once, like seven different evenings had been shelved on top of each other and left burning!

No sun hung anywhere. The light came from the layers themselves, and it fell across the terraced land heavy and warm and eternal, the light of a place where time had been asked to sit down and had agreed!
A Dimension locked in the past. Even before any prompt confirmed it, his instincts read it in everything. Nothing here was waiting for tomorrow. Tomorrow had been amputated!
Noah looked down at himself.

His body was his own, stellar and familiar, but it had been dressed! White robes wrapped him in long clean folds, draped over one shoulder and belted at the waist, the fabric faintly luminous and utterly weightless. And upon his face sat a mask!
He raised his fingers and traced it. Smooth gold, warm as skin, covering him brow to chin. Two simple dots for eyes.
And below them, carved into the gold, an eerie, permanent smile!
And...
There were others!

He lifted his gaze, and across the vast terraced fields he saw them, dozens upon dozens of figures scattered through the folded distances, each one seated alone upon the luminous soil, each one draped in the same white robes, each one wearing the same golden mask with its two dots and its eerie smile.
And every single one of them pulsed with an aura his existence now knew intimately!
Provenance Lifeforms!
Dozens of self-generating existences, seated in ordered solitude across a farm-realm outside of time, and before each seated figure... burned a lake!
The lakes were the most interesting things in the whole folded Dimension.
Each one was a slow whirlpool of stellar obsidian-gold, vibrant and deep, and they did not burn with light so much as with WEIGHT, because swirling within every lake were Causes!

Heavy, oppressive, authentic Causes, the critical structure of existence itself, dozens of them per lake, turning in the obsidian-gold like drowned suns, and their combined pressure rolled off the water and pressed against his body even from afar.
And the masked sovereigns were harvesting them!

Noah watched, fascinated, as the seated figures worked with slow eternal patience, their hands weaving above their lakes, drawing the burning Causes together strand by strand, pulling them into clusters, and the clusters into tighter clusters, condensing the harvested structure of existence toward singularities that formed so gradually that the work must have been measured in eras.
A farm. A farm where the crop was Causes, and the farmers were sovereigns of self-generation wearing smiling golden masks!
Noah thought, his mind racing behind the eerie smile.
’Here sit dozens of sovereigns condensing causes by the lakeful. For whom? Sovereigns do not farm for themselves in uniform. Uniforms mean an employer, and employers at this scale mean...’
His existence BUZZED!
HUUM!

It came from nowhere and everywhere, a deep resonant vibration through all two hundred Decillion of his quarks, his Dream Body thrumming like a struck instrument, and prompts bloomed urgently across his vision!
|Your Provenance Dream Body is reacting.|

|An item held by your true body has pierced the boundary of the Dream. The crystal left behind by Vakochev pulses across existence and time. The weavings of the current Dream are made clear by its light.|
|It has found something.|
And in his fingers, the crystal appeared!

It was illusory, a manifestation of dark light rather than the shard itself, but it pulsed in his grip incessantly, urgently, joyfully, the long-silent treasure of a retreated titan vibrating like a compass needle that had finally, after all this time, found its north!
Information bloomed from it in waves, flowing directly into his existence, and his Provenance Essence caught every thread and pulled it taut and made everything clearer!
|The Records speak, unlocked by the resonance of the crystal.|

|When defeated by THE Immense Ones, Vakochev paid a heavy cost to retreat. The retreat was not clean. Critical parts of his existence were sundered from him and locked away across existence and time, sealed into pockets of existence where only the forces of THE Immense Ones tread.|
|You are near one of his Sundered Weavings of Existence.|
|Your Dream has deposited you within a Dimension locked in the past, isolated from all others.|
|Should you be successful in unsealing the chains binding him, the favor will not go unpaid.|
Noah stood very still upon the luminous soil, and behind the golden mask, his endlessly blue eyes blazed!
And the shape of the larger truth assembled itself in his mind with terrible elegance!

Vakochev had not simply retreated. The being who laid his Scales across all of existence had been defeated, and his retreat had been paid for in pieces of himself, carved off and buried in pockets like this one, and the "random" Dream had brought him here!
’The favor will not go unpaid.’
A favor. From VAKOCHEV. The word rolled through him, and the strategic greed at the center of his existence woke up all at once and began, quietly, to salivate!
But first, the venue. He looked around slowly, a masked farmer among masked farmers, and he followed the work to its destination!
In one direction, down across the folding terraces, he saw it.

A procession! A few of the white-robed Provenance Lifeforms had risen from their lakes, and they moved in a slow, solemn line across the fields, carrying their finished harvests, long condensed strings of heavy Causes coiled in their arms like luminous chains of obsidian gold, each string dense enough to make the air around it kneel.
And they carried them toward a mound.

It rose from the center of a vast cleared basin where no lakes burned, a great swollen hill of dark, packed, luminous earth, long as a fallen titan and shaped with the unmistakable, deliberate finality of one thing and one thing only!
A grave!

The masked sovereigns reached its edge one by one, and one by one they cast their harvests! The strings of condensed Causes unfurled through the air like thrown chains and fell across the grave-mound, settling over its dark bulk, sinking slightly into the luminous earth, layer upon layer upon layer!

Noah’s perception, sharpened by his Provenance, could see the accumulated depth of it, thousands of Cause-chains, tens of thousands, eras of harvests layered across that mound like a mummy’s wrappings woven from the critical structure of existence itself!
And the grave... responded!

Each time a fresh chain of Causes settled over it, the mound shone briefly from within, a deep buried pulse of light, and it hummed, a long, low, resonant note that rolled across the entire basin, the sound of something enormous turning over in its sleep beneath the weight of one more blanket!

The Provenance Lifeforms did not react to the shining or the humming at all. They simply turned, solemn and smiling their carved golden smiles, and walked back toward their lakes to begin the next harvest, as they had clearly done ten thousand times before, as normal as farmers walking back from a well!
Noah breathed behind the mask, and the elegance of it was as horrifying as it was instructive!

Existence protects whatever Causes stand behind. It registers them as critical structure and resists their alteration. So bind a prisoner in enough of them... and existence itself becomes the jailer. Existence itself will resist the unsealing. They did not build a cage as they convinced reality that the cage is part of its own skeleton!
And then, because every horror in his life had taught him to always, always check the sky, Noah raised his head!
The radiant layered heavens stretched above the terraced fields, band upon band of shelved evening light.
And set into them, vast beyond vastness, gazing down at everything!
Was a massive obsidian eye!

It filled a full stratum of the sky by itself, lidless and deep and dark as a hole cut in the heavens, its titanic iris faintly threaded with slow-turning gold, and its gaze lay across the entire Dimension at once, across every lake and every masked farmer and every thrown chain, and most of all, most heavily of all, upon the grave!
An Immense One!
The moment his perception acknowledged it, the Dimension’s own narrative unfurled for him, waves of prompt-information blooming in the style he now knew intimately.
|You now perceive the standing Narrative of this Dimension.|
|THE Narrative of Existence: The Unending Burial.|
|All those within this Dimension are tasked eternally: harvest the binding Provenance Causes cultivated across this Dimension, condense them, and layer them upon the unknown grave.|

|Those who are fastidious in this task shall receive ever greater flows of Existential Moirai. The most fastidious shall receive recognition: their names spoken once, fondly, by the watcher above, and a single keepsake drawn from the hoards of the one below.|
|THE GLOATING JAILER presides over this Narrative.|
And then, at this time...
|THE GLOATING JAILER is in a magnificent mood today. It has been in a magnificent mood for the last several days.|
|It finds the contents of the grave exquisitely amusing. It stops by often, simply to look, the way one visits a trophy.|

|It reminds all diligent harvesters: he measured everything, once. Let him now lie beneath everything, measured. It considers this the finest joke it has ever told, and it has been telling it for a very, very long time.|
|THE GLOATING JAILER is smug. The Records note that this is its resting state.|

Noah stood in white robes among the terraced fields of an amputated Dimension, a golden smile carved over his real one, a pulsing key in his fingers, twenty Essence spent on a dream, and he absorbed all of it!
A titan who had laid his Scales across all of existence, dismembered and buried under chains of harvested Causes, existence itself recruited as his jailer!
Dozens of leashed sovereigns farming his bindings deeper on an eternal clock! An Immense One hanging in the sky above its favorite joke, smug and magnificent and watching everything!

And one uninvited Human Dreamer, standing in the middle of all of it, holding the key, wearing the uniform, with a promised favor from the buried titan himself waiting on the other side of the chains.
Behind the eerie golden smile of the mask, slowly, terribly, Noah began to smile for real!
