chapters.title: Chapter 5688: The Grave Beneath The Eye! II
paragraphs: A wind rose in the deep gold of the citadel, far off where the stacked tiers burned against the shelved evenings of the sky.
It was not a true wind, for no true winds blew in a Dimension where tomorrow had been cut away, but an exhalation of the land itself, and it rolled outward across the folded distances!
It slid down the ascending architecture and out over the pale meditation halls, where white-robed Provenance Lifeforms sat unmoving as carvings with their auras turned inward.
It crossed the unhurried roads and the solemn processions upon them, stirring the hems of burial-walkers who did not look up!

It swept across the terraced Cause-farms, over a hundred stellar lakes and a thousand drowned suns turning in their depths, and it broke at last, like a tide against a final stone, upon a lone figure in white robes standing above an unclaimed lake, the eerie golden smile of his mask turned slowly across everything!
Noah catalogued everything the wind had touched!

Most of the masked Provenance Lifeforms were exactly as he had first read them, seated before their stellar obsidian-gold lakes in eternal patience, weaving the heavy Causes into condensed strings, rising in solemn processions to cast their chains across the humming grave, the Narrative of THE Unending Burial grinding forward beneath the smug obsidian eye in the layered sky.
But not all of them!

In the distance, past the rolling luminous hills, structures could be seen! Pale halls and terraced pavilions rose from the folds of the land, and among them, other white-robed figures sat in deep meditation, unmoving as carvings, their sovereign auras turned entirely inward.

And further still, small processions of masked figures were moving away from the farms altogether, walking unhurried roads toward the deepest regions of the Dimension, where distant gold structures rose stacked and grand against the shelved evenings of the sky, tier upon tier of ascending architecture!
Likely a central citadel!
He gave a light nod to all of it, and then turned his attention to the resource bubbling right in front of him!
The lake!

His assigned station, apparently, since the Dream had deposited him before an unclaimed one. The stellar obsidian-gold whirlpool turned slowly at his feet, and within its depths, the heavy Causes swirled like drowned suns, oppressive and vibrant and utterly unexplained!
Noah crouched at the lake’s edge, and put his hand into the water.
HUUM!
His existence BUZZED instantly!

The reaction did not come from his skin or his senses. It came from his foundations! All Nine of his Teloi, seated through every one of his two hundred Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks, woke at once, and they surged toward his submerged hand like hounds catching a familiar scent, because the things swirling in this lake were their kin, aims and structures and declarations, and his Teloi pressed up against the foreign Causes and began, seamlessly and hungrily, to take them apart.
Prompts bloomed in cascading analytical waves!
|Your Nine Teloi react to the contents of the lake. Analysis begins.|
|Analysis is seamless. A Telos is an aim and purpose that answers to its declarer. A Cause is a command seated in structure. Your integration is deep enough to read one through the other.|
|Three Provenance Causes are identified within this lake.|
|THE Provenance Cause of the Stilled Wing: a binding Cause. What it settles upon loses the right of departure.|
|THE Provenance Cause of the Lowered Crown: a suppression Cause. What it settles upon has its authority pressed beneath its own standing.|
|THE Provenance Cause of the Quiet Name: a sealing Cause. What it settles upon cannot be found by those who seek it.|
Binding! Suppression! Concealment!
Every lake in this Dimension was growing links for the chains on that grave, and now his Teloi tore into the far more interesting question of WHERE such things came from.
|Origin analysis: these Causes were generated from this Dimension itself.|

|A tool of extremely high Dimensionality belonging to an Immense One is located within this Dimension.Its ambient weight saturates all budding Causes cultivated here. Due to this saturation, the budding Causes attain the significance of Provenance upon maturing.|

|Provenance Causes carry the Dimensionality of their making. They ignore the defenses of those with weak Dimensionality: lifeforms with 60 Attributes or less have a hard time ever denying the effects of such Causes.|
|Mitigation exists: if the targeted lifeform has any Causes standing behind them, the terrifying Dimensionality of these Provenance Causes can be mitigated.|
Noah’s eyes were shining brilliantly behind the mask!
Because they were inherently unique, these Provenance Causes, grown in saturated soil, carrying borrowed depth, capable of ignoring the defenses of nearly everything beneath the sixtieth attribute.
But at the end of the day, when his Teloi held them up to the light and turned them over... they were still just another form of authority and power!
And the mitigation clause sang to him loudest of all. Causes defended against Provenance Causes.

’And my Teloi contribute to my Dimensionality directly,’ Noah thought, ’They are integrated into every quark of my matter, passively applied to my existence at all times. If I simply define and utilize more of what is already mine...’
His Dimensionality would climb without a single external treasure!
It was a grand thread, and he wanted to pull it for a century if he could.
But he cut the experiment short, drew his hand from the lake, and rose. Research was for the safe hours, and he was not in a safe place, and the actual problem still hung unsolved before him.
How did one move against that grave, unseal a piece of Vakochev, and walk out of a pocket of locked time, all under the direct, era-long, trophy-admiring gaze of an Immense One?
He turned toward the grave, weighing angles and blasphemies!
And that was when he saw it.
At one particular lake, off along the curve of the basin, something was laying near the water’s edge, and Noah almost had to rub his eyes as if he was seeing things.
Because he saw...
An obsidian slime!

It was laying down gently beside the lake, if a slime could be said to lay down, a small rounded mass of stellar obsidian resting against the luminous soil, and it was so extremely, absurdly out of place among the robed and masked sovereigns of this Dimension.
He looked closer, and the closer he looked, the less sense it made!

The slime was small, barely the size of a curled hound, its simple body a deep translucent obsidian threaded through with faint drifting motes of stellar light, and set within its front were two eyes of dim crimson, half-lidded, unhurried, fixed upon the distant grave with an expression that should have been impossible for a creature made of ooze!
Melancholy!

It looked ancient in its bearing, in the sheer stillness of it, the stillness of something that had watched eras walk past and had stopped waving at them! Its aura could not be felt at all, not veiled, not suppressed, simply absent, a hole in his perception shaped like a small sad slime!
And yet!
When Noah’s deeper senses brushed across its simple little body, his existence prickled from crown to heel, because that small mass of obsidian felt DEEP.
His instincts reported, calmly and insistently, that the tiny creature laying by the lake contained countless miniature dimensions within it, folded and stacked and sleeping.
Noah couldn’t help but frown as his existence buzzed

Slimes! Even his own Records held the old terror of that word. Entire Dimensions across existence exterminated slimes on sight, because of the legends of the one that ATE Dimensions, the feared thing whose survival in any Dimension for a few days marked that Dimension for death.
And here one lay, obsidian and sorrowful, inside a locked pocket of the past, at the edge of a Cause-farm, staring at the grave of a titan.
His intuition pointed.
Noah followed it, and began to walk!

He crossed the luminous terraces at an easy pace, one masked farmer strolling among many, past sovereigns who did not look up from their eternal weaving, until he came to stand beside the small obsidian slime at the water’s edge!
It did not react to his approach at all. Its dim crimson eyes remained on the grave, half-lidded and far away.
Noah looked down at it, and said, simply!
"Hello."
Nothing!
The slime did not even turn towards his direction! It lay there, ancient and melancholic and dripping with more folded depth than some Dimensions he had personally visited, and it ignored him.
Noah scowled behind his golden smile, and waved his hand in front of its crimson eyes!
"Hello? Obsidian slime?"
The half-lidded crimson eyes went wide!

The slime’s entire small body rippled once, sharply, and it turned, and it looked at him, and it blinked, an expression of pure, unguarded surprise blooming across a face that was mostly ooze, and when it spoke, its voice arrived directly against his existence, soft and old and rasped at the edges.
"You...can perceive me?"
The slime rose slightly off the soil, its crimson gaze sharpening!
"Even that Immense One should not be capable of perceiving me right now. How can you...."
It stopped.

Its dim crimson eyes moved across him slowly, up and down, down and up, taking in the white robes, the golden mask, the stellar frame beneath them, and something in its ancient gaze focused, and narrowed, and understood!
HUUM!
Noah’s own existence buzzed at that single syllable, and he became entirely serious, his full attention locking onto the small creature, his Regard sweeping across it.
And the panel that bloomed before his eyes was unique.
|Masamuk|
Rows upon rows of sealed questions, the signature of depth beyond his measure, and above them all, alone and unredacted, as if the name itself refused to hide.
Masamuk!
Noah blinked.
Masamuk. Masamuk. His mind worked extremely fast, tearing through his own Records at the speed of thought, because he had HEARD that name before!
Not in this Dimension! Not in this era! It had been spoken to him once, in the long drawl of the lazy Mnemonic Leviathan.
The memory played in his head.
When Existence was young, and the boundaries between what was and what was not remained fluid and uncertain, there was Masamuk.
Masamuk had split the body of Chaos, not with authority, since authority had not yet been differentiated from raw potential, but through the sheer force of will.
From the halves of Chaos, Masamuk fashioned the territories that would become the first Domains.
Masamuk looked upon the divided Chaos and shaped it, molded it, convinced it to remember the forms that were envisioned.
This was the first great Cause of differentiation through Chaos under the records of Masamuk, as only at this time did he become a true follower of Vakochev!
A follower of Vakochev!
One of the first beings to enact great Causes of Differentiation, a shaper from the era when what was and what was not had still been negotiable, a splitter of Chaos by pure will!
Laying beside a lake, in the shape of a small sad slime, staring at his buried master’s grave.

It slid down the ascending architecture and out over the pale meditation halls, where white-robed Provenance Lifeforms sat unmoving as carvings with their auras turned inward.
It crossed the unhurried roads and the solemn processions upon them, stirring the hems of burial-walkers who did not look up!

It swept across the terraced Cause-farms, over a hundred stellar lakes and a thousand drowned suns turning in their depths, and it broke at last, like a tide against a final stone, upon a lone figure in white robes standing above an unclaimed lake, the eerie golden smile of his mask turned slowly across everything!
Noah catalogued everything the wind had touched!

Most of the masked Provenance Lifeforms were exactly as he had first read them, seated before their stellar obsidian-gold lakes in eternal patience, weaving the heavy Causes into condensed strings, rising in solemn processions to cast their chains across the humming grave, the Narrative of THE Unending Burial grinding forward beneath the smug obsidian eye in the layered sky.
But not all of them!
In the distance, past the rolling luminous hills, structures could be seen!

Pale halls and terraced pavilions rose from the folds of the land, and among them, other white-robed figures sat in deep meditation, unmoving as carvings, their sovereign auras turned entirely inward.

And further still, small processions of masked figures were moving away from the farms altogether, walking unhurried roads toward the deepest regions of the Dimension, where distant gold structures rose stacked and grand against the shelved evenings of the sky, tier upon tier of ascending architecture!
Likely a central citadel!
He gave a light nod to all of it, and then turned his attention to the resource bubbling right in front of him!
The lake!
His assigned station, apparently, since the Dream had deposited him before an unclaimed one.
The stellar obsidian-gold whirlpool turned slowly at his feet, and within its depths, the heavy Causes swirled like drowned suns, oppressive and vibrant and utterly unexplained!
Noah crouched at the lake’s edge, and put his hand into the water.
HUUM!
His existence BUZZED instantly!
The reaction did not come from his skin or his senses.
It came from his foundations!

All Nine of his Teloi, seated through every one of his two hundred Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks, woke at once, and they surged toward his submerged hand like hounds catching a familiar scent, because the things swirling in this lake were their kin, aims and structures and declarations, and his Teloi pressed up against the foreign Causes and began, seamlessly and hungrily, to take them apart.
Prompts bloomed in cascading analytical waves!
|Your Nine Teloi react to the contents of the lake.
Analysis begins.|
|Analysis is seamless.
A Telos is an aim and purpose that answers to its declarer.
A Cause is a command seated in structure.
Your integration is deep enough to read one through the other.|
|Three Provenance Causes are identified within this lake.|
|THE Provenance Cause of the Stilled Wing: a binding Cause.
What it settles upon loses the right of departure.|
|THE Provenance Cause of the Lowered Crown: a suppression Cause.
What it settles upon has its authority pressed beneath its own standing.|
|THE Provenance Cause of the Quiet Name: a sealing Cause.
What it settles upon cannot be found by those who seek it.|
Binding!
Suppression!
Concealment!
Every lake in this Dimension was growing links for the chains on that grave, and now his Teloi tore into the far more interesting question of WHERE such things came from.
|Origin analysis: these Causes were generated from this Dimension itself.|
|A tool of extremely high Dimensionality belonging to an Immense One is located within this Dimension.Its ambient weight saturates all budding Causes cultivated here.
Due to this saturation, the budding Causes attain the significance of Provenance upon maturing.|
|Provenance Causes carry the Dimensionality of their making.
They ignore the defenses of those with weak Dimensionality: lifeforms with 60 Attributes or less have a hard time ever denying the effects of such Causes.|
|Mitigation exists: if the targeted lifeform has any Causes standing behind them, the terrifying Dimensionality of these Provenance Causes can be mitigated.|
Noah’s eyes were shining brilliantly behind the mask!
Because they were inherently unique, these Provenance Causes, grown in saturated soil, carrying borrowed depth, capable of ignoring the defenses of nearly everything beneath the sixtieth attribute.
But at the end of the day, when his Teloi held them up to the light and turned them over... they were still just another form of authority and power!
And the mitigation clause sang to him loudest of all.
Causes defended against Provenance Causes.
’And my Teloi contribute to my Dimensionality directly,’ Noah thought, ’They are integrated into every quark of my matter, passively applied to my existence at all times.
If I simply define and utilize more of what is already mine...’
His Dimensionality would climb without a single external treasure!
It was a grand thread, and he wanted to pull it for a century if he could.
But he cut the experiment short, drew his hand from the lake, and rose.
Research was for the safe hours, and he was not in a safe place, and the actual problem still hung unsolved before him.
How did one move against that grave, unseal a piece of Vakochev, and walk out of a pocket of locked time, all under the direct, era-long, trophy-admiring gaze of an Immense One?
He turned toward the grave, weighing angles and blasphemies!
And that was when he saw it.
At one particular lake, off along the curve of the basin, something was laying near the water’s edge, and Noah almost had to rub his eyes as if he was seeing things.
Because he saw...
An obsidian slime!

It was laying down gently beside the lake, if a slime could be said to lay down, a small rounded mass of stellar obsidian resting against the luminous soil, and it was so extremely, absurdly out of place among the robed and masked sovereigns of this Dimension.
He looked closer, and the closer he looked, the less sense it made!

The slime was small, barely the size of a curled hound, its simple body a deep translucent obsidian threaded through with faint drifting motes of stellar light, and set within its front were two eyes of dim crimson, half-lidded, unhurried, fixed upon the distant grave with an expression that should have been impossible for a creature made of ooze!
Melancholy!
It looked ancient in its bearing, in the sheer stillness of it, the stillness of something that had watched eras walk past and had stopped waving at them!
Its aura could not be felt at all, not veiled, not suppressed, simply absent, a hole in his perception shaped like a small sad slime!
And yet!
When Noah’s deeper senses brushed across its simple little body, his existence prickled from crown to heel, because that small mass of obsidian felt DEEP.
His instincts reported, calmly and insistently, that the tiny creature laying by the lake contained countless miniature dimensions within it, folded and stacked and sleeping.
Noah couldn’t help but frown as his existence buzzed
Slimes!
Even his own Records held the old terror of that word.

Entire Dimensions across existence exterminated slimes on sight, because of the legends of the one that ATE Dimensions, the feared thing whose survival in any Dimension for a few days marked that Dimension for death.
And here one lay, obsidian and sorrowful, inside a locked pocket of the past, at the edge of a Cause-farm, staring at the grave of a titan.
His intuition pointed.
Noah followed it, and began to walk!

He crossed the luminous terraces at an easy pace, one masked farmer strolling among many, past sovereigns who did not look up from their eternal weaving, until he came to stand beside the small obsidian slime at the water’s edge!
It did not react to his approach at all.
Its dim crimson eyes remained on the grave, half-lidded and far away.
Noah looked down at it, and said, simply!
"Hello."
Nothing!
The slime did not even turn towards his direction!
It lay there, ancient and melancholic and dripping with more folded depth than some Dimensions he had personally visited, and it ignored him.
Noah scowled behind his golden smile, and waved his hand in front of its crimson eyes!
"Hello?
Obsidian slime?"
The half-lidded crimson eyes went wide!

The slime’s entire small body rippled once, sharply, and it turned, and it looked at him, and it blinked, an expression of pure, unguarded surprise blooming across a face that was mostly ooze, and when it spoke, its voice arrived directly against his existence, soft and old and rasped at the edges.
"You...can perceive me?"
The slime rose slightly off the soil, its crimson gaze sharpening!
"Even that Immense One should not be capable of perceiving me right now.
How can you...."
It stopped.

Its dim crimson eyes moved across him slowly, up and down, down and up, taking in the white robes, the golden mask, the stellar frame beneath them, and something in its ancient gaze focused, and narrowed, and understood!
HUUM!
Noah’s own existence buzzed at that single syllable, and he became entirely serious, his full attention locking onto the small creature, his Regard sweeping across it.
And the panel that bloomed before his eyes was unique.
|Masamuk|
Rows upon rows of sealed questions, the signature of depth beyond his measure, and above them all, alone and unredacted, as if the name itself refused to hide.
Masamuk!
Noah blinked.
Masamuk.
Masamuk.
His mind worked extremely fast, tearing through his own Records at the speed of thought, because he had HEARD that name before!
Not in this Dimension!
Not in this era!
It had been spoken to him once, in the long drawl of the lazy Mnemonic Leviathan.
The memory played in his head.
When Existence was young, and the boundaries between what was and what was not remained fluid and uncertain, there was Masamuk.
Masamuk had split the body of Chaos, not with authority, since authority had not yet been differentiated from raw potential, but through the sheer force of will.
From the halves of Chaos, Masamuk fashioned the territories that would become the first Domains.
Masamuk looked upon the divided Chaos and shaped it, molded it, convinced it to remember the forms that were envisioned.
This was the first great Cause of differentiation through Chaos under the records of Masamuk, as only at this time did he become a true follower of Vakochev!
A follower of Vakochev!
One of the first beings to enact great Causes of Differentiation, a shaper from the era when what was and what was not had still been negotiable, a splitter of Chaos by pure will!
Laying beside a lake, in the shape of a small sad slime, staring at his buried master’s grave.

chapters.title: Chapter 5689: The Slime At The Lake
paragraphs: There were beings you postured before, and there were beings you did not.
Noah became entirely serious as he looked at the small lifeform in front of him.
One of the oldest followers of Vakochev!
A shaper from the era when what was and what was not had still been negotiable, a splitter of Chaos by pure will, and every instinct in his two hundred Decillion quarks reported the same reading.

The melancholic little slime laying beside this lake was unfathomably more powerful than the father of Thalia, more powerful than anyone he had ever stood before, and quite possibly more powerful than even something like THE Sealed One!

It was OLD, old in the way the first light was old, and as much as Noah liked to act tyrannical and border on arrogant before ancient terrors, his arrogance had always been aimed at the self-serious and the cruel.
This being was neither.

So he gave the slime the respect that it deserved. He nodded towards it, once, with a serious expression, and he chose to say nothing at all, because there was a great deal here that he did not understand, and a wise man did not fill the silence of his elders with noise!
Instead, he sat down.

Noah lowered himself onto the luminous soil at the edge of the lake, casually, unhurried, the warm ground giving softly beneath him, one masked farmer settling at his station among a hundred masked farmers doing the same.

The whirlpool of obsidian gold turned slowly before him, drowned suns swirling in its depths, and to any distant eye he was simply working, simply sitting, simply one more white robe in a Dimension full of them!
Because the slime had said it itself. It should not be perceivable here, not even to the Immense One hanging smug in the layered sky.

And Noah was entirely perceivable, a visible farmer at a visible lake, and he had no intention of standing over an invisible fugitive and giving away the position of the only friendly piece on this entire board by talking down at empty air!
Masamuk watched him do all of this.
The dim crimson eyes moved over him slowly, up and down, taking in the disguise, the caution, the deliberate casualness of the seating, and the ancient slime’s expression remained serene throughout.
"You should be fine to communicate," Masamuk said, its soft rasped voice arriving directly against Noah’s existence.
"My weavings cover this whole region. It will not even seem like you are talking, to the eyes of others."
Noah nodded at this, and let his shoulders settle, and spoke in a low, even tone toward the turning lake.
"I have heard a few stories regarding you. I never thought I would actually come across you."
"For what happened to Vakochev... I am sorry. Are you here to unseal the part of him within that grave as well?"
He asked his questions very clearly, and a flash of surprise bloomed within the ancient slime!
Its small body rippled once, and its crimson eyes widened by a fraction, and then narrowed.

"Existence is vast, and filled with unfathomable terrors," Masamuk said slowly. "My friend and Master had cast out many weavings. I did not think one would appear here so quickly. He expected hundreds, or even potentially thousands of years to pass before any chances could arise."
The slime seemed melancholic as it said these words, its gaze drifting back toward the distant humming grave.
Something in the phrasing snagged against Noah’s mind and held! My friend and Master.
And... chances.
The crystal in his storage, the beacon that had waited patiently in his collection.
Noah couldn’t help but turn serious as he leaned forward slightly, his voice dropping lower.
"What truly happened before these new rulings of existence came to play? What happened between THE Immense Ones and Vakochev?"
The slime’s eyes flashed!
Immense sadness and immense hatred moved through those dim crimson depths together.
It looked out across the lake filled with budding Causes silently.
After a moment, the slime asked a question of its own.
"Do you believe you will die?"
A heavy question arose between them, laid down without warning, and Noah found that he did not need to take a long time to answer it.
He had answered it before, in the quiet of his own Pantheon, in the years before crowns and Verses, in every hour since a hospital room in 1997 that he had personally stood inside.
"I am only human," Noah replied."I live, and in the future, I may die. Maybe to be truly human, it is certain that I will die. But before then... I have boundlessness before me."
Masamuk turned its crimson gaze upon him and nodded
And then the serenity cracked.
"For the first time in my existence," Masamuk said, and its soft voice did not rise, "Those Who Remain, these failures of existence... made me want to die."
BOOM!
The words landed against Noah’s existence heavily!
They made him... want to die?!

This being! A splitter of Chaos! A shaper of the first Domains, older than authority itself, deep enough that an Immense One hung directly overhead and could not perceive him! What could possibly be done to such a lifeform to make it want to DIE?!
Noah continued to listen silently, his hands resting still upon his knees, and Masamuk spoke, and the Dimension around them seemed to quiet itself to make room.
"When they moved against us, our side had one banner. One enemy stood before them. Vakochev. And do you know what these failures did?"

The slime’s gaze stayed on the far grave. "They did not focus their attacks on him. From the very first hour, they focused their attacks on those who followed him. And even that, even that, was not the worst of it."
Its small body was utterly still.

"The worst was the unnecessary cruelness of it. There was no strategy that demanded what they did. No war that required it. It is as if they wish to be cruel simply because they can. They targeted all those that followed Vakochev, and they did not simply kill us, because they know what death is. Death is singular. Death is potentially final. A dead follower feels nothing, and a Master mourns once, and it ends. So they chose otherwise. They chose to make those closest to him, and him by extension, feel pain. Lasting pain. Renewable pain."
The crimson eyes closed for a long moment.
"And across existence, pain comes from connections. From relationships. From memories."
Noah’s chest tightened.
He remembered a memory of...a red-haired woman’s voice crying out from a white pool saying...You promised to always remember!
He pushed it down and kept listening.
"I knew someone," Masamuk said.
The hatred drained out of its voice as it said it, and what remained underneath was so much worse.

"I knew someone who made my entire existence feel brighter and happier just by being near her. Do you understand what that is, at my age? I had watched the first boundaries harden and the first eras turn to sediment, and I had felt many things across all of it, but she walked near me and existence itself was simply... better. I was in love with her. Wholly. And she loved me wholly in return. Two old things, in love the way young things are supposed to be."
The slime’s voice rasped softer.
"And when Those Who Remain targeted me, they did not come for my body. They came for her. Her records. Her...memories. They stripped me of all the memories of my love."

"Can you imagine it?" Masamuk asked, "Not even remembering or knowing those you love? They were artists about it. They cruelly left me with just enough. Enough to know that there WAS someone I loved. Enough to know the intensity of that love, its exact weight, its entire shape pressed into me like a fossil. And then... nothing. I do not remember her name. I do not remember her face. I do not remember her smile."
The small obsidian body trembled, once.

"And yet I remember how her laugh alone used to make me believe that everything would be okay. They left me that. They took away her very memory, her very Records, they took away even more than her, and they left behind the gaps, carved clean, so that I would always know the things that I lost even though I could never again remember them. I live inside a home where every room I loved has been emptied, and the outlines of the furniture remain on the floors."
BOOM!
Noah did not move. Behind the golden mask, his endlessly blue eyes burned!

"The pain that came from this was so unbearable," Masamuk continued, quiet as falling dust, "that for a moment... I wanted to die. I wanted... to die. Because why do we live? We live to enjoy, and to struggle against adversity. We live to be safe, and content, and happy. And Those Who Remain looked at all of that, everything living things live FOR, and they systematically took it away from me, piece by piece, gap by gap, as they almost took my will to live with it."
The crimson eyes opened, and turned from the grave, and looked directly at Noah, and in their dim ancient depths, beneath the sorrow and beneath the hatred,something grand and unbroken still burned.
"Almost."
"Almost..."

chapters.title: Chapter 5690: Rage!
paragraphs: "I wanted to die," Masamuk said. "But as my friend and Master always told me... Persevere. Regardless of the difficulty, Persevere. Regardless of the pain, Persevere. So... I Persevered!"
The small obsidian body straightened upon the luminous soil.
"But even while persevering," the slime finished quietly, "we were fractured."
Its crimson gaze turned towards the distant grave, towards the mound wrapped in eras of chains, humming softly under the weight of its newest layers.
"Many things could be said about... Those Who Remain."

Masamuk said the three words as if they were a heavy insult, spat slowly, each one set down with the deliberate contempt of a being who had watched what those words did when they were let loose upon existence!

"They are careful beings. They do everything to preserve what they hold, and they hold nearly everything. And as much as one can do alone in existence, and one can do a great deal..."The crimson eyes slid toward him. "...one cannot do it all alone. I could sit here and tell you of Dimensionality. Of Tongues. Of Causes and their deeper natures. None of it would truly matter. You need your own high level of power, yes. But you cannot be alone. THEY are never alone. And even here, I have been alone, and so I have not been able to do anything at all. I have laid beside this lake, and the moment I make a single move toward that grave, the eye above will also finally make its move."
Noah blinked at these words, and the shape of the problem turned over in his mind, and resolved itself with beautiful simplicity!
One watcher. One mover. One hiding thing that could act but not survive attention, and one visiting thing that could draw attention but not act. The board did not need a grander piece.
It needed a sacrifice that cost nothing!
"If I make the first move and draw its attention,"Noah asked calmly, "would you succeed in unearthing whatever part of Vakochev lies within?"
Masamuk’s gaze sharpened upon him.
"Your body here would die,"the slime said flatly. "Or worse. Be taken by Them."
Noah raised his hand, and turned it over slowly in the honeyed light, watching the stellar frame of it as one watches a borrowed tool.
"For me, this is only a dream. No harm comes to my existence whatsoever."
Masamuk looked at him silently, up and down, down and up.
Then an obsidian light flashed!
From within the small slime’s body, something rose and floated towards Noah, turning gently end over end. A grimoire!

It was bound in deep obsidian that drank the light of the layered sky, its cover smooth and unmarked, its edges worn round by an eternity of handling, and its pages, glimpsed as it turned, were filled with a script that seemed to rearrange itself shyly whenever his eyes came near, countless entries pressed dense as sediment!
"A journal of mine," Masamuk said simply. "Filled with my musings of existence, and what I know. Think of what you wish to hear me ramble on about while holding it, and the page should open up."
Noah accepted the grimoire with both hands, and the moment his fingers closed around the obsidian cover, prompts bloomed!
|You have received THE Obsidian Journal of Masamuk.|

|Within are the musings of one of the first shapers, accumulated since before authority was differentiated from raw potential. Its contents answer to intent: hold it, and think of what you wish to know.|
|The journal has been keyed to your existence alone. To all other perceptions, it does not exist.|
|The weavings of Masamuk settle around it. Even the Records will not gossip about this gift.|
The grimoire sank into his existence and disappeared, and Noah felt the weight of it settle somewhere deep, an entire era’s worth of rambling waiting patiently for his first question!
He then looked at Masamuk, and he nodded, once.
There was nothing else that needed saying.
Noah rose to his feet and looked at the distant grave.

Then he waved his hand across the lake below, and the whirlpool answered him! Strands of obsidian gold tore free of the turning waters as he grabbed a handful of the Provenance Causes, THE Stilled Wing and THE Lowered Crown and THE Quiet Name coiling in his grip like harvested lightning, oppressive and vibrant!
And he began to walk with grand steps towards the grave!

The masked farmers did not look up as he passed. Another white robe on the burial road, another armful of chains for the eternal work, his sandals pressing soft prints into the warm soil, the incense-heavy air parting around him.
He crossed the final terrace. He reached the edge of the vast cleared basin, where ten thousand layered harvests hummed upon the titan-length mound.
And then Noah broke the season!
He dropped the Causes he was carrying, all of them, letting the harvested chains spill carelessly across the sacred ground, and he JUMPED, his white robes snapping, and landed atop the grave itself!
BOOM!
And he began tearing the Causes apart!

His hands plunged into the layered chains of eras, and his Teloi blazed through his grip, and he RIPPED, strand from strand, THE Stilled Wing shredding between his fingers, THE Lowered Crown unraveling, whole condensed harvests tearing loose from the mound with sounds like existence clearing its throat, and the grave beneath his feet shone!
HUUM!
For one full second, the entire Dimension simply stared!
And then the sky spoke!
|Oh?|
The single syllable arrived pressed into every mind.
|THE GLOATING JAILER stirs from its magnificent mood.|

|It has waited a long time for this. It knew that if it sat beside its trophy patiently enough, one of the rats of Vakochev would eventually crawl out of whatever crack had sheltered it, and come scratching at the lid.|
|It is pleased. It does so enjoy being right.|
WAA!
The pressure came barreling down!

It fell upon Noah like the sky itself deciding to sit, and his figure was yanked up forcefully off the grave, hoisted into the open air above the mound by nothing at all, his limbs spread, his white robes whipping, the golden mask burning cold against his face!
Narrative crushed down all around him, and the obsidian eye in the layered sky turned, fully, for the first time in a while, and looked at him with its whole attention!

|Now then, little rat,| the voice rolled. |Where is the rest of him? The pieces were scattered so carelessly during the retreat. We have gathered some. We are missing others. You crawled here from one of his boltholes, which means you know the smell of the rest. Tell me where the rest of Vakochev lies.|
WAA!
And...the torture began!
Pressure closed around Noah’s existence like a fist around wet clay, and SQUEEZED!

Every quark of him screamed under compression, his Frame groaning, his singularities juddering in their orbits, pain of a magnitude he had never once sampled in all his climbing, the direct attention of an Immense One applied with the precision of a being that had unmade sovereigns for boredom!
|Huh, quiet a weak one you are...|
Noah endured without screaming!

His jaw locked behind the golden smile. His mind held. And in the crushing dark behind his eyes, words rose up to meet him, words from a message of the last will of the being whose grave he was currently bleeding on!
Rage. Rage!
Rage against the dying light! Do not go gentle! Rage! Rage! Rage!
HUUM!
’Rage,’ Noah told his own buckling existence, and his teeth ground behind the mask. ’Rage!’
And atop the wave of agony, with the audacity of the truly shameless, he worked!

The third cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis ignited across his quarks! The crushing force of an Immense One pressed down on every particle of him, and Noah seized that pressure and ROUTED it, weight flowing cell to quark to quark, bear, seat, stabilize, move, using the torture itself as the tempering hammer, converting an architect’s cruelty into his own foundation one particle at a time!
And then, hoisted and crushed and quietly forging, he looked down!

Below, across the terraces, dozens of masked Provenance Lifeforms had risen from their lakes and were staring up at the spectacle, white robes still, golden smiles upturned, and Noah gazed at them through the pain, and spoke.
"When did THE First Lifeforms fall so low?" he called down. "When did we become faces behind masks, following the orders of failures of existence?!"
BOOM!
The Dimension itself flinched!
|THE GLOATING JAILER’S mood is no longer magnificent.|
|It was going to be leisurely about this. It has decided otherwise.|
|Let us see the shape of you, rat. Let us see what you hold most dear in existence... and let us take it away!|
And the Moirai crashed into him!

It came as a flood of gold turned wrong, Existential Moirai weaponized, pouring into his existence with a single surgical purpose, to dig, to find, to ALTER, to reach into his Records and rewrite what it found there, to carve out his loves the way loves had been carved out of a small slime!
Trillions of needles drove into him at once, threading between his quarks, seeking his mother, his daughter, his wife, his people, seeking the furniture of his existence to empty the rooms!
But his existence defended itself.
Across every single one of his two hundred Decillion quarks, all at once, his Nine Teloi flared!

In every quark, nine points of light ignited and spread, shimmering into small golden shields, Quintessence and Existence and Paradox and Chaos and Adversity and Apocalypse and Mana and Harvest and Tyranny, nine seated aims standing up inside every particle of his matter simultaneously, and his entire body LIT UP, a man-shaped constellation of two hundred Decillion burning purposes, his generated Provenance blazing out of every seam of him!
And his purpose, his very Provenance... REJECTED the coming alterations of the Immense One!

The needles struck the golden shields and bent! The digging Moirai found no purchase, existence itself registering every quark of him as critical structure, as aimed and owned and not for editing, the flood of alteration breaking against nine-fold walls in every particle at once, and through the rejection, impossibly, gloriously, prompts flickered at the edge of his shredding vision!
|Your existence resists the alteration of its Records.|
|Under terrifying adversity, tempered by the pressure of an Immense One... your attributes begin to rise.|
But the pain!

The pain of trillions of needles breaking against trillions of shields inside him, of an Immense One’s will grinding against his foundations, of a Baryogenesis cycle running through the middle of it all! It was so painful that he wanted to scream!
He couldn’t help but scream!
The scream tore out of him and rolled across the entire Dimension, and above him the obsidian eye drank it in with vast satisfaction, its whole attention pressed down upon its screaming prize!
Its whole attention!
Below, beside a quiet lake, Masamuk’s crimson eyes went cold.

The melancholy drained out of them like water from a broken bowl, and what remained was the thing from before names, the splitter of Chaos, and its small obsidian body gazed at the eye drinking in the scream, and became blurry!
And it MOVED!
A flash of obsidian light shot low across the terraces, silent as a thought, and struck the grave!
It was only a nanosecond later that the eye above blinked, and its gaze snapped down toward its trophy!
But that nanosecond was enough!
What happened upon the grave in that sliver of time was a glorious, melancholic devouring.

Every Cause upon the mound, ten thousand layered harvests, countless chains, THE Stilled Wing and THE Lowered Crown and THE Quiet Name in their uncountable thousands, disappeared, consumed in a single silent pass.

And beneath them, unearthed for the first time in an unknown time, lay a vast golden coffin, and even as the Dimension’s light touched it, the coffin itself was EATEN, cleanly, immensely, the entire titanic vessel vanishing in one bite that left nothing behind but a fading afterimage stamped with enormous teeth marks!
And underneath it all...
Underneath was a cluster of invisible obsidian brilliance, wrapped in heavy, scorching, multicolored chains!
The chains blazed with a weight that had no business existing!

Across the distant terraces, masked Provenance Lifeforms cried out and LOOKED AWAY, sovereigns of self-generation physically unable to rest their gazes upon the bindings, and Noah, hoisted and screaming and burning golden in the sky, turned his eyes toward the unearthed thing and felt his existence almost pop like a balloon, the sheer power of the multicolored chains pressing against his perception like a boot against a bubble!
And the thing inside the chains!
It could not be perceived at all! Its Dimensionality was too high, a blankness deeper than the Quiet Name, a presence his senses reported only as a wound in what was possible!
But Noah had managed a glance! And in that single, existence-buckling glance, he could barely perceive...
Invisible hands, grasping the multicolored chains!
And pulling!
CRACK!
The chains began to crack, and it did not sound like metal, and it did not sound like authority.
It felt like existence itself... cracking!

chapters.title: Chapter 5691: One Word!
paragraphs: The chains shattered.
Multicolored fragments of scorching authority blew outward across the basin and dissolved into nothing before they landed, and from the devoured coffin’s resting place, something rose!
Noah, hoisted and burning in the grip of the Immense One, could not see it.

No one could see it! Its Dimensionality was too high, a walking wound in what was possible, perceivable only by the way existence flinched around its edges, by the prints that appeared in the luminous soil under no feet, by the way the honeyed air bent aside to let something pass!
An invisible part of a being, imperceivable and immense, standing free.
And the first thing it did was not rise toward the eye.
The invisible presence turned, and crossed the ruined grave, and knelt beside a small obsidian slime.
Masamuk lay at the edge of the torn mound where his devouring charge had ended, and Noah’s crushed perception dragged itself toward him, and what it found made his existence buzz.
The slime... was hazy!

Its small obsidian body, the body that contained countless folded dimensions, was losing its edges! Its deep translucent depths were thinning, its drifting stellar motes going out one by one like lamps down a long street, its entire simple form blurring as if the single nanosecond of that glorious devouring had asked for everything, as if the charge and the feast and the freeing had used up all of its existence at once.
And the invisible being held him.

There was nothing to see, and somehow it was unmistakable! The hazy little slime rose gently off the soil, cradled against a presence that could not be perceived, lifted the way something precious is lifted, and Masamuk’s dim crimson eyes looked up into a face that was not there, and tears fell.
Tears, from a splitter of Chaos.
They slid down the blurring obsidian body and dropped onto the ruined grave, and the slime’s soft rasped voice carried across the silent basin, small and breaking and unbearably gentle.
"If only I remembered. If only."
Noah’s existence clenched around the words.
If only I remembered!
He said this while his existence seemingly faded!
Had Masamuk been teetering at an edge this whole time?! Had the melancholic little thing beside the lake been spending its last reserves waiting for one chance, and this was it, and now it was gone?
Or was this only a body, one vessel of something vaster, falling apart while the true existence endured somewhere folded and safe?
The obsidian slime... surely wasn’t dead, right?!
He could not tell! His Regard was crushed, his perception was bleeding, and the haze kept thinning, and above it all, the sky laughed!
|Oh, how touching,| THE GLOATING JAILER boomed, and its cruelty was unhurried ans entirely unnecessary.

|The little rat spent itself utterly for one embrace it cannot even properly feel. Look at it leaking. Do you know, I could smell something old and sad somewhere in my fields. I assumed it was the grave itself. How delicious to learn my trophy came with a pet.|
The eye’s pressure ground down harder!
|And you, little farmer. You screamed so wonderfully. I do hope the pieces of you remember it, wherever pieces of rats go.|
HUUM!
And then Noah felt something heavy.
Through the crushing, through the grief, through the haze of a dying friend held by an invisible mourner, he perceived the force of nature in the coffin’s wake seemingly RISE.

The unperceivable presence straightened, still cradling the fading slime, and though it had no face and no eyes and no shape his existence could hold, Noah knew with total certainty that it was looking at HIM!
A Piece of Vakochev!
And in the deepest depths of his existence, the crystal shone!
Vakochev’s beacon blazed like a struck flare, pulsing light through his foundations, key and lock finally facing one another across a ruined grave, and an instant later...
The sky stopped playing.
|Enough of this.|
The Immense One applied undeniable force!

There was no wind-up and no flourish! The pressure that had been torture became verdict, the full unveiled seriousness of one of Those Who Remain closing around Noah’s Provenance Dream Body like a hand around a moth, and every defense he had was simply overwhelmed.

The nine-fold golden shields in his quarks blazed and broke! His singularities shrieked in their orbits! His Body, his Precepts, his blazing generated purpose, all of it was pressed past its limits at once, and Noah Osmont, in the last moments of a body that was only a dream, made a choice that no sane existence would make.
He opened himself to ALL of it!
’It is a dream,’ he thought, savage and clear inside the collapse.
’No harm comes to my existence. Which means this, right here, is the only place I can ever afford this lesson. So let me feel absolutely everything!’
And he felt it.
He felt his processes seethe and fight to the last.
The third Baryogenesis cycle roared on through the destruction, tempering quarks even as they burst!

His Teloi shields shattered and REFORMED and shattered again, nine aims refusing to stop standing up! His Sanguine weavings boiled, his Tongue pressed against his teeth wanting to speak Words into a dying mouth, every single system he had ever built raging against the verdict with the full stubbornness of his existence, and he catalogued all of it, every failure-point, every seam that held longest, every defense that died well, a complete map of his own limits drawn in his own destruction!
And here was the wonder that the pain could not drown.
Even applying its full seriousness, even with undeniable force, it still took the Immense One more than a nanosecond to finish him!

More than a nanosecond! His quarks did not crumble, they were overcome, each one holding to the last edge of its purpose, and as the final wave crushed inward, as his existence popped like a balloon at last and the Provenance of THE Human Dreamer scattered into radiant blue-gold mist across a ruined Dimension!
The sky spoke over his scattering, and its words were the cruelest it had said all day, because they were not even aimed at him.
As if THE Immense One gad simply killed an insignificant ant.

|Look at that. Yet another lifeform that moved for you, and lived for you, killed senselessly. You really are the worst, Vakochev. So many little ones dying for your sake. That little slime. That old granny. That black spider... so many avoidable deaths. So many...|
The words burned themselves into Noah’s dissolving perception.
His perception guttered. The Dimension smeared. And through the last thinning window of the Dream, Noah saw the eye of the Immense One gain more definition.

Its vast obsidian iris sharpened! Its gold-threaded depths clarified, texture and terrible detail resolving as if the gaze were descending, as if the being behind it had finally decided that watching from above was no longer sufficient, as if it were coming DOWN!
And in the next instant, the part of Vakochev that had been unleashed from the coffin... spoke.
It said a single word, with utmost coldness.
"Persevere."
HUUM!
One word!
One word, and Noah’s scattering perception was granted one final, perfect clarity, as if existence itself insisted he witness this properly.

He perceived every inch of the isolated Dimension at once, the terraced fields, the folded distances, the pale halls, the gold citadel stacked against the layered sky, the thousand lakes with their drowned suns, the hundreds of masked Provenance Lifeforms turning their golden smiles upward in dawning horror as...!
All of it disintegrated.
DISINTEGRATED!

The entire Dimension came apart in a single silent breath, soil and sky and citadel and lakes unmade together, the leashed sovereigns of the eternal Burial dissolving mid-turn with their harvests still in their arms, an era-old jail and every hand that had tended it erased between one fraction of an instant and the next, until nothing remained of the amputated Dimension at all!
Nothing, except a cold eye above!

The obsidian gaze hung alone in the formless dark where a Dimension had just been, stripped of its trophy, its fields, its farmers, and its joke, and only then, only after witnessing that single word do all of that, did Noah entirely feel his perception of this Dream ending!
BOOM!
Noah woke violently!

His body convulsed upward out of the scorching golden waters of THE Vasiliou Primordial Spring, a wave of liquid gold crashing off him as his entire body SHOOK, tremors rolling through him from crown to heel, his hands trembling against the warm rock edge, his breath tearing in and out of lungs that did not need air and demanded it anyway!

The steam pressed close and hot against his skin. The faded skeletons slept below. And his existence rang like a struck bell, because the effects of the torture, of the needles, of the collapse of a body by an Immense One’s undeniable force, had reached all the way back to his TRUE self!
It was several long moments before the shaking stilled.
And then the surge came!
His Provenance and his immensity rose, swelling through his foundations like a tide answering a moon, and prompts cascaded across his vision in radiant waves!
|The Provenance Dream has ended.|
|The Dream Body was destroyed. Your existence is unharmed. Everything felt was retained.|
|Accounting of the Dream begins.|
|Boon: THE Obsidian Journal of Masamuk remains keyed to your existence.|
|Boon: the crystal left behind by Vakochev is TRANSFORMING. Its purpose stirs.|
|Boon: the third cycle of THE Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis advanced tremendously under the tempering pressure of an Immense One.|

|Grandest Accounting: you stood beneath the direct torture of one of Those Who Remain. Your Records were assaulted, and you remained yourself. Your existence was crushed, and you remained yourself. Remaining true to what you are before a force that unmakes truth is a terrifying difficulty. It has been overcome.|
|Living truly is advancement.|
|VERITAS has risen to 86.|
|PROVENANCE has risen to 86.|
|PONDUS has risen to 78. POTENTIA remains INFINITE.|
Eighty-six!

The grief of a slime that might or might not still exist.

An eye that had begun to descend. And one word, spoken with utmost coldness, that had unmade an entire Dimension and every leashed sovereign in it faster than his perception could track the unmaking!
Persevere!

sentences.text: The chains shattered.
Multicolored fragments of scorching authority blew outward across the basin and dissolved into nothing before they landed, and from the devoured coffin’s resting place, something rose!
Noah, hoisted and burning in the grip of the Immense One, could not see it.
No one could see it!

Its Dimensionality was too high, a walking wound in what was possible, perceivable only by the way existence flinched around its edges, by the prints that appeared in the luminous soil under no feet, by the way the honeyed air bent aside to let something pass!
An invisible part of a being, imperceivable and immense, standing free.
And the first thing it did was not rise toward the eye.
The invisible presence turned, and crossed the ruined grave, and knelt beside a small obsidian slime.
Masamuk lay at the edge of the torn mound where his devouring charge had ended, and Noah’s crushed perception dragged itself toward him, and what it found made his existence buzz.
The slime... was hazy!
Its small obsidian body, the body that contained countless folded dimensions, was losing its edges!

Its deep translucent depths were thinning, its drifting stellar motes going out one by one like lamps down a long street, its entire simple form blurring as if the single nanosecond of that glorious devouring had asked for everything, as if the charge and the feast and the freeing had used up all of its existence at once.
And the invisible being held him.
There was nothing to see, and somehow it was unmistakable!

The hazy little slime rose gently off the soil, cradled against a presence that could not be perceived, lifted the way something precious is lifted, and Masamuk’s dim crimson eyes looked up into a face that was not there, and tears fell.
Tears, from a splitter of Chaos.
They slid down the blurring obsidian body and dropped onto the ruined grave, and the slime’s soft rasped voice carried across the silent basin, small and breaking and unbearably gentle.
"If only I remembered.
If only."
Noah’s existence clenched around the words.
If only I remembered!
He said this while his existence seemingly faded!
Had Masamuk been teetering at an edge this whole time?!
Had the melancholic little thing beside the lake been spending its last reserves waiting for one chance, and this was it, and now it was gone?
Or was this only a body, one vessel of something vaster, falling apart while the true existence endured somewhere folded and safe?
The obsidian slime... surely wasn’t dead, right?!
He could not tell!
His Regard was crushed, his perception was bleeding, and the haze kept thinning, and above it all, the sky laughed!
|Oh, how touching,| THE GLOATING JAILER boomed, and its cruelty was unhurried ans entirely unnecessary.
|The little rat spent itself utterly for one embrace it cannot even properly feel.
Look at it leaking.
Do you know, I could smell something old and sad somewhere in my fields.
I assumed it was the grave itself.
How delicious to learn my trophy came with a pet.|
The eye’s pressure ground down harder!
|And you, little farmer.
You screamed so wonderfully.
I do hope the pieces of you remember it, wherever pieces of rats go.|
HUUM!
And then Noah felt something heavy.
Through the crushing, through the grief, through the haze of a dying friend held by an invisible mourner, he perceived the force of nature in the coffin’s wake seemingly RISE.

The unperceivable presence straightened, still cradling the fading slime, and though it had no face and no eyes and no shape his existence could hold, Noah knew with total certainty that it was looking at HIM!
A Piece of Vakochev!
And in the deepest depths of his existence, the crystal shone!
Vakochev’s beacon blazed like a struck flare, pulsing light through his foundations, key and lock finally facing one another across a ruined grave, and an instant later...
The sky stopped playing.
|Enough of this.|
The Immense One applied undeniable force!
There was no wind-up and no flourish!

The pressure that had been torture became verdict, the full unveiled seriousness of one of Those Who Remain closing around Noah’s Provenance Dream Body like a hand around a moth, and every defense he had was simply overwhelmed.
The nine-fold golden shields in his quarks blazed and broke!
His singularities shrieked in their orbits!

His Body, his Precepts, his blazing generated purpose, all of it was pressed past its limits at once, and Noah Osmont, in the last moments of a body that was only a dream, made a choice that no sane existence would make.
He opened himself to ALL of it!
’It is a dream,’ he thought, savage and clear inside the collapse.
’No harm comes to my existence.
Which means this, right here, is the only place I can ever afford this lesson.
So let me feel absolutely everything!’
And he felt it.
He felt his processes seethe and fight to the last.
The third Baryogenesis cycle roared on through the destruction, tempering quarks even as they burst!
His Teloi shields shattered and REFORMED and shattered again, nine aims refusing to stop standing up!

His Sanguine weavings boiled, his Tongue pressed against his teeth wanting to speak Words into a dying mouth, every single system he had ever built raging against the verdict with the full stubbornness of his existence, and he catalogued all of it, every failure-point, every seam that held longest, every defense that died well, a complete map of his own limits drawn in his own destruction!
And here was the wonder that the pain could not drown.
Even applying its full seriousness, even with undeniable force, it still took the Immense One more than a nanosecond to finish him!
More than a nanosecond!

His quarks did not crumble, they were overcome, each one holding to the last edge of its purpose, and as the final wave crushed inward, as his existence popped like a balloon at last and the Provenance of THE Human Dreamer scattered into radiant blue-gold mist across a ruined Dimension!
The sky spoke over his scattering, and its words were the cruelest it had said all day, because they were not even aimed at him.
As if THE Immense One gad simply killed an insignificant ant.

So many little ones dying for your sake.
That little slime.
That old granny.

His perception guttered.
The Dimension smeared.

Its vast obsidian iris sharpened!

chapters.title: Chapter 5692: The First Entry
paragraphs: Noah sat within the scorching golden waters of THE Vasiliou Primordial Spring, steam rolling off his stellar body, and grasped THE Obsidian Journal of Masamuk with both hands.
The cover was warm, worn smooth by an eternity of small handling, and it drank the spring’s golden light without returning a single gleam. He held it, and he thought of exactly one thing.
Immense Ones!

He had just been tortured by one. He had hung spread beneath a lidless eye while trillions of needles hunted his loves through his quarks, and he had felt the difference between reading about a terror and being held in its hand!

His knowledge of the architects was a pile of secondhand fragments, warnings, and taunts. That was no longer acceptable. If he was going to survive these beings, and eventually bury them, he wanted to understand much more about them!
’Show me,’Noah thought into the warm obsidian. ’Immense Ones. Everything you rambled about them.’
HUUM!
The journal answered!
It rose gently from his hands and hung in the steam before him, and its cover swung open, and the pages began to flutter!

Endless white pages turned past his eyes, blank and blank and blank, an eternity of unmarked white flowing like a river of snow, until finally the fluttering slowed, and stopped, and the journal lay open to a single white page.
And on that page, words began to appear!

They surfaced out of the whiteness unhurried, dark strokes of old obsidian ink settling into lines, and Noah’s endlessly blue eyes settled onto the first sentence as the voice of a small melancholic slime rose off the paper and wrapped around his mind!
<The First Time I Met An Immense One>
There was a time when I was fascinated by THE Immense Ones. There was a time, and I record it here so I cannot deny it later, when I even looked up to them.
The young look up at whatever is tallest. I was young once, though the stars were younger.
In those days, my Master had just finished his grandest work. He had laid his Scales across the whole of Existence, and the whole of Existence was still ringing from the weight of them settling.
Everything that lived woke up that day inside a structure. Everything that lived could suddenly see the rung it stood upon, and the rung above it, and the long ladder going up into the light.
My Master was tired, and proud.
Then the invitation came.
It did not come as a message. It came as a door standing open in a place where no door had been, and my Master looked at it for a long moment, and said only, "One of the big ones wishes to talk."
I asked to come along. I was fascinated, as I have written. I wanted to see one of THE Immense Ones with my own eyes.
He allowed it. I have wondered since whether he allowed it because he wanted a witness.
We stepped through the door carefully, and what we stepped into was...unique.
The place was not a Dimension. It was not an Observable Existence, and it was not one of the Unobservable ones either.
It was a pocket of Narrative Existence.

There are beings whose Dimensionality runs so deep that they can set aside a portion of it and furnish it. The place we entered did not exist anywhere. It existed only inside the depth of the one who had designed it, the way a story exists only inside its teller.
To walk into it was to be included.We were, for the length of our visit, characters in a place she was quietly telling herself.
We stood in a garden at the end of a day that never finished ending.

There were low hills of dark grass that remembered being walked on. There was a porch of grey wood, and on the porch there was a table, and the table was set for two, with a settling warmth upon the cups as though they had been poured moments ago.
She was waiting on the porch.

I will not record her form, because her form was not the truth of her, and also because I could not hold it. What I could hold was the pressure of her, and the pressure was...immeasurably old, and immeasurably tired.
THE Immense One was...
THE REMINISCING WIDOW.
My Master inclined his head to her. She looked at him for a long time before she spoke.
"You have gone and done it, then," she said. "You have measured and scaled everything."
"I have given everything a structure," my Master replied.
"Yes," she said.
She poured nothing, and offered nothing. I stood at the edge of the porch, and I listened to the conversation.
"I called you here to warn you," THE REMINISCING WIDOW said.

"What you have built may bring you death. Not only you. All you love, and all who love you, down to the smallest thing that has ever smiled at your name. I am telling you this before the others finish deciding how they feel, because once they finish, no telling will matter."
My Master was not a man who frightened. He set his hands upon the table, and he asked.
"Why?"
"You will have to be more specific," she said. "There are so many answers."

"I gave Existence a structure that everyone can follow. Not a decree. A structure. A thing that stands the same for every lifeform that meets it, in every corner, in every era. Before my Scales, the low lived and died without ever knowing where they stood, or whether their striving moved them at all. Power was fog. Standing was rumor. Now every existence that faces adversity can see its own progress with its own eyes. Now the climb is real. All those facing adversity have a chance to elevate themselves, and to know it, and to be known for it."
"Hm." she said.

"I ended the age of begging,"my Master said. "You know what standing was before me. Standing was patronage. It was granted, and it was revoked, and it lived in the moods of the mighty. A framework that measures cannot be bribed and cannot be offended. The smallest lifeform in the smallest realm now holds something no architect ever gave it and no architect can take away. A rung."
"Go on,"she said.

"And what is measured is protected," my Master finished. "A thing with a recorded standing cannot be quietly erased. It leaves a mark upon the Records of what exists. I have made every life in Existence slightly harder to disappear. Structure...is the only mercy that scales."
I remember that I wanted to cheer!
THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked at him through the dusk for a long, long moment.
"Everything you have said is true, but..." she said.
She lifted her cup, and did not drink from it, and set it down again.

"You have heard, I am sure, what the young kinds whisper about my kind. That we are the ones who failed. The apex things that could not exceed themselves when the great exceeding happened. The bitter ones."
She was quiet for a moment.

"Some of us are exactly that. Some of my kind are precisely as small as the whisper says, and they are the loudest of us, and the cruelest, and they will hate your Scales for the plainest reason in Existence. Your ladder tells them, every day, in every corner of reality, that they stopped climbing."
"When your Scales teach the young to climb, you should ask yourself very carefully what you are teaching them to climb TOWARD."
BOOM!
I did not understand those words then. I am not certain I understand them now.
My Master was silent for a time. Then he said, "The others. What do they see, when they look at my work?"

"Three things,"she said. "First, the insult. You have ranked the unrankable, and dignity at our age is a wound that never closes. Second, the threat. Your structure gives adversity a ladder, and hope is heavy. Despair is formless, and formless things cannot organize."
"And third. The precedent. This is the one that will kill you. How dare you? What gave you the right to blanket all of existence under your scales when those so much grander than you have not?"
My Master was silent for a long time.
"Will they attack me? Will they come for the Scales?" my Master said.
"No," said THE REMINISCING WIDOW.

"They will not come for the Scales first. Destroying a maker’s work only proves the work mattered. They will come for everything that loves you. Death is small, maker. Death is singular, and it ends. I know this...too well."
She looked, then, at the second cup on the table,reminiscing!
My Master stood, after a time. He thanked her.
And at the door that was not a door, he stopped, and asked her the question.
"Why warn me at all?"
THE REMINISCING WIDOW sat on her porch, in her endless dusk, with her two cups.
"Because someone once built something grand for my sake, and no one warned him either."
The door closed. The evening went on without us.
My Master walked on in silence, and I moved beside him, and he never spoke of that visit again.
I record all of this now, an old thing writing by the light of everything that has since burned down, and I find I have only one remark to close the entry with.

My Master heard every word she said that evening. He weighed them, I am sure, on scales of his own. And then he went on exactly as he had planned, because he was a maker, and makers believe their works can bear any weight.
I have wondered, across all the eras since, whether he should have taken a bit more heed of that warning.
I wondered then.
I wonder still.

I wondered then.
I wonder still.

chapters.title: Chapter 5693: What Has Always Been
paragraphs: Noah sat in the scorching golden waters of THE Vasiliou Primordial Spring, the closed journal resting warm against his palm.
He reflected on everything Masamuk had recorded.

Vakochev had heard the warning. The maker of the Scales had sat on that porch, listened to an architect lay out the exact shape of his ruin, thanked her sincerely, and walked on exactly as planned. And why not?
He was the grandest maker of his era! His people were shapers and splitters of Chaos, titans who had stood since before authority had a name!
Not one of them, Noah suspected, had truly believed they would face losses. Not one of them had imagined that the existences of those they LOVED could simply be... rewritten.
Unwritten. Carved out like rooms being emptied while the house still stood.
They had prepared for war. No one prepares for erasure!
And the thought turned, as heavy thoughts always did, toward himself.
What if such a thing happened to him?
What if, in the worst scenario, he was made to forget his mother? Made to forget the woman who had stared down a preschool teacher with nothing but night shifts and love in her hands?
What if Henry was carved out of him, his son reduced to a warm gap and an outline on the floor? His women? His daughter? THE Infiniverse, who held his people inside her own body?

Or the other direction, which was somehow worse. What if THEY were made to forget HIM? What if he walked into his own Realm and his mother looked at him with the polite, careful eyes one gives a complete stranger?
It was a horrid thought, and Noah did not look away from it, because looking away from horrid thoughts was how Vakochev’s people had died!
And the biggest thing...
Even Vakochev may never have held this as something that could happen to HIM.
The strongest being of an entire era had likely carried the same quiet certainty Noah caught himself carrying every single day.
The certainty that regardless of what happened, he would be okay. That the story bent toward him. He was THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist, after all! Existence itself had handed him the author’s seat!
But if even Vakochev... if even such a being could be defeated, dismembered, buried under chains, and made into a smug jailer’s favorite joke...
Then even Noah Osmont, THE Human Dreamer, was not immune.
Warm arms found him while he sat in that thought.
Thalia had appeared in the spring without ceremony through that golden doorway, her stellar essence folding through the steam, and she saw his gaze before he could compose it.
She came down through the golden waters and grabbed his head and placed it gently against her chest, her fingers sliding into his hair, her heartbeat steady against his cheek.
"You have worried eyes again," Thalia said softly. "How did the talk with my Father go? It made you this melancholic?"
Noah let himself rest there for a moment, in the small warm feeling of her, and her bountiful chest.
"He is an interesting guy. I do have to do a lot of things to prove I can even hold you."
He felt her huff a quiet laugh above him.
"But we have to get going to these... Atlas Elseworlds. Atlas was profound enough to make Immense Ones worry and target him, and we need to understand why. We need to-"
Noah stopped speaking!
His senses blared, every alarm in his two hundred Decillion quarks firing at once, and none of them were pointed at any threat he could find.
What they were pointed at was her. The figure of Thalia Vasiliou, four columns of ninety-nine, the Queenling of the Vasiliou, was trembling and freezing against him!
He took his head out of her chest and looked up, and her face...!
Her eyes showed anger, and beneath the anger, a flash of something he had never once seen in her, not in the pool, not before the Ruling, not before her own mother.
Fear!
And she was not looking at him. She was looking beside him!
Toward the journal!
Noah turned, and his existence went cold, because unseen to his senses, unfelt by a single one of his blaring instincts, THE Obsidian Journal of Masamuk had opened by itself.
It lay upon the warm stone at the spring’s edge, open to the exact page he had just read, the entry of the porch and the dusk and the two cups.
And on that white page, in the middle of the old obsidian ink...
An eye had bloomed!

It was drawn and it was real at once, a single heavy-lidded eye of deep gold rendered upon the paper, and it was not decoration! Its gaze had weight, and its weight was pointed directly at him and Thalia, and words unfurled across the Dimension in the style he knew far, far too well!
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW asks: why will none of you simply leave things be?|
|She asks: why will none of you ever listen?|
BOOM!
Noah MOVED!

His Provenance flared to its absolute totality as every part of his quarks roared awake, nine Teloi igniting through every particle, his Infinite Sanguine Mana surging up through the golden waters in a rising crimson tide!

He grabbed onto Thalia, pulling her against him, and the full weight of THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer gathered behind his eyes as every ounce of power in the Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle coiled to erupt, to author, to override, to dream!
BOOM!
But...
Everything froze.
Everything.
The rising tide of Sanguine Mana hung motionless in the air, a sculpture of crimson gold. The steam stopped rolling.

The falls of essence on the Elsemountain above stood still in their descent. The Baryogenesis humming through his quarks paused between one particle and the next, and his Mantle, his Provenance, his Tongue, every authority he had ever generated or stolen or dreamed, sat inside him fully loaded and utterly unable to fire, like a scream held behind a hand!
And from the page, the eye became two.
And then a figure began to rise!
She came up out of the paper the way ink would rise if ink decided to stand, unhurried, vertical, impossible, the white page giving her up in slow flowing folds!
She rose to her full height above the open journal, and the steam of the sacred spring bent politely away from her, and Noah, frozen, beheld THE REMINISCING WIDOW!

She wore the loose draped grace of a highborn woman of some impossibly old court, pale cloth gathered at one shoulder and falling in long unhurried folds, her arms bare, her bearing neither armored nor adorned.
Her figure carried the same heavy settling pressure he read of, feminine and grand and immeasurably tired in a way that had made peace with its tiredness.
And her face!
Her face was astonishingly beautiful, and it could barely be perceived.
It slid off his gaze like light off deep water, arriving only in fragments, the line of a cheek, the suggestion of sorrow, beauty of a magnitude that perception itself refused to hold in full!

And around that half-veiled face floated two halos of golden metal, thin and perfect and slowly turning. One ringed her head at the height of her eyes, framing two heavy-lidded depths of gold. The second floated lower, ringing the height of her mouth, and when she spoke, her words did not come from her lips.
They came from everywhere, in the style of her kind, pressed into the Dimension itself for the two of them to read!
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW speaks, and she speaks sternly.|
|Existential Narrative is the most critical thing that THE Immense Ones hold. It is our marrow. It is our estate. I warned Masamuk, ages ago, not to even peer into us.|
|If you share our records, if you read of me in a journal, my words and what I said ages ago... my Narrative can sense this. The telling reaches back to its owner. You then give me access.|

|I warned him. I warned his Master on my own porch, with my own evening. He did not listen. His Master did not listen. And now an old entry is read beside a sacred spring, and here I am, because none of you ever, ever listen.|
The two golden halos turned slowly, and her half-perceived gaze settled upon the frozen pair in the water, and the dusk of her deepened until the golden spring itself seemed to dim toward evening.
|So she asks, and she is tired of asking: if warnings are not enough, just what do I need to do for you all to leave things alone?|
|There is no scenario of change.|
|There is no scenario of victory.|
|There is only what is... and what has always been.|
BOOM!
The words settled over the spring like a lid over a coffin!

Noah’s eyes swirled with endless seas of blue! His Infinite Sanguine Mana RAGED against the stillness, a boundless ocean throwing itself at the inside of a single frozen moment, his quarks howling, his Teloi blazing, his Mantle straining to author a single syllable of override, and none of it moved!

Not a finger. Not a thought made real. He, who had torn an architect’s executioner in half, who had walked through an ancient boundary as though it were a dream, who had endured the torture of a lidless eye and come out heavier!
He looked at the manifestation of an Immense One standing on the page of a journal, risen out of ink and an old evening, and he could not move!
Thalia was frozen against his chest. The spring was frozen around them. The golden skeletons slept below, and above them all stood a widow in her endless dusk, patient and stern and immeasurably sad.
Catastrophe had arrived far, far too soon!
