chapters.title: Chapter 5694: A Kindness To Kill!
paragraphs: She looked at them the way an era looks at a single day!

THE REMINISCING WIDOW had risen from the page of an obsidian journal, and she stood above the golden spring with her barely-perceivable face angled down, her two golden halos turning their slow deliberate circles in the steam-heavy air, and she did not move or speak as she regarded the two small frozen figures below her.

She did not need to hurry. She had presided over evenings that outlasted kingdoms, and two lifeforms arrested mid-embrace in a sacred spring were not, by any measure of her long experience, cause for urgency!
The dusk she carried pressed down as her gold eyes swept across the figure of Thalia Vasiliou and settled upon THE True Human Emperor, and she spoke!
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW speaks.|
|It is always the same. Lifeforms touch power. They look at the existing structure. And then they promise themselves that they will change it.|
|Why?|

|There is a system in place, and no matter its potential negatives, it has been working. Those like you, when you seek to enact change, cause such tremendous bloodshed. Truly. All you need to do is stop.|
The halos pulsed, golden light rippling through the steam!
|I permit you to speak.|
Noah moved!

The golden spring erupted around him as he came free, his Infinite Sanguine Mana surging up in a massive crimson tide, his eighty-six Provenance singularities igniting across every particle of his Baryogenesis-hardened existence, nine Teloi blazing through two hundred Decillion Provenance Telos Quarks as the weight of THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist Mantle coiled behind his eyes with the pressure of a narrative about to be REWRITTEN!
And then he said absolutely nothing.

He took his time with it! He turned slowly in the golden water and he faced the manifestation standing above him, this impossible figure of dusk and golden light and barely-perceivable grief, and he looked at her with the full swirling weight of his existence behind his eyes, and he was simply, completely, wordlessly silent.
She had told him he could speak. She had permitted him.
Just because she permitted him, he now had to?
He chose not!

But while his mouth stayed shut his mind did not, as behind those seas of blue, THE True Human Emperor thought at the speed of a being whose quarks had each carried the weight of Existence and survived it.
He stared at the Immense One and he worked, because something about this entire picture was wrong in a way that the threat itself could not account for!

Masamuk had known. He had to have known! The ancient slime had existed since before the first Domains had a name, had served the grandest maker of his era, had suffered the stripping of every loved memory and still endured, and he had sat in a Dimension with three Provenance Causes and the weight of Vakochev’s chained weavings pressing down on him, and he had willingly handed Noah his journal!
He had known what was written in it! He had known that reading it could do exactly this!
So why?
Would a being who had suffered so precisely not understand the danger? Would a mind that had persevered through eras of loss make an oversight so catastrophic?

Noah’s eyes held steady on the Widow’s golden rings and he turned the question over and over as his Teloi hummed their low burning note through his matter, searching for the answer that a grieving ancient slime had buried somewhere in the ink!
And one sentence surfaced above all the others!
A single line from the closing of the entry, the thing Vakochev had asked at the door when the evening was ending and the warning was finished. WHY warn him at all?
And she had answered!
Because someone once built something grand for my sake, and no one warned him either.
Someone had built something grand for her sake. Nobody had warned him!
And Masamuk had known this too!
There was something in that! Something Noah had not yet pulled to the surface, but he was circling it now as his existence hummed with the warmth of a coming understanding.
Above him, THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked at his silence with patience that had no floor to it, and the golden halo at her mouth pulsed once, and she spoke again.

|Vakochev is done for. He was done for across many deaths and ages of pain inflicted upon him and all those who loved him. You are reading the musings of one of his greatest, and yet I hold no memory of you, which means you are not one of Vakochev’s people.|
|You are one of those like him. One of those with Boundless Potential. Infinite Potential.|

|Lifeforms like you are walking disasters. You carry a sense of infinite hunger within you that you cannot quiet and will not quiet, and you bring destruction and apocalypse to every corner of existence your trajectory sweeps across. The greatest threat to your people is not any enemy you will face. It is you. People like you who simply will not stop.|

|You do not need any of this. You could sit still on a farm somewhere. You could enjoy your family, your feasts, your people, let the millions and millions of years of existence wash over you and hold you warmly. Existence will continue to unfold without you. It has done so since before your kind had eyes to witness it.|
|Just stop.|

|I warned Vakochev before he fell. He did not stop. I warn you now. If I must be forceful, if ending you here is the necessary kindness to save countless lifeforms the pain your trajectory will inflict on them, I will do so.|
BOOM!
She descended!

She came down through the steam and the golden light, the halos orbiting her descent, her form lowering until her barely-perceivable face was close, until the dusk of her filled the whole of Noah’s vision and the pressure of an attended eternity sat in the air between them!
"Will you stop?"
Noah looked at Thalia.

She was frozen at his side, the Queenling of the Vasiliou, with her eyes wide and that first-ever flash of fear across her face, and for one stretched instant he held that sight and felt everything that lived inside him on the subject of it.
And then he spoke!

"I cannot stop," Noah said. "Nobody knows this. But I live in constant fear! Fear of exactly something like this, a power I cannot deny standing before me and I cannot even lift a finger against it! Because of exactly something like this, I cannot stop! I have to attain more power! I have to find the absolute peak of existence to make sure that nothing can ever stand before me and simply decide my fate!"
HUUUM!
THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked at him, and her gold eyes held no anger, and they held no mockery.
"But this is only because you will not stop,"she said.
"If you stop, nothing like me will appear before you again. You will have no need for that fear."
Noah shook his head!

"I live in fear that if I ever retreat to my farm, if I simply live and eat and love my family and do nothing to advance, we will all one day die from a choice others like you made! My Dimension collapsed without our say! My people were ground beneath an existence they never once consented to stand inside! Existence itself changed around us without a word in our direction!"

His Provenance blazed through the steam as his voice held its quiet and steady weight. "If I do nothing, if I stop, I would live every day of every million years feeling like an ant. Waiting for a boot I cannot see, held by a foot I cannot name, and knowing that when it falls it will find everyone I love standing beside me. And I will have been the one who decided that the feast was worth more than the capacity to PROTECT the feast!"
He looked at the barely-perceivable face before him and let both things be true at once, the fear and the refusal of the fear, and his voice did not waver!

"So no. Regardless of what you say here. Regardless of what happens today!" A pause, as his singularities blazed their quiet blue-gold light through the golden water."I cannot stop. My fear will not let me. My Quintessence will not let me. My humanity..."
BOOM!
"...will not let me!"
The spring held its quiet around those words.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked at him.
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW looks at you, and she grieves, and she speaks her decision.|
|Then for the sake of saving the pain and deaths of many, even your own people, I will end you.|
|Every point of your origin across Existence and Time. I will make it so that you never exist, so that your people and many others can attain salvation from what your trajectory would bring them.|
|It is the kindness I can give you.|

It has done so since before your kind had eyes to witness it.|
|Just stop.|
|I warned Vakochev before he fell.
He did not stop.
I warn you now.
If I must be forceful, if ending you here is the necessary kindness to save countless lifeforms the pain your trajectory will inflict on them, I will do so.|
BOOM!
She descended!

She came down through the steam and the golden light, the halos orbiting her descent, her form lowering until her barely-perceivable face was close, until the dusk of her filled the whole of Noah’s vision and the pressure of an attended eternity sat in the air between them!
"Will you stop?"
Noah looked at Thalia.

She was frozen at his side, the Queenling of the Vasiliou, with her eyes wide and that first-ever flash of fear across her face, and for one stretched instant he held that sight and felt everything that lived inside him on the subject of it.
And then he spoke!
"I cannot stop," Noah said.
"Nobody knows this.
But I live in constant fear!
Fear of exactly something like this, a power I cannot deny standing before me and I cannot even lift a finger against it!
Because of exactly something like this, I cannot stop!
I have to attain more power!
I have to find the absolute peak of existence to make sure that nothing can ever stand before me and simply decide my fate!"
HUUUM!
THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked at him, and her gold eyes held no anger, and they held no mockery.
"But this is only because you will not stop,"she said.
"If you stop, nothing like me will appear before you again.
You will have no need for that fear."
Noah shook his head!
"I live in fear that if I ever retreat to my farm, if I simply live and eat and love my family and do nothing to advance, we will all one day die from a choice others like you made!
My Dimension collapsed without our say!
My people were ground beneath an existence they never once consented to stand inside!
Existence itself changed around us without a word in our direction!"
His Provenance blazed through the steam as his voice held its quiet and steady weight.
"If I do nothing, if I stop, I would live every day of every million years feeling like an ant.
Waiting for a boot I cannot see, held by a foot I cannot name, and knowing that when it falls it will find everyone I love standing beside me.
And I will have been the one who decided that the feast was worth more than the capacity to PROTECT the feast!"
He looked at the barely-perceivable face before him and let both things be true at once, the fear and the refusal of the fear, and his voice did not waver!
"So no.
Regardless of what you say here.
Regardless of what happens today!" A pause, as his singularities blazed their quiet blue-gold light through the golden water."I cannot stop.
My fear will not let me.
My Quintessence will not let me.
My humanity..."
BOOM!
"...will not let me!"
The spring held its quiet around those words.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked at him.
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW looks at you, and she grieves, and she speaks her decision.|
|Then for the sake of saving the pain and deaths of many, even your own people, I will end you.|
|Every point of your origin across Existence and Time.
I will make it so that you never exist, so that your people and many others can attain salvation from what your trajectory would bring them.|
|It is the kindness I can give you.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5695: It Is Never So Easy!
paragraphs: Power was not going to save him today!
Noah stood in a frozen spring with an Immense One’s declaration hanging over everything, and he understood there was no way.
His Provenance blazed, his Teloi burned through his quarks, his Mantle coiled with narrative weight enough to rewrite a battlefield, and none of it mattered against something like this.
Her Dimensionality was too unfathomable.
So he did the only other thing he knew how to do!
He thought.
Not ordinary thinking, but thinking elevated by his very Provenance of THE Human Dreamer, as his eyes stayed fixed on the barely-perceivable face of THE REMINISCING WIDOW....
Noah pulled THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer deep into himself and turned it fully inward.
The Human Dreamer was a Lens.And right now it turned on everything he had read!

Everything in his existence became dreamlike as he envisioned himself thinking at speeds as if time had stopped, and his existence analyzing and having epiphanies every instant as he dreamed of information and solutions.
His entire existence became surrounded by a dreamy light as his eyes even seemed heavy as if he would soon fall asleep, and yet his eyes were...ridiculously bright!
He began to think.
What did he KNOW about her?

The journal entry! He had read every word of it while she was still ink on a page. She had sat on a porch in an endless dusk at a table set for two, with one chair ever sat in and a second cup kept almost warm.

She had warned Vakochev because of something that had happened to HER, because someone had built something grand for her sake and nobody had warned him either, and she had been attending evenings alone ever since!
She was a WIDOW!
Which meant she had not always been one!

Which meant there was someone, once, who had sat in the second chair and drunk from the second cup, and she had watched that someone be ended, and the second cup had been almost warm ever since because she could not bring herself to stop filling it!
But there was more! She had warned Vakochev! She had called him to her porch and laid out the full anatomy of his ruin, piece by careful piece, and then she had let him walk away.
She had not stopped him! She had not ended him on the spot the way she now threatened to end Noah, for all that the result of his not-stopping was exactly the catastrophe she had predicted.
Why?
Why warn someone if you believe the warning cannot matter? Why give a choice to something you believe will choose wrong?
His Provenance ran faster, linking, linking, linking!
And Noah felt the understanding arrive like a dreamy knowledge of brilliance as his eyes cut upward to the barely-perceivable face of the Immense One above him and his mouth opened.
"What about you?"
"THE REMINISCING WIDOW." He held her barely-perceivable gaze without flinching. "Who made you a Widow? Did you simply stop? Your love that they killed... would he have wanted you to stop?"
BOOM!
Existence buzzed!
The golden warmth of THE Vasiliou Primordial Spring vanished beneath an instant blanket of frost and cold as temperature dropped across the whole region of the Elsedimension.
She looked at him!
For a long, long moment she simply looked at him.
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW speaks: careful now.|
|There are things you can speak of. And things that will bring your ruin far quicker.|
Noah did not move back.
He held his ground in that frozen spring with Thalia motionless beside him and his entire existence at a full stop.
"You did not stop," he said!
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW is still.|

"The second cup in that memory,"Noah said. "You still fill it. After everything. After every era that has passed since the one who sat there last. You still go out onto that porch, in that endless dusk you carry with you everywhere, and you set the table for two, and you keep the second cup almost warm. That is not someone who stopped."
Frost crystals ticked softly against frozen water in the silence that followed!
THE REMINISCING WIDOW did not respond immediately, as the gold of her eyes, heavy-lidded and ancient and full of a sorrow she had long since made peace with, pulsed!
She spoke unfathomably slowly.
|He...was not like the ones who came before or after him.|
And for the first time in the conversation something in the Widow’s bearing shifted.

|He made immensity itself. Everything he designed, everything he shaped and carved and made real, he made it so it could exist without him. So it could outlast him. So others could find their way inside it long after his hands were gone.|
Her gaze found something beyond the spring, beyond the Elsedimension, something that only existed inside the depths of her!
|He believed that existence deserved better architecture. He spent... a very long time on it.|
"And he was ended for it," Noah said.
|Yes.|
"By beings like you."
The cold deepened for one instant and then settled again, and her voice remained exactly level.

|By those of us who looked at what his foundations were pointing at, and made the same calculation I made when I looked at Vakochev’s Scales. That the direction of the pointing would bring tremendous death to countless lifeforms before any destination was reached...Yes.|
Noah’s eyes pulsed as he felt like he was a opening a door, and he needed to spread it much wider.
He had to spread it wide!
"You warned Vakochev, but you did not end him there. You gave him the choice."
|I gave him the information. The choice was always his.|
"Why? Why give a choice to something you believe will choose wrong? If the outcome is catastrophe either way, why warn? Why call him to the porch at all?"
The golden halos pulsed! The Widow was quiet for a moment that stretched!
|Because I am not in the business of stealing choices from beings who have the capacity to make them. Even wrong ones.|
Her eyes held steady on him.
|Even from beings who will make exactly the wrong one.|
"That sounds,"Noah said quietly, "like someone who is not entirely certain the choice is wrong."
HUUM!
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW does not answer.|
"Vakochev could not stop," Noah said, and his voice was very gentle now.

"Not because he was reckless. Not because he was careless of the cost. But because of who he was. He was the kind of being who looked at the way things were and could not rest inside the wrongness of them."
He looked up at her. "Is a river wrong to flow downhill? Is it a flaw in the river’s nature that it carves the canyon?"
|Rivers carve canyons.|
She said it casually.
|And the canyon floor becomes a grave for everything that falls in.|
"Yes," Noah said. "And the river also carries everything forward. And makes things grow. And finds the sea."
He looked up at her barely-perceivable face, at the sorrow arriving in fragments.

"The one who built something grand for your sake... he was that kind of river too, wasn’t he? He could not look at the way things were built and simply accept it. He had to try to build something better. Not for himself. For others. He could not stop that drive any more than Vakochev could. Any more than I can."
The frost on the spring’s surface crackled softly!
"And he was ended for it," Noah said, "by those who thought that stopping him was a kindness to the many. The same calculation you are making about me, right now."
He held her gaze.
"Does that mean they were right? Does it mean that if someone had simply convinced him to stop, to go to his farm and enjoy his ages and trouble no one, that existense would have been better?"

"Or does it mean that existence lost something it did not know it needed, and the only monument to that loss is a second cup on a table in an endless dusk that you can never bring yourself to stop filling?"
|THE REMINISCING WIDOW is very still.|
The cold was absolute. The frost was absolute. The silence was absolute!

And then, slowly, the gold of the heavy-lidded eyes that had been looking at him from above the height of the spring lowered, just slightly, just one degree, as a thought arrived in them that had not been invited!
And for just a moment, one frost-cracked moment that stretched wider than it should have, something moved across the barely-perceivable face.
It was doubt!

And then it was gone, and her composure returned, and she looked at him, and she blinked once, and when her eyes opened again they held a different quality, something sharpening beneath the heaviness, a mind arriving at a conclusion that had nothing to do with him!
|Ah.|
It was barely a word! It was the sound a vastly experienced intelligence makes when it catches itself being played.
|Ah, I see. That little slime gave you these records purposefully. So that I could meet you like I met them ages ago.|
The gold eyes were steady on him now, and something in their depths was almost, almost amused.
|That little slime... was trying to manipulate an Immense One? To use my name, and what happened to me, to what end? Instead of warn, now support another one of the monsters of existence?|
The frost held its silence around them!

And then from the Widow above the journal above the frozen spring, in a voice that had not changed its composure by a single degree, came the one thing Noah had not expected to hear from an Immense One who had just declared his erasure!
A sound that was almost, almost a laugh!
|Haha.|
Her golden halos turned.
|Is it so easy?|

chapters.title: Chapter 5696: Probability! I
paragraphs: |THE REMINISCING WIDOW speaks: you know what? I will leave it entirely up to chance.|
The frost held its stillness across the whole of the spring as the golden halos turned!
|You are throwing arguments that you are like Vakochev. Or like someone you cannot even fathom. Someone whose name you have not earned the right to hold in your mouth.|
|Okay.|
|Let us put that to the test.|
She waved her hand!
BOOM!

A blinding singularity bloomed in the frozen air above the spring, and Noah’s eyes narrowed against it as the light collapsed inward on itself and left something spinning slowly in the space where it had been!
A ring.
It was gray, and it was small, and it was the least impressive object Noah had ever seen an Immense One produce.

It turned in the air without hurry, and across its outer band ran lines that did not behave, lines that went around the ring and came back on the other side without ever crossing an edge, an outside that was also the inside, a single unbroken surface pretending to be two.
And on its interior, where a finger would go, there were spikes!
They filled the inner circumference completely, dozens of them, gray and sharp and angled inward toward the center, leaving no opening at all. Not a narrow opening. Not a difficult one.
None.
It was a ring that could not be worn, and it had been made that way on purpose.
|This was left behind by a special someone.|
The Widow’s voice pressed into the frozen air from everywhere at once.

|I have not been able to figure it out. Neither has any other Immense One I have given it to, and I have given it to several, across a great many eras. It has been examined by minds that predate the frameworks you climb.|
|If you wish to throw arguments that you are like others, if you wish to compare yourself to them...|
|Put this ring on.|
The gold of her eyes did not move from him.
|If you can put that ring on, I will spare you. You may continue your path. The path that will inevitably lead to more deaths than you will ever be able to count.|
The ring drifted toward him through the frozen steam.
Noah watched it come, and his gaze became heavy.
How the hell would he be able to put on a ring that even Immense Ones could not figure out?!

They had eras. He had a conversation! They had Dimensionality that made his own look like a puddle beside a sea, and they had turned this small gray thing over in their attention and set it back down without an answer!
The ring reached him.
Noah’s hand rose out of the frozen water and closed around it, and it was cold, and it was heavier than it had any right to be, and the spikes pressed against his palm.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW looked down at him coldly.
|Well? Put it on.|
|You are just like them, are you not? Like Vakochev. Like the one whose foundations I watched be broken.|

|There will be no thinking you can talk your way out of this after. You have had your conversation. If the ring does not go on, there will simply be a thorough narrative ending for all parts of your existence, across every point of origin you have ever occupied.|
It felt like a taunt from death itself!
Noah ignored the words entirely.
He closed his eyes.
He held the ring in both hands, in that frozen spring, with Thalia motionless beside him and an Immense One’s verdict hanging over the whole of the Elsedimension, and he felt it.
He turned it over. He examined every part of the thing with senses that had catalogued Existential Treasures and Remnants and the bones of First Lifeforms.
And all he saw was question marks!
Naturally, he wanted to try infusing it with his Provenance, to push a thread of himself into that gray band and see whether anything at all would answer, but...
CRACK!
His existence shook.

Noah’s eyes flew open as he felt something crack inside him, something deep, something that had been sitting in his existence for some time now that he had stopped feeling its weight, and he looked down at his own chest with genuine shock as he realized what it was!
THE Aurate Collar!

The treasure he had taken from THE Ymnaros Dimension! The chest bones of a Provenance Lifeform, the covenant object of THE First Purity, the thing that had produced the white pool and everything that had come out of it!
It was breaking!
He felt it come apart inside his existence, piece by piece, the bone splitting along lines he had never known were there, and it did not shatter into fragments and it did not burn away!
It turned to liquid!

Bronze liquid, thick and slow and shining, flowed out of his existence in a stream that passed through his chest and down his arm and out of him entirely, and Noah watched with his mouth slightly open as the treasure he had worn poured out of him and went toward the small gray ring in his hands.
The liquid wrapped around it!
It coated the band and ran along the impossible lines and filled the inside of the ring completely, and where it touched, the spikes began to RECEDE.
They drew back into the inner wall of the ring, slowly, one after another, sliding inward and vanishing as though they had never been forged there at all.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW blinked!

Noah saw it. He saw an Immense One who had not moved a single degree of her composure across the entire conversation, who had declared his erasure blink down at his hands with something that was unmistakably incredulity!
And Noah was incredulous too!
No way, right?
And in the next moment, the ring moved!
It tore itself out of his hands on its own and shot to his right hand and drove itself onto his finger, and the spikes had not receded all the way!
SHRK!
They tore through his skin as though his defenses did not exist!

The chest bones of a Provenance Lifeform, the covenant object of THE First Purity, the thing that had produced the white pool and everything that had come out of it!
It was breaking!
He felt it come apart inside his existence, piece by piece, the bone splitting along lines he had never known were there, and it did not shatter into fragments and it did not burn away!
It turned to liquid!

Bronze liquid, thick and slow and shining, flowed out of his existence in a stream that passed through his chest and down his arm and out of him entirely, and Noah watched with his mouth slightly open as the treasure he had worn poured out of him and went toward the small gray ring in his hands.
The liquid wrapped around it!
It coated the band and ran along the impossible lines and filled the inside of the ring completely, and where it touched, the spikes began to RECEDE.
They drew back into the inner wall of the ring, slowly, one after another, sliding inward and vanishing as though they had never been forged there at all.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW blinked!
Noah saw it.

He saw an Immense One who had not moved a single degree of her composure across the entire conversation, who had declared his erasure blink down at his hands with something that was unmistakably incredulity!
And Noah was incredulous too!
No way, right?
And in the next moment, the ring moved!
It tore itself out of his hands on its own and shot to his right hand and drove itself onto his finger, and the spikes had not receded all the way!
SHRK!
They tore through his skin as though his defenses did not exist!

chapters.title: Chapter 5697: Probability! II
paragraphs: Noah’s crimson gold blood welled up instantly around the band, and there was no resistance at all, no interception, none of his Provenance Body’s layers doing anything whatsoever, and his blood ran hot down his finger and into the gray metal.
And the ring drank it.

It sucked the crimson gold in greedily, absorbing every drop that touched it, and only THEN, only after it had tasted his blood, did the remaining spikes fully recede and the band clasp itself around his finger.
And then it began to shine!

Gold erupted along the ring’s surface, a terrifying gold, deep and old and heavier than any light Noah had ever generated. The impossible lines on its outer band lit up and began to pulse, the single unbroken surface running its endless circuit, light chasing itself around a shape that had no outside and no inside, faster and faster and faster!
The ring clasped tight on his finger and...
BOOM!
A blinding golden light detonated across the frozen spring!

And with it came a VOICE! A voice that felt old, and elegant, and filled with a kind of ingenuity that Noah recognized instantly as belonging to a mind that had never once in its existence been satisfied with how things were.
|Before the first light, before the first law, we were, and we were our own...|
Those words!
Noah’s whole existence went rigid, because he knew those words! They were the words of THE Aurate Collar! The covenant voice that had repeated inside it since the moment he had put it on.

The words he had spoken, only the first line of them, to trigger THE Provenance Kismet of First Purity, which had produced the white pool, which had opened across time and delivered Thalia Vasiliou into his Realm!
He heard them again now, in his mind, in that golden light.
And this time, they continued!
|Before the first light, before the first law, we were, and we were our own...Nothing granted, nothing borrowed, nothing owed. What I am, I made. Let existence bear witness.|
HUUM!

The words resounded again and again in his mind, rolling through him, and Noah understood exactly what was being asked of him, because it was the same thing that had been asked of him once before, when he had spoken only a single line of it and existence had answered.
This time he said the whole thing.
"Before the first light, before the first law, we were, and we were our own...Nothing granted, nothing borrowed, nothing owed. What I am, I made. Let existence bear witness!"
HUUM!
Every particle of the blinding golden light vanished instantly!

Noah blinked in the sudden absence of it, standing in the frozen spring with steam frozen around him, and he looked down at his right hand where a golden ring now sat on his finger, pulsing slowly, its impossible lines still running their endless circuit.
Then he looked up at THE REMINISCING WIDOW.
She was extremely still.
And Noah’s eyes pulsed, because shockingly, unbelievably...
He could see her!

Not fragments. Not a line of a cheek arriving and sliding away. Not a beauty that perception itself refused to hold. He looked up at the Immense One standing above the frozen spring and he could actually see and perceive her cleanly!
And just as he began to truly look at her...
The ring on his hand became unfathomably hot!
And a grand booming voice erupted out of it, only for him to hear.
|Destiny and fate are not real. Not entirely, anyway.|

|What is real is probability. Destiny and fate are merely the outcomes of probabilities, and every outcome that has ever been called inevitable was simply a number that got large enough to look like a law.|
|So consider the numbers, whoever you are.|

|The probability of my ring landing in the hands of a lifeform who is not an Immense One, when I left it in the keeping of an Immense One. And then, on top of that, the probability of that same lifeform independently satisfying two of the prior conditions I set, so that the ring could actually trigger and activate.|
|The probability of both of those events occurring is so infinitesimally low that for them to happen at all, the lifeform in question has to be someone who beats the odds.|
|They have to be someone who can bend Narrative Probability.|
|And with such a lifeform... maybe there is a chance.|
|Hello, and welcome to these crazy weavings of life.|
|I am Atlas.|
|And I hope that maybe, just maybe, your probability, and your capability to bend it, is grander than mine was. For existence is vast, and there is much to be done.|
Atlas?
THE Atlas?!
Noah’s existence buzzed with pure incredulity as the name landed in him and detonated.
THE ENGINEER!

The one who ran circles around Immense Ones! The being who had designed Elsedimensions and Provenance Body arts and weapons made to kill architects, the one whose legacy Aurelius Vasiliou had told him to go and find!
That Atlas!
And the second understanding arrived right behind the first, faster and heavier.
So HE was the man who made THE REMINISCING WIDOW into a widow.
The one who sat in the second chair! The one whose cup was still being kept almost warm at a table in an endless dusk after however many eras had passed.
He had been out here, this early, close enough to an Immense One that she had spent every age since setting a place for him at her table!
But even as Noah was thinking all this...
|Now, since we are here, let us play some more games of probability and choices. Okay?|
The voice echoed out of the golden ring on his finger, entirely too pleased with itself.
|Because maybe, even after all those different probabilities are met, there could still be a factor of luck. And luck is a variable I never liked leaving in a design.|
|So here is a choice.|
|You have somehow gotten a grand artifact designed by me, out of the hands of an Immense One.|
|Will you keep the artifact and infuse it with your Provenance? You may consider it a weapon that could topple an Immense One, if it is used correctly.|
|Or the second option. Will you give it back to the Immense One?|
|It carries some sentimentality.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5698: Engineer! I
paragraphs: Noah controlled his expression, and internally he cursed with everything he had.
What fucking choice?!
Because there was no choice. The choice to be made here was clear, and it was horrible, and it was clear precisely because it was horrible.
A weapon that could topple an architect, offered to a man standing frozen in front of one, and the correct answer was to hand it back!
Noah did not hesitate.

He gripped the golden ring and physically pulled it off his finger, the metal coming free without resistance now, and he drew his arm back and threw it up through the frozen steam toward THE REMINISCING WIDOW!
"This ring was given to you."
His voice carried across the whole of the frozen spring!

"It is a grand artifact and I could choose to keep it. But I know what it means to you. It was the last thing he gave you." He watched it turn end over end as it rose toward her. "You can now put it on."
The ring reached her.
THE REMINISCING WIDOW caught it.

She did not speak as she held the small golden band in fingers that Noah could see clearly now, and she looked at it for a length of time that had no measure to it, in a silence so complete that the frost stopped ticking against the frozen water.
And then she put it on her finger.
BOOM!
Her two golden halos EXPANDED!

They swelled outward from her face and multiplied, ring after ring after ring blooming into existence around her head, growing and layering and overlapping until her entire visage was surrounded and buried behind them, circle upon circle of turning golden metal that hid her completely.
She... did not want a single one of her emotions to be seen!
Noah understood that immediately.
And in the place where the ring had been, in the empty air where it had spun before he ever touched it, Noah alone saw a faint golden brilliance still hanging there.
A residue. A remainder. Something left behind that only his eyes could find!
And out of it, into his mind, came a laugh!
|Haha! You actually gave it away?|
Atlas!
|You dumbass, I would have actually let you keep it!|
Noah’s eye twitched!
|Haha! But no. It was not something you made. So giving it away was the right choice, and you would not have liked what you became if you had kept it.|
|That was one of my finest creations. A Gu Elsedimension Ring.|

|But I will help you make your OWN, so that you remain true to yourself. Our Provenances are grand, and yet we still cannot do things alone. I will make sure you learn to become a grand Engineer in your own right.|
|Understand what I am, before you get any ideas. I am here and not really here. I am a cluster of records and probability. I do not have my own cognizance.|
|For now, say goodbye to the one who loved the wrong person. Being near an Immense One for too long will alert him.|
|I learned that the hard way.|
Noah’s eyes pulsed.

He looked up through the frozen steam at THE REMINISCING WIDOW, at the layered halos hiding her entirely, at the hand that had lowered from them and was now turning the golden ring slowly on her finger, stroking it with a thumb, over and over, in the manner of someone who had done this exact motion in her mind ten thousand times without anything actually being there.
And Noah spoke, and his voice was heavy.
"You need to go."
The stroking did not stop!

"I did what you wanted. I even reunited you with his weavings, and you may be hearing his voice even now."He held his ground in the frozen water with Thalia motionless behind him. "Your presence here alone is a danger to me. So you... need to go."
The halos turned!
|Yet another person I warned.|
|And who did not listen.|
The frost held its silence around them, and when her words came again it was slower, and it carried a weight of melancholy that had nothing performative in it at all!
|You all... I truly do not know what to say to you all anymore.|

|Do whatever you want. Build whatever you wish to build. Climb whatever you have decided to climb. And when death inevitably comes for you, and it will come, you will remember me. You will remember this evening, and this spring, and every word I said to you.|
|They always do.|
|For doing what you have done for me today, I owe you a favor.|
|You know how you can reach me.|
And with those words, THE REMINISCING WIDOW departed!

Her visage folded downward through the frozen air, the layered halos collapsing inward one by one, her draped form flowing back down toward the obsidian journal lying open at the spring’s edge, and she sank into the page she had risen from as the ink drank her back into itself!
The eye on the page closed.
And everything came back!

Warmth crashed across the Elsedimension as the frost broke apart into vapor and the ice sheeting the spring’s surface shattered into golden water, the steam rolling again, the falls resuming their long descent down the Elsemountain, the entire region returning to what it had been before an architect had decided to visit.
And Thalia unfroze.
She came out of it moving, crossing the water in an instant, and she threw her arms around Noah from behind and locked them across his chest and held on.
Noah’s hands came up and closed over hers.

He breathed out, long and slow, and let his head tilt back, and stood there in the scorching golden water with her arms around him, because he had just walked out of a catastrophe that should have ended every point of his existence across all of time, and he had walked out of it with a favor owed!
And in his mind...
|Has she left?|
Atlas!
|If she has, we can proceed ahead. Find a place where you can privately work.|

|Because I was a genius, and I always found everyone else to be imbeciles. Even Immense Ones. I do not know how much work it will take to teach you to be even a percentage of the engineer that I was.|
|Ah, to be a genius like me.|
Noah’s eye twitched again!
|Get going, O Provenance of Existence. O Chance of Chances. O Author of Probability.|
|Let us see if you will better fit all those titles, because even I could not fully live up to them. But maybe what I could not do, you may manage to do.|
|Let us see.|
|Send your Provenance onto the residual Elsedimension Ring when you are ready to get started, and we will begin.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5699: Engineer! II
paragraphs: Thalia unflinchingly...did not let him go.

The spring had returned to what it was, and the steam had come back, and the falls were running down the Elsemountain again as though nothing at all had happened here. Yet her arms stayed locked across his chest, tight, as if he would be gone if she let go.

Of course, she had reason. She had spent that entire conversation frozen, watching an architect stand over the man she had crossed time to reach, unable to move so much as a finger in his direction. There are worse things than danger. Being present for it and useless is one of them.
"That was... an Immense One," she said against his back. "How did they even..."
The question did not finish. In truth, it did not need to!
Then she asked the other one.
"And you. My Provenance, are you really fearful all the time? Do you truly live with fear constantly?"
Noah turned in her arms.
He took her by the shoulders and drew her in, and their noses brushed.
"Yes," he said. "Constantly."
Her eyes moved between his.

"For humans like us, fear was never the enemy. Fear is the oldest teacher our kind ever had. It is the thing that told the first of us to look up at a sky we did not understand and ask what lived in it. It is what built every wall and lit every fire and made a person check the dark before they slept, and every one of those was a small refusal to simply lie down and accept whatever came."
He held her gaze.

"Fear is a drive that makes sure a man does not remain still. It sharpens what love makes soft. It keeps me honest about what I actually am rather than what I would like to be. I thought I gave away my everything of fear and doubt before, but...it was always there."
He shrugged, and the shrug was small.
"Being afraid and moving anyway is what a true human has always been good at."
Thalia looked at him for a long moment.

Then the tears came, and she did not wipe them away or apologize for them or seem to notice them at all. She simply took his face in both hands and started kissing him, small pecks, everywhere, his cheek and his brow and the bridge of his nose and the corner of his mouth, over and over, as though she could cover every part of him that carried something heavy.
"Let me carry some of your fear,"she said between them. "Some of your weight."
Another kiss, at his temple.
"In that possible future, I know you carry so much weight. I have seen what it makes of you. Let me carry even a percentage of it for you."
Noah stayed in the moment.

He was not, generally speaking, a man who stayed in moments. Yet here he was, standing in scorching golden water with an unfathomable woman holding his face in her hands, and he did nothing at all except look at her.
Then he shook his head.

"In existence, a man has his duties,"he said."I know you can carry any weight you want to carry. But my job is to bear everything, so that you and many others can live happily without needing to bend your backs."
He brushed a thumb under her eye and took the tear away.
"Do not worry about any weight I carry. I can handle it. I have a grand Provenance, and I have infinite musing to allow me to do so.For me, it is normal."
Thalia looked at him.
And whatever she had been holding back since she came out of that pool, since the frozen instant, since the future she would not describe, she stopped holding it back.
Her clothing fell away, and the mist of the spring rose and covered her, and she pushed him down into the golden water.
Then the light came.

Golden brilliance flooded the whole of the spring, filling the basin and rising up the walls of this region of the Elsedimension until the steam itself burned gold. Nothing at all could be seen through it!
And nothing at all was seen.
<Aurelius Vasiliou>
Far from that spring, at the top of a golden tower that had stood since before the current arrangement of things, two Provenance Lifeforms watched their people move.

Vasileia Elsecity, among other names it had, spread out beneath them in tiers of pale stone and hanging light. Dozens of the lineage moved through it at this hour, going about the small business that even the grandest existences cannot escape.
Aurelius Vasiliou looked down at all of it with his hands behind his back.
Beside him, Rosalia Vasiliou watched the Provenance Lifeforms below.
"Is this really the right choice?" she asked. "For us to go to war against an Immense One?"

Compared to most questions asked in that tower, it was a simple one. She was not arguing. She had come to the same conclusions he had, most likely before he had, since she usually did. She was asking her husband to say it out loud so that she could hear how it sounded in the open air.
Aurelius took his time.

"Maybe our Provenance shines brighter in the end for it,"he said. "I have thought about this more than I have thought about anything in my life, and I keep arriving at the same place. For years I woke with the same picture in my head. My daughter, promised away, handed up to a thing that would use her for whatever it needed and then set her down somewhere quiet when the use ran out. That was the safe road. That was the road where our lineage endured and our name stayed on the lists and nobody came for our Elsedimension. I would have walked it. I was walking it. And every year of it made me smaller."

"Then an existence appears who generates his own Provenance out of nothing anybody gave him, who stands a chance at anything touching Atlas. And I find that I would rather take that bet. Not because the odds are good. Because a bet at least has a second outcome."
Rosalia was quiet for a while.
"And him?" she said. "This Human Dreamer. This Osmont. You had your talk with him."
"It seems like he may treat our daughter well."Aurelius made a sound that was almost a laugh, which was rare enough that his wife turned her head.
"She is stronger than him at present, by a considerable margin. So at the very least, she will keep him in line."
Below them, complex weavings of Provenance Lifeforms unfolded.

The two Provenance Lifeforms stood above their city and talked about their daughter, and about the war that was coming, and about whether the choice they had made would be judged kindly by whatever came after them.
And neither of them had any idea that the power of an Immense One had flared in a certain spring not too long ago.
Well, and what was happening there now after an ordeal was passed!

sentences.text: Thalia unflinchingly...did not let him go.
The spring had returned to what it was, and the steam had come back, and the falls were running down the Elsemountain again as though nothing at all had happened here.
Yet her arms stayed locked across his chest, tight, as if he would be gone if she let go.
Of course, she had reason.
She had spent that entire conversation frozen, watching an architect stand over the man she had crossed time to reach, unable to move so much as a finger in his direction.
There are worse things than danger.
Being present for it and useless is one of them.
"That was... an Immense One," she said against his back.
"How did they even..."
The question did not finish.
In truth, it did not need to!
Then she asked the other one.
"And you.
My Provenance, are you really fearful all the time?
Do you truly live with fear constantly?"
Noah turned in her arms.
He took her by the shoulders and drew her in, and their noses brushed.
"Yes," he said.
"Constantly."
Her eyes moved between his.
"For humans like us, fear was never the enemy.
Fear is the oldest teacher our kind ever had.
It is the thing that told the first of us to look up at a sky we did not understand and ask what lived in it.
It is what built every wall and lit every fire and made a person check the dark before they slept, and every one of those was a small refusal to simply lie down and accept whatever came."
He held her gaze.
"Fear is a drive that makes sure a man does not remain still.
It sharpens what love makes soft.
It keeps me honest about what I actually am rather than what I would like to be.
I thought I gave away my everything of fear and doubt before, but...it was always there."
He shrugged, and the shrug was small.
"Being afraid and moving anyway is what a true human has always been good at."
Thalia looked at him for a long moment.
Then the tears came, and she did not wipe them away or apologize for them or seem to notice them at all.

She simply took his face in both hands and started kissing him, small pecks, everywhere, his cheek and his brow and the bridge of his nose and the corner of his mouth, over and over, as though she could cover every part of him that carried something heavy.
"Let me carry some of your fear,"she said between them.
"Some of your weight."
Another kiss, at his temple.
"In that possible future, I know you carry so much weight.
I have seen what it makes of you.
Let me carry even a percentage of it for you."
Noah stayed in the moment.
He was not, generally speaking, a man who stayed in moments.
Yet here he was, standing in scorching golden water with an unfathomable woman holding his face in her hands, and he did nothing at all except look at her.
Then he shook his head.
"In existence, a man has his duties,"he said."I know you can carry any weight you want to carry.
But my job is to bear everything, so that you and many others can live happily without needing to bend your backs."
He brushed a thumb under her eye and took the tear away.
"Do not worry about any weight I carry.
I can handle it.
I have a grand Provenance, and I have infinite musing to allow me to do so.For me, it is normal."
Thalia looked at him.
And whatever she had been holding back since she came out of that pool, since the frozen instant, since the future she would not describe, she stopped holding it back.
Her clothing fell away, and the mist of the spring rose and covered her, and she pushed him down into the golden water.
Then the light came.
Golden brilliance flooded the whole of the spring, filling the basin and rising up the walls of this region of the Elsedimension until the steam itself burned gold.
Nothing at all could be seen through it!
And nothing at all was seen.
<Aurelius Vasiliou>
Far from that spring, at the top of a golden tower that had stood since before the current arrangement of things, two Provenance Lifeforms watched their people move.
Vasileia Elsecity, among other names it had, spread out beneath them in tiers of pale stone and hanging light.
Dozens of the lineage moved through it at this hour, going about the small business that even the grandest existences cannot escape.
Aurelius Vasiliou looked down at all of it with his hands behind his back.
Beside him, Rosalia Vasiliou watched the Provenance Lifeforms below.
"Is this really the right choice?" she asked.
"For us to go to war against an Immense One?"
Compared to most questions asked in that tower, it was a simple one.
She was not arguing.
She had come to the same conclusions he had, most likely before he had, since she usually did.
She was asking her husband to say it out loud so that she could hear how it sounded in the open air.
Aurelius took his time.
"Maybe our Provenance shines brighter in the end for it,"he said.
"I have thought about this more than I have thought about anything in my life, and I keep arriving at the same place.
For years I woke with the same picture in my head.
My daughter, promised away, handed up to a thing that would use her for whatever it needed and then set her down somewhere quiet when the use ran out.
That was the safe road.
That was the road where our lineage endured and our name stayed on the lists and nobody came for our Elsedimension.
I would have walked it.
I was walking it.
And every year of it made me smaller."
"Then an existence appears who generates his own Provenance out of nothing anybody gave him, who stands a chance at anything touching Atlas.
And I find that I would rather take that bet.
Not because the odds are good.
Because a bet at least has a second outcome."
Rosalia was quiet for a while.
"And him?" she said.
"This Human Dreamer.
This Osmont.
You had your talk with him."
"It seems like he may treat our daughter well."Aurelius made a sound that was almost a laugh, which was rare enough that his wife turned her head.
"She is stronger than him at present, by a considerable margin.
So at the very least, she will keep him in line."
Below them, complex weavings of Provenance Lifeforms unfolded.

The two Provenance Lifeforms stood above their city and talked about their daughter, and about the war that was coming, and about whether the choice they had made would be judged kindly by whatever came after them.
And neither of them had any idea that the power of an Immense One had flared in a certain spring not too long ago.
Well, and what was happening there now after an ordeal was passed!

chapters.title: Chapter 5700: Engineer! III
paragraphs: His Provenance Realm had changed again, as it always did when he did.

Above the blue-gold hills, where there had once been a single unmoving star, there now hung a field of them. Radiant sun-singularities, one for every Provenance Essence he carried, burning steady in a sky that had no weather and asked for none. Anyone counting them would have arrived at the same number he did.
Eighty-nine!
Of course, that number had been eighty-six not so long ago. Standing in front of an architect and surviving the standing had apparently been worth three.
|VERITAS: 89|
|PROVENANCE: 89|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 88|
Ninety was close now!

Noah sat on the bank of the river of light where it ran fastest, in the shape his Provenance had settled into. Bare feet in the star-pooled shallows. Pure dark hair. Skin without a single mark on it, which was somewhat funny given the amount of it that had been removed recently.
His eyes were obsidian singularities in one second and endlessly blue in another, and they were currently pointed at his own right hand.
There was a ring on it that was not there.
Illusory, faint, gold, visible to nobody else in existence and barely visible to him. The residue of something a genius had left behind!
In truth, since another of his bodies was currently occupied with the considerable pleasures of being human in the Vasiliou Elseworld, he would have this body begin thr work.
So he sent his Provenance Essence into the ring.
He was ready to get started.
|Alright.|
The voice boomed out over the Realm, coming from the ring and from the air and from a little behind his own ears at once.

|It seems you are ready to get started, which means this will actually be an experiment for the both of us. I am not here. I am not even a little bit here. This is something unique of mine doing the talking.|
|I am like a record. Except considerably better than a record, because a genius designed it, and I can do a great many things a record cannot.|

|You can ask questions. Do so rarely. Questions interrupt my flow, and answering them will draw on your energy and your authority in ways you will feel. So any question you have for me will cost you. Price it before you open your mouth, and if that offends you, take it up with the man who is dead.|
|Most of what I carry stays locked until I have given you the basics and the introductions. So.|
|Welcome to Existential Engineering 101.|
The illusory ring pulsed.

Golden light spilled out of it and unfolded into the air above the river, and it wrote itself, in an ancient tongue that Noah found he could read without the smallest effort, as though the words had been waiting for eras for eyes that would bother.
EXISTENTIAL ENGINEERING: BASICS
Noah looked at it with shining eyes.
And the voice continued.

|Now. When it comes to engineering, and all the crazy things around dimensional authority and existential narrative and truly terrifying levels of Dimensionality, I did what any reasonable person would do. I simplified all of it into an art.|

|I broke it down into the basic building blocks of existence, and I made those my engineering. Every design I ever made came from using the components of existence itself as ingredients for the immensity I built.|

|And there are many, many ingredients. I will have to teach you how to isolate parts of existence, timelines, parallel weavings, all of it, into clean separated ingredients you can actually construct with. That goes in our course on time and temporal mechanics, which you are not remotely ready for.|
|So let us start at the beginning. There is engineering, and there is alchemy. Sometimes they go hand in hand.|
Diagrams began to appear.
They unfolded out of the golden light one after another, hanging over the running river, drawn in that same old script with lines connecting the parts of them.
A vessel with something suspended inside it. A lattice with nine points. A shape Noah could not name at all, which annoyed him considerably.
|When a lower lifeform considers alchemy, it imagines boiling water and crushed herbs. When it considers engineering, it imagines metal struck against an anvil.|
|Compared to the truth, those are the playthings of children who have not yet worked out that they are living inside a locked room.|
|In fact, at their core, neither art is about the manipulation of physical matter at all. Both are the manipulation of absolute laws.|

|So ask yourself. What is an Aspect of Existence? Is it a thing you express, or is it a fundamental building block? If an Immense One can harvest the unspent Causes of a bloodline to mortar their pristine thrones, does that not make a Cause a brick?|
The lattice diagram brightened, and a single point on it detached and hung by itself, and the light around it wrote the word for brick.
Noah’s eyes did not leave it.
|Naturally, to use these bricks, one must understand conceptual extraction.|

|Alchemy is the act of boiling down a timeline that was violently aborted, skimming the grief off the top, and distilling the raw potential into a liquid truth. You take an abstract concept, the weight of a dying Primeval, the suppressed ambition of a harvested lineage, and you force it into a consumable state.|
|Thus, you are not brewing potions. You are drinking isolated existence.|
The vessel diagram filled slowly with something that had no color the Realm could render.

|By comparison, engineering is the framework that cages the extracted truth. Once you have distilled an aspect of existence, where do you put it? You weld it. You take the extracted Cause, or the extracted Provenance, and you carve pathways of narrative into it until it holds a shape and does work.|
|Since Aspects of Existence are merely ingredients, anything can be built.|
|A lesser smith builds a sword. A sovereign engineer builds a new timeline.|

|Become proficient enough at engineering existence itself, and you can construct mechanisms grand enough to mimic the Immense Ones. Engines that generate their own localized Scales. Their own rulings. Structures that bypass the architects entirely, since the architects only own the board so long as nobody else learns to make boards.|
|Perhaps you will even find, one day, that the foundational blueprints of Existence itself are recorded inside a grand conceptual structure somewhere.|
The light hung on that sentence a moment longer than it had hung on any other, and then moved on without explaining itself.
|In truth, existence is not sacred. It is simply waiting to be melted down.|
|But we are getting ahead of ourselves.|

|One of the more basic places to start is with an ingredient that happens to be the most stable one I ever found in nature, and I found that out through a great deal of trial and a considerable amount of tribulation.|
|That ingredient is a Cause.|
The nine-point lattice turned slowly above the river.

|Being able to harvest and isolate Causes as an ingredient is going to be basic work for you. And one of the better ways to harvest them is not from Observable Existences or Dimensions that are built out of those Causes, because the moment you take them away, the structure goes unstable and you will have made a mess for no reason.|

|Lifeforms are better. Unique ones. The kind capable of generating their own Causes are some of the best subjects you will ever find for this, and you will not necessarily be stripping the Cause away from them. You isolate the essence of the Cause, which they regenerate over time on their own.|

|We will start with Causes, and we will expand from there. Because when it comes to authorities, all of them distill. Provenance included. Everything can be reduced to its own unique ingredient, given enough patience and a sufficiently unpleasant amount of failure.|
|So let us start with something simple that requires Causes as an ingredient|
|Let us have you design your own Elsedimension.|
BOOM!
Simple?
That was something SIMPLE?
Noah sat very still on the bank of his own river, in his own Realm, with his eyes blazing!
|Now.|
|An Elsedimension is actually fairly simple. It has only a few main ingredients, and we will take them one at a time.|
|Let us start with the most basic. Distilled Cause Essence.|

|You need to extract and crystallize the essence of at least nine Causes into Distilled Cause Essence. Depending on your Provenance, this will be either easy or extremely difficult, and I genuinely cannot tell you which, because nobody has ever tried this with whatever it is you are.|
|Find something to extract it from. An Observable Existence will do. A Lifeform will do better.|
|And if you are using an Observable Existence, please empty it of all life first, so that you do not go around causing unnecessary genocides.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5701: Engineer! IV
paragraphs: He started with something he had made himself, which seemed only fair.

Noah reached into THE Infiniverse and pulled out a young Observable Existence, one of the thousands that had bloomed out of the Genesis Tesseracts and had been growing quietly ever since. It came into the Realm and hung over the river of light, turning slowly, no larger than a fruit at this scale and containing an interior he could have walked for an age without finishing.
Of course, there were no lifeforms in it. Not one!
He looked at it for a moment anyway.
Then he dreamed.

That was the only word for what THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer actually did here. His eyes lowered halfway and did not close, and the light around him went soft at the edges. The river kept running. The eighty-nine suns kept burning. And Noah sat on the bank of his own Realm and dreamed the young Observable Existence apart.
In the dream, its Causes were visible.

Nine of them, which was simply what an Observable Existence grows on its own if you leave it alone, wound through the structure of the thing like the veins in a leaf held up to a light. He did not cut them. He did not pull. In the dream he simply understood that the essence of each Cause was a separate thing from the Cause itself, the way the taste of a fruit is separate from the fruit, and having understood it, it was already true.
The first essence came away.
It rose out of the turning Existence as a thread of pale color that had no name, and it hung in the air over the river.
Then the second. Then the third and fourth together, since he had the shape of it now.
By the seventh he was no longer being careful, and by the ninth the threads had begun to find each other on their own, winding together over the water. They combined!
What was left was a liquid.

It swirled in the air, unhurried, holding nine colors that all belonged to it, and it moved slower than liquid should. Noah rose from the bank and drew a bottle out of nothing, glass and stoppered, and let the thing pour itself in.
|DISTILLED CAUSE ESSENCE|
|The isolated conceptual essence of nine naturally-arisen Causes, rendered into a stable liquid state.|
|Classification: base ingredient, foundational tier. Stability: the highest observed in nature.|
|Retains the function of a Cause without retaining the Cause. Existence does not recognize the loss.|
And above the river, the Observable Existence he had drawn it from finished changing.

It had been turning with a slow inner light. That light was gone now. It kept its shape, all of it, every domain and cosmos and world inside it exactly where it had been, and none of it was going anywhere ever again. A thing that could hold, but could no longer become.
|TERMINAL OBSERVABLE EXISTENCE|
|Structure intact. Causal generation ceased. No further growth will occur.|
In truth, Noah felt bad about that more than he had expected to!
Fortunately, it was fixable. He could resuscitate it himself with enough attention. Better still, he did not have to.

He waved a hand, and the dead thing lifted and went, crossing out of the Realm toward a distant domain where a certain manifestation was currently overseeing thousands of infant Existences. THE Infiniverse would resuscitate it!
Although as the terminal Existence dwindled out of sight, Noah found his thoughts wandering.
Causes as ingredients. Nine from an Observable Existence.

Compare that to what Atlas had actually recommended, which was Lifeforms, and specifically the ones capable of generating their own. Take the essence, leave the Cause, walk away. They regrow it. Nobody dies. Nobody even limps.
That was harvesting.
And Noah knew exactly where the richest fields were, which was the part he did not like.

The Laestrygonians would soon be reborn inside THE Infiniverse and birthing Causes natively, a whole restored people producing the most stable ingredient in existence simply by living. Hvitrmarr, with nine First Causes seated in her organs, transformed and hers now. The Steeds, bred as burden-bearers for exactly this reason by beings who had looked at living things and seen carrying capacity.
Was this the reason for THE SLEEPLESS FIEND’s fixation with causes and lifeforms that inherently held them?
Noah shook his head and refocused.
Then he spoke into the ring for the first time.
"I have successfully extracted Causes into Distilled Cause Essence."

The moment the words left him, he felt his Provenance being drawn on. A decimal of a percent, sapped away slow and steady, small enough to be nothing and precise enough that he knew exactly what he had spent.
The ring buzzed on his finger.
|That was rather quick.|
|You did not cause a genocide, did you? Do not go down that route. Everyone who goes down that route tells themselves it was efficient, and every one of them was wrong.|
|But if you did it that fast, it means your Provenance is very suitable for this.|
|Because some would start whining at this point. Sir, how exactly do I extract the Causes into Distilled Cause Essence? That would have been a dumb question.|
|You did not ask. Which means you most likely told your Provenance, here are the Causes, extract their essence for me. And your Provenance did it.|
|So sometimes the right Provenance does it all. Remember that when you are tempted to be proud of yourself.|
Noah’s mouth twitched.
|Alright. The other ingredients of an Elsedimension.|
|First, your own Provenance. It serves as the basis and the core, and it is what actually makes the thing YOURS rather than a room you happen to be standing in.|
|Second, an extremely high concentration of hydrogen. Helium. Lithium. Beryllium. Boron. Europium. Strontium. Neodymium.|
Noah blinked.
|And you might ask yourself, what the fuck do these elemental particles have to do with anything.|

|Well. When I began engineering existence itself, I looked at the makeup of stellar bodies, and I told myself that the ingredients had to be things that were easily accessible, so that whoever came after me would have boundless possibility rather than a shopping list they could never fill.|
|Do not make things overly complex. Complexity is what people reach for when they have not understood a thing well enough to make it simple.|
|Wonder has to bloom out of the most common things. The most ordinary things, made grand.|
Noah’s eyes shone at that!
He tugged upward with two fingers.
Another Observable Existence floated down out of THE Infiniverse and settled over the river.

Inside it were countless domains, and inside those, cosmos beyond counting, universes and their worlds and stars beyond that, and every one of those stars was made largely out of exactly what Atlas had listed.
The commonest things there were.
He waved a hand, and they came out.

Stellar rivers poured from the young Existence into the air above his Realm, eight of them, braided and enormous, hydrogen and helium running silver-white at the front, lithium and beryllium and boron threading through them, europium and strontium and neodymium arriving last in colors that had no business being that beautiful!
They came out at concentrations that would have collapsed a star and left the Existence itself entirely unharmed, since he was not taking its structure, only its abundance.
The rivers turned slowly over the bank, waiting.
Noah sent his Provenance into the ring.
|Good. Now listen, because the assembly matters more than the ingredients.|
|You will begin with the Elseengine. That is the core, and everything else is built outward from it, and if you get the core wrong you will not find out until the whole thing comes apart around you.|

|Take your Provenance and the Distilled Cause Essence, and fuse them. Not layered. Not adjacent. The Essence provides function that existence recognizes as legitimate, and your Provenance provides the authority that answers to nobody. Together they will hold a law up without borrowing a single thing from anyone. That is an Elseengine.|
|Then weave the elements around it. All eight, in the order I gave them, because the order is the order for reasons you will understand in about a hundred years maybe.|
|And here is the part that matters most, so hear it properly.|
|You will include nothing else.|

|No Argent Loom. No Infinity. No Primordial Source. No Narrative. Not a thread of any framework’s Dimensionality, not one borrowed weaving, no matter how convenient it would be and it will be extremely convenient.|

|Because whatever authority you build INTO a place has standing INSIDE that place forever. Include the Loom, and the Loom may enter. Include Infinity, and everything that has ever mastered Infinity has a door. By excluding them at the foundation, you are not hiding from those authorities. |What you get is a domain bent uniquely to your Provenance, running your rules, sitting outside the scope of the weavings that every powerful lifeform in existence has spent their entire lives climbing.|
|An Elsedimension is like a second body of your own.|
|And nobody has greater autonomy over your body than you.|

He took the bottle in his left hand and unstoppered it, and he brought his Provenance up out of the depth of himself, and he put them together over the river of light.

The Distilled Cause Essence did not pour. It reached. Nine colors that had grown inside a young Existence found the blue-gold weight of something that had generated itself out of nothing, and there was a moment where nothing at all happened!
Then they fused!
HUUM!

The Elseengine came into being over the water, small and turning and impossibly heavy, throwing a light that did not resemble any authority in existence because it was not borrowing from any of them. Noah felt it take hold. He felt it hold a law up on its own, needing nothing, asking nothing, owed to nobody.
He brought the rivers in.
Hydrogen first, and it wrapped the engine and thinned into a shell.
Helium after it, settling into the gaps. Lithium, beryllium, boron in sequence, and with each one the shell stopped being a shell and started being a place, gaining depth!
Europium came in and the light inside changed character entirely. Strontium threaded the edges. Neodymium last, and when it landed, the whole construction went quiet.
Then it BLOOMED.

An Elsedimension unfolded over the river of light in Noah’s Realm, and it shone, and it shone like a budding flower! Not brighter than his eighty-nine suns. Differently. It cast a light that owed no one anything.
Noah spread his hands, and it grew.

|Included authorities: none. THE Argent Loom holds no standing here. THE Provenance of Existence holds no standing here. No framework of Dimensionality has been granted entry.|
|First act of Existential Engineering completed without instruction failure. The work was understood, not copied.|
|VERITAS: 90|
|PROVENANCE: 90|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 89|
Ninety!
|Did it work?|
The ring buzzed.

|If it did, your existence should be feeling the pleasure of advancement right about now. That feeling is real and it is not vanity. Engineering alone can make you understand the secrets of Existence and elevate your Dimensionality, because you cannot build a thing without learning what it is made of, and everything is made of the same handful of things.|
|Making an Elsedimension is the first step.|
|Our goal is to make you your own Gu Elsedimension Ring, since you gave the last one away.|
|Haha. I still cannot believe you gave it away. If you had any idea how hard that thing was to make and how prized it is.|
|But hey, forget about it. We will take things a step at a time. Do not worry.|
|For now, you have the capability to make an Elsedimension. So the next step is naturally Gu.|
|And for that, you need to make a trip to a place lost through existence and time. Somewhere most Immense Ones do not even know is there as others of their kind keep it a secret.|
|THE CHRYSALIS OF THE FIRST SUNDERING.|
|Knowing about it is one thing.|
|Getting there. Now that is the fun part.|

Noah reached into THE Infiniverse and pulled out a young Observable Existence, one of the thousands that had bloomed out of the Genesis Tesseracts and had been growing quietly ever since.
It came into the Realm and hung over the river of light, turning slowly, no larger than a fruit at this scale and containing an interior he could have walked for an age without finishing.
Of course, there were no lifeforms in it.
Not one!
He looked at it for a moment anyway.
Then he dreamed.
That was the only word for what THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer actually did here.
His eyes lowered halfway and did not close, and the light around him went soft at the edges.
The river kept running.
The eighty-nine suns kept burning.
And Noah sat on the bank of his own Realm and dreamed the young Observable Existence apart.
In the dream, its Causes were visible.
Nine of them, which was simply what an Observable Existence grows on its own if you leave it alone, wound through the structure of the thing like the veins in a leaf held up to a light.
He did not cut them.
He did not pull.

In the dream he simply understood that the essence of each Cause was a separate thing from the Cause itself, the way the taste of a fruit is separate from the fruit, and having understood it, it was already true.
The first essence came away.
It rose out of the turning Existence as a thread of pale color that had no name, and it hung in the air over the river.
Then the second.
Then the third and fourth together, since he had the shape of it now.
By the seventh he was no longer being careful, and by the ninth the threads had begun to find each other on their own, winding together over the water.
They combined!
What was left was a liquid.
It swirled in the air, unhurried, holding nine colors that all belonged to it, and it moved slower than liquid should.
Noah rose from the bank and drew a bottle out of nothing, glass and stoppered, and let the thing pour itself in.

|Retains the function of a Cause without retaining the Cause.

And above the river, the Observable Existence he had drawn it from finished changing.
It had been turning with a slow inner light.
That light was gone now.
It kept its shape, all of it, every domain and cosmos and world inside it exactly where it had been, and none of it was going anywhere ever again.
A thing that could hold, but could no longer become.

|Structure intact.
Causal generation ceased.
No further growth will occur.|
In truth, Noah felt bad about that more than he had expected to!
Fortunately, it was fixable.
He could resuscitate it himself with enough attention.
Better still, he did not have to.
He waved a hand, and the dead thing lifted and went, crossing out of the Realm toward a distant domain where a certain manifestation was currently overseeing thousands of infant Existences.
THE Infiniverse would resuscitate it!
Although as the terminal Existence dwindled out of sight, Noah found his thoughts wandering.
Causes as ingredients.
Nine from an Observable Existence.
Compare that to what Atlas had actually recommended, which was Lifeforms, and specifically the ones capable of generating their own.
Take the essence, leave the Cause, walk away.
They regrow it.
Nobody dies.
Nobody even limps.
That was harvesting.
And Noah knew exactly where the richest fields were, which was the part he did not like.
The Laestrygonians would soon be reborn inside THE Infiniverse and birthing Causes natively, a whole restored people producing the most stable ingredient in existence simply by living.
Hvitrmarr, with nine First Causes seated in her organs, transformed and hers now.
The Steeds, bred as burden-bearers for exactly this reason by beings who had looked at living things and seen carrying capacity.
Was this the reason for THE SLEEPLESS FIEND’s fixation with causes and lifeforms that inherently held them?
Noah shook his head and refocused.
Then he spoke into the ring for the first time.
"I have successfully extracted Causes into Distilled Cause Essence."
The moment the words left him, he felt his Provenance being drawn on.
A decimal of a percent, sapped away slow and steady, small enough to be nothing and precise enough that he knew exactly what he had spent.
The ring buzzed on his finger.

|You did not cause a genocide, did you?
Do not go down that route.
Everyone who goes down that route tells themselves it was efficient, and every one of them was wrong.|
|But if you did it that fast, it means your Provenance is very suitable for this.|

That would have been a dumb question.|

Which means you most likely told your Provenance, here are the Causes, extract their essence for me.
And your Provenance did it.|

Remember that when you are tempted to be proud of yourself.|

|First, your own Provenance.
It serves as the basis and the core, and it is what actually makes the thing YOURS rather than a room you happen to be standing in.|

Helium.
Lithium.
Beryllium.
Boron.
Europium.
Strontium.
Neodymium.|
