chapters.title: Chapter 5702: Peace and Blood! I
paragraphs: <THE Continuum Paradox>
They were crossing through THE Dimensional Provenance Train.
They were, but...
The pull took them mid-sentence, and existence answered before their feet had even found ground.
|THREE PARTICIPANTS HAVE BEEN PULLED ACROSS THE DIMENSIONAL PROVENANCE TRAIN.|
|You are arriving within a Narrative of Existence in progress.|
|Records note: this Narrative has failed to entertain. The combatants within it met no hardship worth recording. Victory arrived without cost, without struggle, and without a single moment of doubt.|
|The reigning champions of this Cabin hold a Narrative of devouring and usurpation. It has consumed everything placed before it, and it has done so far too easily.|
|Should the arriving participants attain victory and BREAK this Narrative of Existence, additional rewards shall be given.|
Three frowns landed at once!

Descartes, THE Continuum Paradox, took the information as it came and did not move a muscle of his face beyond the frown itself. Beside him THE Primordial Paradox rolled his shoulders and made a sound of open disgust at being moved without being asked. And Erwin, THE Living Paradox, simply tilted his head.
Then they looked around!

They stood in a Dimension made of gaseous stellar matter and debris. Vast clouds of it hung in every direction, greens and rusts and deep violets rolling slow through each other, and through the clouds drifted rock, mountains of it, continents of it, tumbling without hurry through a space that had no floor and no sky and no end that any of them could find.

Auras saturated all of it. Thousands of them. Descendants and Primeval Ones, the weight of their existences pressing against the stellar clouds from every direction at once, enough gathered power to level Dimensions stacked one atop another out to the horizon.
And it was silent.
Not quiet. SILENT! Not one voice, not one breath, not one scrape of movement across all that floating stone. Thousands of the mighty occupied this place and produced no sound whatsoever.
Above everything, an eye watched.

It hung in the upper dark past the clouds, enormous and patient, and it was not looking at the Dimension. It was looking at THEM, with the settled anticipation of something that had cleared its schedule.
Erwin looked up at it and smiled pleasantly.
The eye did not react!
Compared to what came next, none of that was the strange part.

Because as the three of them turned to survey the floating stone, they found the mighty of this place seated and standing across all of it. Descendants on the tumbling rock, robed and horned and marked. Primeval Ones sprawled across whole asteroids, ancient and enormous and still. Some sat cross-legged. Some stood at edges looking out at nothing. Thousands of them, scattered through the debris in every direction.
And when the three arrived, all of them turned at the same time.
Every single one!

Thousands of heads swung toward the arrival point in the same instant with the same speed, thousands of faces angling to the same degree, and thousands of pairs of eyes settled on them glazed over with an obsidian purple sheen!
THE Primordial Paradox blinked.
Erwin blinked beside him.
"Well," Erwin said mildly. "That is...familiar."
They looked further in, toward the center of the Dimension, where the debris thickened around a single massive floating asteroid that everything else seemed to orbit.
Two figures sat upon it.

The first was a man in white robes, and by every ordinary measure he was fairly average. Average build. Average height. A plain face that would not have earned a second glance in a crowded market. Nothing about him screamed anything at all.
Except for the circle on his chest!

It was divided into nine sections, a nine-pointed star outlined across his breast, and set into the edges of it were gems. Nine of them, radiant, each one a different color and every color impossible, and each single gem radiated the profound aura of a pristine First Cause.
Nine First Causes! On one man’s chest! Blazing around the edges of an Enneagram like ornaments he had picked out that morning!
And his eyes were clear.

That was the thing THE Continuum Paradox marked immediately, since it was the only thing in the entire Dimension that did not fit. Not one thread of that obsidian purple unity ran through this one’s gaze. He was himself, entirely, and he was looking directly at Erwin with a coldness that had nothing polite in it whatsoever.
He was looking at THE Living Paradox the way a man looks at someone he has already decided to fight.
But the thing that seized the attention of the two Paradoxes was not the man with nine First Causes on his chest!
It was the being sitting beside him.

A stellar titan, humanoid, so vast that the asteroid served him as a stool. His entire body shone with an obsidian allure, a dark that gave back light instead of drinking it, and across every inch of that enormous frame ran boundless weavings of chaos, churning and folding and unmaking themselves without pause. He sat with one arm across a raised knee, and he wore an expression of profound and ancient boredom.
And both Paradoxes knew that face!
"Abbadon?"
THE Primordial Paradox said it out loud, and incredulity carried the word across the whole silent Dimension!
"Why do your eyes seem their depressed and ancient selves? Your entire mind was taken over, as far as I knew! Which also seems to be the case for every single one of these..."
He gestured, and the gesture took in thousands of purple-glazed faces still turned toward them in perfect unison.
In the distance, Abbadon harrumphed.

THE Primordial Chaos shifted his enormous frame, and the chaos-weavings across his body churned faster with the motion, and when he spoke his voice rolled through the stellar clouds without disturbing a single one of them.
"I worked out a deal to move with my own autonomy."
He looked the three of them over without much enthusiasm.
"I thought another set of meals was coming for me and the master. I did not expect to see you two. Are we still considered acquaintances? Or are we enemies?"
BOOM!
The question landed and detonated, because of everything Abbadon had just said, one word did the real damage!
The Master!

One mind. One singular mind of unity, integrated across thousands of Descendants and Primeval Ones at once, wearing them the way a lesser being wears clothing, moving their heads in the same instant and glazing their eyes with the same obsidian purple. Thousands of the mighty gathered here, and not one of them was anybody anymore.
THE Great Usurper had grown grandly!

Not to be mistaken for the one who held the mantle of THE USURPER, who was and was not a vessel of THE Sealed One, currently occupying an entirely different region of THE Dimensional Provenance Train.
Two devourers on one train!
And above them all, the enormous eye narrowed!
|THE OVERSEEING ONE observes with growing displeasure.|
|You KNOW each other?|

|Records confirm prior acquaintance between the arrivals and the native inhabitants. This was not accounted for. A Narrative constructed around confrontation loses its tension when the confronting parties open with pleasantries and inquiries after each other’s health.|
|This Narrative is not going according to plan.|
|Something else will have to be done about this.|
The eye pulsed once, and the whole Dimension pulsed with it, the stellar clouds flattening and rebounding across light years!
|A sufficient Narrative of Existence guaranteeing amusement has been selected.|
|THE NARRATIVE OF EXISTENCE: THE TRAGIC HEROES is being instituted.|

paragraphs: |Terms, for the benefit of the participants.|
|You are hereby the unlikely heroes. Outmatched, unprepared, and arriving late, as such heroes always are. You will face a Dark Lord, and the Dark Lord will face you.|

|Due to the considerable annoyance of the preceding Narrative, this one has been set in advance. You are to be DEFEATED. Existential Moirai shall wrap around the Dark Lord to ensure it, and the wrapping is already underway.|
|Should this Narrative somehow be overcome, THE NARRATIVE OF THE TRAGIC HEROES may be overwritten entirely, and the rewards for such a thing would be stupendous.|
|Should things proceed as expected, the Records of your existences will be locked and sent back across time to this initial starting point. You will arrive here again.|
|THE Overseeing One watches with great interest to see how many times you will die before your existences fully collapse.|
|Or whether, on one of your returns, you triumph.|
|Begin.|
The Dimensional Cabin began to shake!

Far across the debris field, a doorway split open in the empty space between two tumbling continents. It cracked wider, and wider still, and obsidian darkness began to spill out of it and pour downward through the stellar clouds, and from the other side came auras that made the thousands already gathered here feel like a warmup!
Descartes looked at it with cold eyes.
THE Primordial Paradox looked at it with colder ones.
Erwin, THE Living Paradox, looked at it and did not blink at all.

And among the Descendants bound in unity, every purple-glazed face turned once more toward THE Primordial Paradox, thousands of them at once across all that floating stone, and they opened thousands of mouths and spoke as one!
"I haven’t reached out to Osmont for help for months now, as I don’t intend to do so now."
The voices came from every direction at once, layered over themselves, one mind and thousands of throats!
"How about it? You all think we can work together to fuck shit up?"
Thousands of heads tilted at the same angle.
"Unity shall spread over everything by itself. But with help..."
The laugh came out of every mouth in the Dimension simultaneously.
"Haha. Things become infinitely easier."
And even as the words finished, the being adorned with the Enneagram rose!

Alexander, THE Peacemaker, stood up on the central asteroid without hurry, and the nine First Causes around his chest brightened as he moved. He thrust out his left hand, and one of the gems on the Enneagram flared, and radiant multicolored light spilled out of it and gathered and drew itself into shape across his open palm!
A bow!
It formed in his grip in a wash of nine-fold color, tall and clean and humming, and the pressure of it alone pushed the stellar clouds back from the asteroid in a slow spreading ring!
He rolled his neck, and it cracked once.
Then he began to float toward the doorway spilling endless darkness, unhurried, average in every way except for the nine roots of Existence burning across his chest and the weapon in his hand!
His voice could barely be discerned as he passed them.
"Peace... is often bloody."
BOOM!
<THE True Human Emperor>
THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering.
The name alone was grand!

It sat in the air of the Realm after Atlas had spoken it, heavier than the ninety suns above the blue-gold hills, heavier than the layered Elsedimension that now shone off to one side of the river like a second horizon that owed nobody anything. Noah stood on the bank and the voice of Atlas continued to ring out over all of it.
|This place is uniquely connected to the time when Immense Ones first rose. It is located in a period of endless potential.|
|But one may ask. Why the hell are Gu Lifeforms involved?|
|Well. Here is where an argument comes in about whether THE First Lifeforms truly were thr first...or if Gu came first from nature.|
|Provenance Lifeforms. Or little insects.|

|Haha! It hurt the pride of many when I posed this question, and I posed it often. Provenance Lifeforms always looked at themselves as THE First Lifeforms. The ones who generated their own weavings of existence, from whom immensity bloomed, all of that.|
|But when we arose, little insects and microbes and things of no cognizance whatsoever were already there.|

|I never understood why we all had to be so prideful that we did not even care that insects like Gu were around before us. Maybe the argument is that they had no will and no cognizance. Fine. But Gu are among the lifeforms most closely bound to nature itself. It is as if they bloomed out of the surrounding existence into shapes and forms on their own. They are blank slates, and many things can be written on a blank slate.|
|Think of them like empty pages in a vast book, waiting to be filled.|
|They have the potential to become ANYTHING. Which makes them one of the grandest materials in the entire Engineering of Existence.|
Gu!

Noah’s eyes shone sharply as the word landed, because he knew someone who used them! Ryaenara! A lifeform close to him, who had wielded those little insects since before he had ever met her, and whose weavings of existence had always carried something unique that he had never quite gotten to the bottom of.
Her and her brother. Ulf, with his rhymes and his paintings, were unique.
Already, another body of his was moving!
Across existence, a second Noah turned his steps toward the two siblings, because if Gu were a material grand enough, then he wanted every scrap of information the two of them held.
But the voice of Atlas continued.

|The nature of Gu is unique. Loose existence does not stay loose. Left alone long enough in a sealed place, surrounding existence condenses, and what it condenses into in THE Chrysalis are lifeforms.|
|Gu are that condensation. Each one is a single concept that has become alive.|
|A Time Gu is not a creature that manipulates time. It IS time, in the shape of an insect. And it is hungry.|

|Their purity comes from being one thing entirely. A Cause holds an Observable Existence up. A Gu simply is the concept, with nothing else mixed in. Compare them as ingredients. A Cause is a brick, stable and dead. A Gu is a living brick.|
|There are Gu related to Time. Dream. Destiny. Death. Life. Space. Silence. Memory. Weight. Hunger. Records. Purity. Chance.|
|There are common Gu. There are rare Gu. And there are Gu that even Immense Ones will fight you for, and lose gracelessly.|

|They have extremely high Dimensionality as many can’t even percieve them. And one unique thing about them. To sustain themselves, they feed on the parts of existence they are made from. A Dream Gu eats dreams. A Time Gu eats timelines. A Chance Gu eats luck.|
|And THIS is also how you enter.|
|You have to make yourself into a meal that a Gu will want to pull into THE Chrysalis and eat.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5704: Chrysalis I
paragraphs: He had to make himself into a meal.
Noah sighed lightly. He craned his neck to one side until it clicked, and then to the other, and rolled his shoulders once, and was ready to get started, because of course that was the method!
|Of course, something like that alone might be too hard to conceptualize. So.|

|Wrap your entire existence in whatever nature your Provenance holds. And while you do so, communicate with your surroundings how you WANT to be consumed. How you are giving yourself away for something grander and greater than yourself.|
|Provenance offered away is one of the easiest ways to get the attention of a Gu of a similar type in THE Chrysalis.|
|But even then, you could be doing that for years and never be picked up. The Chrysalis is not short on meals.|

|Which is where I come in. I have been there before. So I can form a tether from you to THE Chrysalis. You are the bait, and I am the fishing line, connecting you to the jaws of whatever Gu decides to consume you and pull you across.|
|Ready?|
|Imagine you are appetizing and grand. And then say the words...|
|I am filled with determination.|
Noah’s eyes pulsed as he got ready!

He drew his Provenance Essence up out of the depth of himself and let it out, and it came out as waves of blue-gold light that rolled off his skin and rose and wrapped him, layer over layer, until he stood inside a cloud of his own making with ninety suns burning above it!

He envisioned himself as the most appetizing meal in existence. He put his whole will into it, and he told the surroundings without words that here was a Provenance, self-generated, freely offered, given away for something grander!
THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer pulsed!

Waves of endless dreams poured out of him and joined the cloud, dreams of everything he had ever been and everything he had decided to become, and they wound through the blue-gold light until the whole of it shimmered with the soft heavy quality of a thing that is more than half asleep and entirely awake at once!
And Noah said the words.
"I am filled with determination!"
HUUM!
Brilliance pulsed across the whole Realm!
And out of the ring came a sound Noah had heard once before and had hoped not to hear again.
|Haha! Did you really say the words ’I am filled with determination’?|
|You actually do not need to say that shit! Haha!|
Noah stood inside his cloud of offered Provenance and dreams, appetizing and grand, and said absolutely nothing at all.
|Alright, alright. I will get serious and tether you.|
The ring on his finger went hot!
|Be ready. Once you are eaten, you will appear in the belly of a Gu related to your Provenance.|
|I hope it is a common Gu that does not metabolize you instantly.|
Noah’s eye twitched.
He hoped it was a common Gu!
Noah closed his eyes, appetizing and grand, and waited to be eaten as he was trusting an ancient lifeform who messed around far, far too much!
It did not take too long before...
Something hooked into him!

Not a hand, not a grip, not any of the shapes that pulling usually took. It was a thread going taut somewhere behind his sternum, and the taut thread was attached to somewhere else, and the somewhere else began to reel!
Noah’s existence left!

It left the Realm, left the bank of the river, left the ninety suns and the layered Elsedimension, and it went out along the thread toward another weaving of existence entirely, and the going was not like crossing a Dimension!
Crossing a Dimension was still travel. This was something stranger, because as he went, he felt himself leaving the weavings of time itself.
Before and after came apart around him.

Duration stopped being a thing that happened and became a thing he was passing out of, almost like how a swimmer passes out of water, and on the far side of it there was no current, no direction, no order to events, only a wide slow place where time had no meaning because time had not yet decided to mean anything!
And then...after what could have been days or years, he felt like he...was being eaten.
His Provenance was being sucked away, drawn off him in long hungry pulls, as existence materialized around him out of nothing and he found himself inside something!

Murky golden clouds of dream surrounded him on every side, thick and soft and warm, and through the clouds ran tentacles, dozens of them, pale and translucent and lined with something that shimmered, and every one of them was fastened to him and siphoning his Provenance into the murk!
BOOM!
Noah withdrew immediately!

He pulled his Provenance in all at once, from the offered cloud, from the dreams he had poured out as bait, from every tentacle that had latched onto him, drawing the whole of it back inside himself in one hard contraction, and the thing he was inside of RUMBLED!
The golden murk convulsed around him. The tentacles whipped loose. Whatever had been feeding found its meal suddenly and violently inedible, and it did what anything does with an inedible meal.
It spat him out!

Noah shot forward through membranes, one after another after another, each one pulsing with heavy brilliance as he tore through it, wet golden light bursting around him on every side, and then the last membrane gave way and he was out, tumbling through open air into light!
HUUM!
And instantly...
Every quark in his existence buzzed.
Every cell. Every particle of the two hundred decillion. All of them thrummed at once with a single unmistakable message, which was that he had arrived somewhere grand.
|You have arrived at an unfathomable place.|
|Nature here is extremely loose and permeable. Reality is entirely fluid and heavily hallucinatory.|
|The sky might rain liquid fire. The ground might turn to event horizons. Time itself dilates and contracts without warning.|
|If you remain in one place for too long without individual thoughts, or without sufficient Trueness, you may assimilate into the surrounding existence.|
|Be immeasurably careful.|
|You have arrived in THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5705: Chrysalis II
paragraphs: Noah righted himself in the air and looked at what he had come out of.
It hung before him, vast and slow, and it was the strangest living thing he had ever laid eyes on, and he had laid eyes on a great many!
It should be...
A Dream Gu!

It was insect and microbe at once and neither, a bloated golden body the size of a small moon that was somehow also translucent, with the murky dream-clouds he had just been inside visible drifting through its interior like weather.

Segmented plates ran along its length, soft and overlapping, and from between them extended the pale siphoning tentacles, now curling back inward, and beneath its body hung dozens of thin jointed legs that did not touch anything and did not need to. Its whole surface shimmered with the quality of a thing half-remembered on waking, edges that would not hold still, colors that changed depending on whether he looked directly at them!
And it had eyes.
Many of them, scattered across its front in no particular arrangement, each one a slow golden orb, and every single one of them was pointed at him.
They looked at him the way a thing looks at an oddity. Not hostile or afraid. Simply confused that a meal had stopped being a meal.
Then its existence buzzed, and it vanished!

It moved so fast that Noah could barely follow it, the great translucent bulk of it shooting away into the distance and shrinking, and as it went he strained after it with everything he had and caught only the barest glimpse of its details before it was gone entirely!
|DREAM GU|
|Rarity: Common|
|VERITAS: 104 / PROVENANCE: 101 / POTENTIA: 107 / PONDUS: 102|
Common?
That was a COMMON Gu?!
It had run from him, and every attribute it held was above a hundred, and it was COMMON.
Noah stood in the air and did not move for a moment, and then, since the thing had gone and nothing else was trying to eat him yet, he looked around!
Strands descended from above.

Multicolored, fine as silk, falling in slow unhurried drifts all around him, thousands of them, more, catching a light that came from nowhere he could locate. They floated down gently and did not land anywhere, since there was nowhere to land, and they touched his skin as they passed and each touch carried something.
A color that was also a mood. A texture that was also a memory of a thing that had never happened to him.
And beyond the strands, in every direction, all around and all around...
Nebulas!

Boundless, swirling, kaleidoscopic, filling the whole of the visible existence from horizon to horizon in every axis, gold and violet and a green he had never seen and a red that hurt to look at, all of it turning and folding and unfolding again, never repeating, layered so deep that the far ones showed through the near ones and the near ones showed through his own hands!
This was where the beings who exceeded had left their leavings.

Noah stood very still inside a chrysalis older than Records, with silk falling around him and nebulas turning past him, and he breathed once, slowly, and made very sure that he kept thinking his own thoughts.
|You did not get eaten?|
Atlas voice echoed out.
|This is good. Welcome to THE Chrysalis.|

|A dangerous place, where you may very well die before you accomplish anything at all. It is a place of immensity and wonder. The Gu Lifeforms are mostly doing things of their own nature and will leave you be, but if you attack them, or try to capture particularly powerful ones, they may kill you before you even know it has happened.|
|Oh, and some particularly unique Immense Ones may be moving around here. So. Death from all sides is possible.|
|But hey. Is this not a fun place?|
Noah’s eye twitched.
|This is where I made some of my grandest designs. Haha!|
|Let us get you familiar with the different types of Gu, and then we can see whether you can locate a decent one to try forming your first Gu Elsedimension Ring.|
|It will not be anywhere near as grand in quality as mine was. But hey.|
|We all have to start somewhere. Right?|
Noah listened to the crazy Engineer inside thr illusory ring as he kept thinking!

That was the first rule of this place! He moved slowly through the falling silk with his own thoughts running loud and deliberate in his head, refusing the surrounding existence every soft invitation to simply stop being a separate thing and join it!

Because it WAS inviting. The nebulas turned past him in colors that had never existed anywhere else, and the strands brushed his skin and left moods behind, and every part of the Chrysalis whispered that it would be so easy to loosen a little. Just a little. Just enough to see what it felt like.
Noah did not loosen!
The ring on his finger went warm.
|Are you still you? Alright. Before you go blundering into something that eats you properly this time, let me tell you what lives here.|
Golden light spilled out of the ring and unfolded in the air before him!

It drew itself into shapes, thin bright lines hanging against the kaleidoscope, holographic and turning slowly, and the first shape it made was an insect Noah recognized, bloated and translucent and many-eyed, rendered small enough to sit in his palm.
|There are three rarities of Gu. I will give them to you in the order you will meet them, which is also the order in which they will kill you.|
|First. COMMON GU.|
The golden insect pulsed!

|These are what happens when loose existence sits sealed in one place long enough to condense. Nothing more. No one made them. No one meant them. A concept drifted here after the Sundering, found nothing to hold it, and slowly folded itself into a shape with legs.|
|One concept each. Total purity. A Common Gu is a hundred of one thing and nothing at all of anything else. No will beyond hunger. No cognizance beyond appetite.|
|There may be hundreds of thousands of them in the Chrysalis. They flee from anything that is not food.|
|Uses: everything. Engines, rings, weapons, locks, the foundation of any serious design. Cheap. Plentiful. Do not get sentimental about them.|
The golden insect faded, and a second shape drew itself in its place, and this one was different!

It was longer, sleeker, plated in overlapping gold that caught light from angles the light was not coming from, and at its head, where the first shape had scattered many eyes, this one held only two. The lines that drew them were very careful.
|Second. RARE GU.|
|A Rare Gu does not condense out of loose existence. It condenses AROUND something.|

|The beings who exceeded and departed shed pieces of themselves. A memory too heavy to carry through. An ambition that would not fit. A grudge. A grief. A single decision they refused to be defined by any longer. Those shed pieces fell here, and existence condensed around them the way pearl condenses around grit.|
|A Rare Gu carries an ECHO of whatever it grew around. Not the being. The being is gone. But a preference. A leaning. Sometimes a grudge that outlived the one who held it by an age.|
|A Rare Gu will look at you and decide whether you are worth the effort of noticing, and if it decides yes, that is not necessarily good news.|
|Their depth is a full Fold above the Common ones, which I will explain shortly. Immense Ones may fight you for a Rare Gu if you come across them.|
|My ring, the one you gave back, was built around a Rare Chance Gu that I spent three hundred years earning the attention of. So. That is what you gave away.|

The golden shape faded.

|THE FIRST GU.|

|One per concept. Time. Dream. Death. Chance. The rest. One each, and none of them has ever left, and every Gu of that weaving of existence of that concept in existence descends from them.|

Did they know and feel thst Narrative? Did they sense whenever those descended from their concepts have anything done?
|Have I met one? Maybe. Maybe. Ah...|
The house-sized hologram folded down into nothing.
|Now. Since I have taught without explaining things too well, I should probably teach you how everything is ranked on the weavings and constraints of Dimensionality.|
|Which is only part of the equation, by the way.|

The sheet creased once, and the crease glowed.

A third fold, deeper, and the gold went darker where it turned. Did that fold correlate to THE Transfinite Verse?

|A Common Gu sits at the Seam.|
The sheet folded a fourth time, and the fold was so tight it was hard to see where the gold went.

|THE WEAVE.|

Noah said it before he had decided to, and the instant the words left him he felt it, a decimal of a percent of his Provenance drawn away, small and exact and gone!
|Ah.|

|Now you know what a wasted question feels like, because I am not answering it. There is a fold past the Weave. What it is called and what it is like are not things I will say inside a place that is listening.|
The golden weave dimmed.

Three rings of gold drew themselves in the air, interlocking.
|DEPTH. Which fold you occupy. That is Dimensionality.|
|MAGNITUDE. How much of you sits there. This can be a measure of Trueness, your Provenance, Lifeforce, even potential of your existence.|
Those...would be the 4 attributes he designed to percieve and quantify himself?

The three rings held a moment longer, turning through each other, and then folded away into the ring on his finger and were gone.

|Engineering raises depth and magnitude. That is the whole reason I am teaching you and not simply handing you tools. Every Elsedimension you build, every Gu you bind, every design you understand from the inside pushes you one thread deeper into the cloth. I climbed from the Crease to the Hem by building things. You may climb faster, because you generate what I had to gather.|

|Let us find you a Common Gu that does not run, and see whether you can bind it into your first ring.|

Because among the thousands of multicolored strands drifting gently down through the kaleidoscope all around him, one was not drifting.

It hung perfectly still, taut, running upward out of sight, and at the bottom of it, no larger than his hand and plated in gold that caught light from angles the light was not coming from, something with exactly two eyes was looking at him.
It was not confused.
It was deciding!
Oh.
Fuck!

chapters.title: Chapter 5706: Defy!
paragraphs: Noah did not move!

Not a finger and not a breath he did not need. He stood in the falling silk with the kaleidoscope turning past him and he held himself utterly still, because the thing at the bottom of the one taut strand was looking at him, and it had not yet finished deciding what he was!
It hung no larger than his hand.

Golden plates overlapped along its body, and they caught light from angles the light was not coming from, so that it seemed lit from inside by something that was not quite in this place! Six jointed legs folded neatly against it. Two wings lay closed along its back, and through them, faint and slow, drifted shapes that were not there when he looked directly and were there again when he looked away.
And at its head sat exactly two eyes, deep gold, unblinking, and both of them held him the way a scale holds a weight!
|DREAM GU|
|Rarity: RARE|
|Depth: THE HEM|
|VERITAS: 341 / PROVENANCE: 328 / POTENTIA: 356 / PONDUS: 339|
|Echo: condensed around a shed fragment. Nature of fragment: a dream that was not finished.|
Three hundred and forty-one!

A full Fold above him! Sitting at the edge of the cloth where he had never stood, holding an echo of something a departed being had dreamed and could not carry through the crossing, and looking at him with total patience while his ring went warm and then very deliberately went silent!
Atlas was not going to help with this one.
And then the Gu spoke!

Its voice did not come from its mouth, since it had none that he could find. It came from the silk. Every falling strand in the vicinity carried a thread of it, so that the words arrived from above and around him at once, layered, grand, and unhurried in the way of a thing that has never once been made to wait!
"I sensed the weavings of a Unique Dream here."
The two eyes did not blink.

"Something dreamed in this place that was not of this place. Grandly. Grandly enough to draw me down from where I hang. Nothing dreams as grandly as I do within a great many strands of here, little one."
The wings along its back stirred, and the shapes inside them turned.
"So I will put it to a test. Dream with me. Keep pace, and I will know what you are. Fall behind, and you will simply become part of what I dream."
BOOM!
The Dream Gu dreamed!
And the Chrysalis around Noah was gone!

He stood on a shore of black glass beneath a sky that was a single closed eyelid, and the sea before him was made of every conversation he had ever left unfinished, murmuring, and the tide was going out!
He had one heartbeat to understand what was being asked, and he understood it, because THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer surged up through his quarks and he did not resist the dream!
He joined it!

THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM woke inside him, and Noah imposed his own mind’s simulation over the Gu’s, not against it, alongside it, weaving his dream through the Gu’s dream at the seam where the two met!

The tide was going out. He dreamed a moon. The moon rose over the closed eyelid of the sky, and the tide turned, and the sea of unfinished conversations came back in and he stood in it to his knees and let them finish!
The Gu’s dream shifted!

The shore folded upward into a staircase with no top, each step a year he had not lived yet, and it was already climbing without him, and to fall behind was to be left on a year that would never arrive!

Noah dreamed his legs longer. He dreamed the steps shorter. He dreamed that he had always been at the top already and was only remembering the climb, and the staircase, faced with a dreamer who refused its premise, agreed with him!
Faster!
The dream became a city that was also his own skeleton, streets running along his ribs, and something was hunting through it that wore his son’s face and was not his son!
Noah dreamed the streets lit. He dreamed the thing’s true face, and it was only a dream of a fear, and he dreamed the fear a chair and sat it down and told it to wait.

The dream became a fire that burned memories for fuel, and he dreamed himself into a memory the fire could not reach, one it had never been given, a preschool teacher and a word he had not understood at five years old and the way his mother’s hand had tightened on his!

The dream became a silence that ate the names of things, and he dreamed his own name into the silence and let it be eaten and dreamed it again, and again, and again, faster than the silence could swallow, until the silence gave up!
Faster!
The Gu was not slowing!

It was curious now, and its curiosity ran the dreams harder, stranger, folding three into one, a war that was also a wedding that was also the last second before a star collapsed, and Noah dreamed through all three at once, his Provenance blazing, sweat standing on his skin in a place that had no heat, dreaming, dreaming, dreaming alongside a thing three hundred and forty-one Trueness deep and refusing, absolutely refusing, to fall one single step behind!
And then it stopped.

The Chrysalis came back around him all at once. Silk falling. Nebulas turning. Noah standing exactly where he had been standing, breathing hard, his Provenance drawn thin and humming, and the small golden Gu hanging at the bottom of its strand exactly where it had hung.
It looked at him for a long moment.
Then it nodded.
One slow inclination of that plated head, and the shapes inside its wings turned once and settled!
"It is nice," the Dream Gu said, "to see a little one starting out who is a true dreamer."
The strand it hung from began to draw upward.
"There are so few. Most who come here dream of things. You dream with them. That is the older way. Take this."
Something detached from beneath one of its wings and drifted down, slow, turning, and landed in Noah’s open palm!
A scale.
A single golden plate no larger than a coin, still warm, still catching light from angles the light was not coming from, and as it touched his skin, prompts unfolded!
|DREAMER’S SCALE|
|A shed plate of a Rare Dream Gu, given freely. It carries the Gu’s recognition.|

|Function: a key. In the Chrysalis, the deeper silk of the Dream weavings will part for the bearer. Elsewhere, any dream the bearer walks will know they were acknowledged by something older than dreaming.|
|Function: a mark. Other Dream Gu will perceive the bearer as one who kept pace. Most will not test again. Some will be curious.|

The Dream Gu rose along its strand, and the strand rose with it, and in the space of a breath it was gone into the upper silk and only the falling threads remained, gentle and multicolored and no longer looking at anyone.
Noah closed his hand around the scale.
The ring on his finger grew warm again.
|For a second there, I thought you were dead.|

|My weavings are waking up a bit more, in this place that used to be my home for some time. This construct can have a bit more freedom here. So let us go. You survived one encounter with a Rare one that you cannot overcome, and I would like that to remain the total.|
|Let us find a Common one.|
|You should be able to converse with me more freely here. At most, you can treat me like a database. Ask questions. They will eat your Provenance. Ask anyway.|
Noah looked at the ring for a moment.
Then he looked at the scale in his hand, and the silk, and the place where a thing a Fold above him had gone back up into the dark with a nod, and he made a decision about how to spend what he had.
"I can ask you a lot of questions," he said. "But tell me something that you feel is the most important for me to know."
The ring was silent.

Not the silence of before, when Atlas had held back so the Gu could judge. A different silence. The silence of a cluster of records and probability searching a very long life for the one thing in it that mattered most, and taking its time about the search!
Then Atlas spoke, and for once, there was no laugh in it.
|When I was rising in power, I traveled for a time with two Immense Ones.|

|One of them you know. She did not go by Widow then. She had another name, and I will not say it here, since she has earned her quiet and this place listens. The other was a strand of a different kind, and does not matter to this story.|
|The three of us came to a region of THE Chrysalis that holds a mountain.|

|I want you to picture it properly. The whole mountain was made of Gu. Not living on it. Made of it. Millions of them, Common and Rare, locked together into a peak that went up past the sky and out of sight, every one of them powerful enough to kill me twice at the depth I held then, and every one of them still and quiet and waiting.|
|And at the summit sat a Gu so rare that any Immense One in existence would go mad for it.|

|Here is the thing. Existence itself held a Narrative over that mountain. A Ruling, undeniable, older than the two Immense Ones I stood beside. The Ruling said: to reach the peak and claim the Gu, one must follow the path that has been carved. There was a path. It wound up the mountain through all those millions of waiting Gu. And the Ruling was the kind that existence does not argue with, because existence wrote it.|
|So the two Immense Ones climbed.|

|They were strands of the Weave, and they walked the carved path, and the path was a Ruling, and Rulings hold. But the path was carved to break whatever walked it. Every turn of it fed them to the mountain a piece at a time. And halfway up, the two most powerful beings I had ever stood beside could not go further. They were injured in ways I did not know Immense Ones could be injured. She was bleeding light. I will never forget it.|
|And I did not climb.|
The ring was warm in Noah’s hand, and the silk fell, and he did not interrupt.

|I looked at the carved path and I thought, this is a Ruling. It is undeniable. Existence wrote it. Fine. What does it actually say? It says the peak is reached by the path. It does not say the path is reached by walking.|

|I turned around and went back down into the outer silk, and I spent a long while looking, and I found a Common Gu. A Defiance Gu. The least impressive insect you have ever seen. A concept condensed out of nothing, no will, no echo, just a small pure crystallized refusal with six legs, running from me the moment it tasted that I was not food.|
|I caught it anyway. I bound it into the first shield I ever built, and the shield held one thing, which was its Defiance. Not strength. Not depth. Refusal, held up in front of me like a lantern.|
|Then I went back to the mountain, and I raised the shield, and I did not walk the carved path.|
|I walked straight up.|

|And the Ruling of the mountain met a Common insect’s refusal and did not know what to do with it, because a Ruling is a sentence existence wrote, and the Defiance Gu was a concept existence had condensed, and they were made of the same stuff, and the older one was the refusal. The mountain could not decide whether I was breaking its Ruling or expressing it. While it was deciding, I reached the top.|
|I took the Gu. Then I went back down, and I carried two Immense Ones off that mountain one at a time under a shield made out of a bug that was afraid of me.|
|That is the story.|
The silk kept falling. The nebulas turned.
|This is the most important thing I know, and I have spent a very long time knowing it.|

|In Existence, many beings hold Rulings. Existence itself holds Rulings, and Scales, and Narratives, and a great many more things besides. Some of them are undeniable, and they are called undeniable because it is true. You will meet a hundred of them before you die, and every one of them will be written in a sentence that sounds final.|
|But you do not necessarily have to follow those Rulings. Or those Scales. Or the words of anyone else. Including me. Especially me, because I am a record, and records love to be obeyed.|
|Question everything you hear. And then bring your own refusal to it, whatever shape your refusal takes, and hold it up, and walk straight up the mountain.|
|Your own defiance...your own path.|
|That is what leads to the peak. Nothing else ever has.|

Noah stood in the silk with a Dream Gu’s scale warm in one hand and a dead man’s most important lesson warm in the other, and for a long moment he simply held both of them, and did not move, and thought his own thoughts.
Then he closed his hand, and went to find a Common Gu!

sentences.text: Noah did not move!
Not a finger and not a breath he did not need.

He stood in the falling silk with the kaleidoscope turning past him and he held himself utterly still, because the thing at the bottom of the one taut strand was looking at him, and it had not yet finished deciding what he was!
It hung no larger than his hand.
Golden plates overlapped along its body, and they caught light from angles the light was not coming from, so that it seemed lit from inside by something that was not quite in this place!
Six jointed legs folded neatly against it.
Two wings lay closed along its back, and through them, faint and slow, drifted shapes that were not there when he looked directly and were there again when he looked away.
And at its head sat exactly two eyes, deep gold, unblinking, and both of them held him the way a scale holds a weight!
|DREAM GU|
|Rarity: RARE|
|Depth: THE HEM|
|VERITAS: 341 / PROVENANCE: 328 / POTENTIA: 356 / PONDUS: 339|
|Echo: condensed around a shed fragment.
Nature of fragment: a dream that was not finished.|
Three hundred and forty-one!
A full Fold above him!

Sitting at the edge of the cloth where he had never stood, holding an echo of something a departed being had dreamed and could not carry through the crossing, and looking at him with total patience while his ring went warm and then very deliberately went silent!
Atlas was not going to help with this one.
And then the Gu spoke!
Its voice did not come from its mouth, since it had none that he could find.
It came from the silk.

Every falling strand in the vicinity carried a thread of it, so that the words arrived from above and around him at once, layered, grand, and unhurried in the way of a thing that has never once been made to wait!
"I sensed the weavings of a Unique Dream here."
The two eyes did not blink.
"Something dreamed in this place that was not of this place.
Grandly.
Grandly enough to draw me down from where I hang.
Nothing dreams as grandly as I do within a great many strands of here, little one."
The wings along its back stirred, and the shapes inside them turned.
"So I will put it to a test.
Dream with me.
Keep pace, and I will know what you are.
Fall behind, and you will simply become part of what I dream."
BOOM!
The Dream Gu dreamed!
And the Chrysalis around Noah was gone!

He stood on a shore of black glass beneath a sky that was a single closed eyelid, and the sea before him was made of every conversation he had ever left unfinished, murmuring, and the tide was going out!
He had one heartbeat to understand what was being asked, and he understood it, because THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer surged up through his quarks and he did not resist the dream!
He joined it!

THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM woke inside him, and Noah imposed his own mind’s simulation over the Gu’s, not against it, alongside it, weaving his dream through the Gu’s dream at the seam where the two met!
The tide was going out.
He dreamed a moon.
The moon rose over the closed eyelid of the sky, and the tide turned, and the sea of unfinished conversations came back in and he stood in it to his knees and let them finish!
The Gu’s dream shifted!

The shore folded upward into a staircase with no top, each step a year he had not lived yet, and it was already climbing without him, and to fall behind was to be left on a year that would never arrive!
Noah dreamed his legs longer.
He dreamed the steps shorter.
He dreamed that he had always been at the top already and was only remembering the climb, and the staircase, faced with a dreamer who refused its premise, agreed with him!
Faster!
The dream became a city that was also his own skeleton, streets running along his ribs, and something was hunting through it that wore his son’s face and was not his son!
Noah dreamed the streets lit.
He dreamed the thing’s true face, and it was only a dream of a fear, and he dreamed the fear a chair and sat it down and told it to wait.

The dream became a fire that burned memories for fuel, and he dreamed himself into a memory the fire could not reach, one it had never been given, a preschool teacher and a word he had not understood at five years old and the way his mother’s hand had tightened on his!

The dream became a silence that ate the names of things, and he dreamed his own name into the silence and let it be eaten and dreamed it again, and again, and again, faster than the silence could swallow, until the silence gave up!
Faster!
The Gu was not slowing!

It was curious now, and its curiosity ran the dreams harder, stranger, folding three into one, a war that was also a wedding that was also the last second before a star collapsed, and Noah dreamed through all three at once, his Provenance blazing, sweat standing on his skin in a place that had no heat, dreaming, dreaming, dreaming alongside a thing three hundred and forty-one Trueness deep and refusing, absolutely refusing, to fall one single step behind!
And then it stopped.
The Chrysalis came back around him all at once.
Silk falling.
Nebulas turning.
Noah standing exactly where he had been standing, breathing hard, his Provenance drawn thin and humming, and the small golden Gu hanging at the bottom of its strand exactly where it had hung.
It looked at him for a long moment.
Then it nodded.
One slow inclination of that plated head, and the shapes inside its wings turned once and settled!
"It is nice," the Dream Gu said, "to see a little one starting out who is a true dreamer."
The strand it hung from began to draw upward.
"There are so few.
Most who come here dream of things.
You dream with them.
That is the older way.
Take this."
Something detached from beneath one of its wings and drifted down, slow, turning, and landed in Noah’s open palm!
A scale.
A single golden plate no larger than a coin, still warm, still catching light from angles the light was not coming from, and as it touched his skin, prompts unfolded!
|DREAMER’S SCALE|
|A shed plate of a Rare Dream Gu, given freely.
It carries the Gu’s recognition.|
|Function: a key.
In the Chrysalis, the deeper silk of the Dream weavings will part for the bearer.
Elsewhere, any dream the bearer walks will know they were acknowledged by something older than dreaming.|
|Function: a mark.
Other Dream Gu will perceive the bearer as one who kept pace.
Most will not test again.
Some will be curious.|

Noah closed his hand around the scale.
The ring on his finger grew warm again.

This construct can have a bit more freedom here.
So let us go.
You survived one encounter with a Rare one that you cannot overcome, and I would like that to remain the total.|

At most, you can treat me like a database.
Ask questions.
They will eat your Provenance.
Ask anyway.|

Then he looked at the scale in his hand, and the silk, and the place where a thing a Fold above him had gone back up into the dark with a nod, and he made a decision about how to spend what he had.

chapters.title: Chapter 5707: Powerless! I
paragraphs: <THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering>
Far from where a Human Dreamer walked with a golden scale in his hand, the silk was being torn.

Nine riders moved through the deep nebulas at a pace that did not belong to this place. The Chrysalis was slow. Everything in it drifted. These did not drift. They drove forward through the falling strands in a wedge, and the strands parted ahead of them and did not settle behind, and the kaleidoscope itself seemed to hold its colors still until they had passed!
They were Descendants, and then, there were theseDescendants.

Not the cursed kind with rot at the fissures and salvation begged from a Father who never answered. These were the other thing, the thing the cursed ones had been bred as a shadow of! Each of them stood the height of a small mountain, titanic and ancient, and their bodies were carved of the same substance that Jarl Erling’s had been, bronze and stone and old fire, but nothing in them was cracking.
Their skin held no fissures. Their eyes held no fear. They sat their mounts with the posture of beings who had never once in their existence had to ask whether they would wake up tomorrow!
And their Steeds burned with glory.

Every one of them akin to a living Observable Existence, bred exactly as Hvitrmarr had been bred, and every one of them was whole! Their First Causes did not fail. Nine or more in every mount, seated in the organs, pouring light out through the hide, so that each Steed moved through the silk wrapped in its own dawn!
No two were alike.
The leading Steed was a colossal white stag, its antlers branching upward into forks that held whole Observable Existences turning in their tines.
Beside it walked a thing with six legs and a serpent’s body, scaled in gold, its Causes lighting the scales from underneath so that it looked struck through with sunrise.
Behind them a quadruped of black stone with rivers of molten Cause running down its flanks. A winged one, feathered in silver, wings folded because there was no wind here to need them.

A low heavy beast with a shell of overlapping plates, each plate a continent. A hound with three heads and one heartbeat. A horse, plainly a horse, and somehow the most frightening of them all for it, since only a being of terrible confidence chooses to ride the ordinary shape!
And behind the nine, dragged by ropes, came the catch.
Three Common Dream Gu.

Moon-sized, translucent, bloated with murky golden dream-weather, their many eyes rolling in every direction and their soft plates heaving! They had been bound in obsidian rope, thick as rivers, and the rope burned with Causes, and where it touched the Gu the dream-stuff inside them went dark and still.
The Gu did not struggle. Something in the rope had convinced them not to as the faint power of an Immense One could be felt coursing through the ropes.
The hunt had gone well.
At the head of the wedge, on the white stag whose antlers held Observable Existences, the leader sat with the reins gathered in one hand!

She was the largest of them. Fierce-faced, titanic, her crimson eyes burning steady in a face carved of old bronze, and her armor was not armor but the plain bare weight of a body that had never needed any. The Causes of her Steed lit her from below. The silk parted ahead of her before she reached it.
She looked back once at the three bound Gu, and her mouth curved.
Then she grasped the reins.
"Father enjoys his dreams more than usual."
Her voice went out through the nebulas and did not come back!
"So we have to find at least ten Dream Weavings Gu. If we can obtain more..."The crimson eyes turned forward. "Then it is only greater glory for us."
The white stag lowered its head.
"Come on!"

The nine drove forward into the deep silk, wedge tight, Steeds blazing, dragging three bound dreams behind them toward a Father who had not once in the whole of recorded existence been described as sleeping!
The Descendants of THE Sleepless Fiend. his First Borns, were hunting in the Chrysalis!
<THE Vasiliou Elseworld>
Existence...was always unpredictable.
Noah knew this. He made many plans because of unpredictability. But still, he never knew everything.
It was only human to not know everything!
At this time.
While one of his bodies held an important journey in THE Chrysalis, one of Noah’s other bodies felt a tremendous change in the golden spring inside a certain mountain.
He was holding onto Thalia when...
The spring went cold before anything arrived.
It was a heavy cold, and Noah felt it first in the stolen thing inside him, THE Provenance of THE Immense Sovereign, which had sat quiet in his depths since the day he took it.
Thalia’s hand closed on his arm as they stopped their Dual Cultivation session.
"Something is coming!" she said with alarm as robes covered her body!
At this time, when it seemed ever so peaceful and without absolutely any issues...
Above the Vasiliou Elseworld, the violet sky tore.

The whole bioluminescent dome of it simply stopped being a sky and became a face, or the pressure of one, enormous and looking down, and the moss-stone arcs on their localized gravities began to drift out of true as the gravities themselves lost their nerve!
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR has arrived. You can honor him by many different names, but today, he is a Collector that was not paid.|

|He perceives what was taken from him. It is still being drawn upon. It is being drawn upon now, in a spring, by a thing that did not ask. He can smell his prize filled with the seed of another as he is furious.|
|He is more than fucking displeased.|
An Immense One who did not get what he was promised!
Noah had known this being may send forces or even come himself, but he didn’t expect it so soon!

And he...had gone under the assumption that truly, the influence of an Immense One would be diminished in an Elsedimension! And yet here was one bypassing whatever rulings...and having his power crash into the inhabitants of an Elsedimension. How?
At this time.
The Elseworld answered!
Every lotus in the crystalline lakes below sealed at once, island-sized petals closing over the basins in domes of blue-gold. Light ran up the continent-trunked trees.

And from the golden tower at the heart of Vasileia, Provenance Lifeforms rose into the air, the twelve Elders of the lineage at their head, ancient and radiant, the beings Noah had seen ringed around Aurelius before.
He knew their faces.
They rose to defend their lineage, twelve Ages of standing gathered in the torn violet air!
And at their head, Aurelius Vasiliou.

He came up out of the city with his hands still behind his back, and THE Provenance of THE Unfallen Vanguard unfolded around him for the twelfth time in his existence, and the unfolding was a truth stated aloud to the whole Elseworld: that to injure his home, they would have to get through him, that what stands here will still be standing after!
He rose to the level of the enormous face, and he did not flinch from it, and he spoke!
"You did not get what was promised," Aurelius said, and his voice went out steady across the Elseworld.

"My lineage does not hide from a debt. So name it. What price is owed, and what price can be paid? Speak it, and let us settle this as existences that have both stood a long time, and not as a fire and the thing it burns. We have weavings and karma with other Immense Ones as we can always work-"
HUUM!
The face in the sky interrupted him.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR hears the patriarch’s offer.|
|He finds it quaint and says...you dumb fucking buffoon.|
|Today,|he said, and the pressure gathered as he said it,|I will not collect so much as I will kill. I don’t give a damn what you are allied with.|
The pressure came down as Aurelius was shocked and horrified!
What!
This was not how things should play out! An Immense One shouldn’t act so openly and brazenly like this!
What...
BOOM!

It did not strike Aurelius. It struck the lineage around him, and an Elder with the long white braid... simply became less. Her light thinned. Her outline lost its edges. And then the air where she had been held nothing at all!
Rivers of undeniable power of an Immense One continued to come down in spans of instants!

|Some beings should know their place,| the Collector said, |You have lived a long while beside your betters and mistaken proximity for peerage. A candle set near a strand of the Weave is still a candle. It only learns this at the end.|

|Do Provenance Lifeforms no longer fear Immense Ones? Did you all think we are so passive and laid back, only sending messages? Is that why you fucked me over? Did you all forget you sit below us? You aren’t even some ancient clan as I cannot fathom what gave you the balls, you fucking buffoons. |
HUUM!

Another Provenance Lifeform, a broad quiet Elder, threw himself across the space before Aurelius, arms wide, and took the descending power of THE Immense One and did not make a sound, and went out like a flicker of light, his Provenance extinguished!
|The dignity of some existences cannot be crossed,| the Collector went on, unhurried, as a second Elder guttered and a third roared, the entire Vasiliou Elseworld thrown into panic!
|Mine was crossed by a thief, and I have come to teach the whole of the house that sheltered the drawing of it that some lines, once crossed, do not admit of payment. Only of correction.|
Aurelius’s Vanguard held, barely as he was ashen while looking at the destruction!
This truly was not what he had envisioned!
He had thought wrong! Oh, so wrong!

It is being drawn upon now, in a spring, by a thing that did not ask.
He can smell his prize filled with the seed of another as he is furious.|
|He is more than fucking displeased.|
An Immense One who did not get what he was promised!
Noah had known this being may send forces or even come himself, but he didn’t expect it so soon!
And he...had gone under the assumption that truly, the influence of an Immense One would be diminished in an Elsedimension!
And yet here was one bypassing whatever rulings...and having his power crash into the inhabitants of an Elsedimension.
How?
At this time.
The Elseworld answered!
Every lotus in the crystalline lakes below sealed at once, island-sized petals closing over the basins in domes of blue-gold.
Light ran up the continent-trunked trees.

And from the golden tower at the heart of Vasileia, Provenance Lifeforms rose into the air, the twelve Elders of the lineage at their head, ancient and radiant, the beings Noah had seen ringed around Aurelius before.
He knew their faces.
They rose to defend their lineage, twelve Ages of standing gathered in the torn violet air!
And at their head, Aurelius Vasiliou.

He came up out of the city with his hands still behind his back, and THE Provenance of THE Unfallen Vanguard unfolded around him for the twelfth time in his existence, and the unfolding was a truth stated aloud to the whole Elseworld: that to injure his home, they would have to get through him, that what stands here will still be standing after!
He rose to the level of the enormous face, and he did not flinch from it, and he spoke!
"You did not get what was promised," Aurelius said, and his voice went out steady across the Elseworld.
"My lineage does not hide from a debt.
So name it.
What price is owed, and what price can be paid?
Speak it, and let us settle this as existences that have both stood a long time, and not as a fire and the thing it burns.
We have weavings and karma with other Immense Ones as we can always work-"
HUUM!
The face in the sky interrupted him.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR hears the patriarch’s offer.|
|He finds it quaint and says...you dumb fucking buffoon.|
|Today,|he said, and the pressure gathered as he said it,|I will not collect so much as I will kill.
I don’t give a damn what you are allied with.|
The pressure came down as Aurelius was shocked and horrified!
What!
This was not how things should play out!
An Immense One shouldn’t act so openly and brazenly like this!
What...
BOOM!
It did not strike Aurelius.
It struck the lineage around him, and an Elder with the long white braid... simply became less.
Her light thinned.
Her outline lost its edges.
And then the air where she had been held nothing at all!
Rivers of undeniable power of an Immense One continued to come down in spans of instants!
|Some beings should know their place,| the Collector said, |You have lived a long while beside your betters and mistaken proximity for peerage.
A candle set near a strand of the Weave is still a candle.
It only learns this at the end.|
|Do Provenance Lifeforms no longer fear Immense Ones?
Did you all think we are so passive and laid back, only sending messages?
Is that why you fucked me over?
Did you all forget you sit below us?
You aren’t even some ancient clan as I cannot fathom what gave you the balls, you fucking buffoons. |
HUUM!

Another Provenance Lifeform, a broad quiet Elder, threw himself across the space before Aurelius, arms wide, and took the descending power of THE Immense One and did not make a sound, and went out like a flicker of light, his Provenance extinguished!
|The dignity of some existences cannot be crossed,| the Collector went on, unhurried, as a second Elder guttered and a third roared, the entire Vasiliou Elseworld thrown into panic!
|Mine was crossed by a thief, and I have come to teach the whole of the house that sheltered the drawing of it that some lines, once crossed, do not admit of payment.
Only of correction.|
Aurelius’s Vanguard held, barely as he was ashen while looking at the destruction!
This truly was not what he had envisioned!
He had thought wrong!
Oh, so wrong!

chapters.title: Chapter 5708: Powerless! II
paragraphs: Aurelius stood in the center of the thinning with his Provenance wrapped around him, and the pressure that had unmade three of his Elders met that truth and stopped, exactly as it had stopped eleven times before, and for one breath the Elseworld believed!
Maybe!
The Provenance of their leader was special! It was grand!
They believed.
Then... the Collector pressed as undeniable golden rivers crashed down.

The Provenance bent. From the mountain he rushed from with Thalia, Noah saw it bend, saw the edges of the Unfallen Vanguard curl inward under a weight that did not care what had been declared, and Aurelius Vasiliou, who had never once in eleven stands taken a step backward, took one!
Blood came out of his mouth.
This was an Immense One. His standing and Dimensionality was unfathomably higher as what could the Provenance of a single Provenance Lifeform do?
|Did you believe you had friends among my kind?|
The pressure ground down against the bending truth.

|Did you think, in your long quiet centuries, that you had earned a single ally among us who would stay my hand for the sake of your pleasant little lineage? There are none. Look around your torn sky. None came. None will come.|
|None can save you now.|
POOF!
Across the city, multiple Provenance Lifeforms turned to a puff of red dust as if the defenses of Aurelius did not even exist!
THE Immense One wss killing slowly as he had not even targeted Noah and Thalia yet, seemingly intent on destroying what Thalia knew as home to torment her first.
Noah gazed at the horrific power barreling down as he... did not throw a single attack.

He knew. That was the terrible clarity of it. His Infinite Sanguine Mana would do nothing. His Provenance would do nothing. His Mantle, his Teloi, the whole roaring arsenal of two hundred decillion quarks, all of it was a wrinkle in a cloth, and the cloth was up there deciding where everyone stood, and it would not so much as notice a strike from him.
The gap in Dimensionality was too vast.
He had learned that from a dead man only a short while ago, and he was watching the lesson be proven in the deaths of people who had never harmed him!
To throw power he knew was useless would be a lie. A performance of doing something, so that afterward he could tell himself he had tried. That he was somehow defiant and tyrannical.
So he did the only true thing available.
He took Thalia’s hand, and he moved!
He had a few plans he could initiate as he remembered Atlas’ words to be defiant on set rulings and existence itself. He began to implement a possible plan!

He moved toward the center of the thinning, toward the two figures at the heart of the dying light, and Thalia moved with him, the two of them crossing the burning air of the Elseworld while Provenance Lifeforms guttered on every side, closer, and closer, to Aurelius and Rosalia!
Rosalia had reached her husband.

She had come up through the air with no ceremony at all and taken his weight against her, and his blood ran down the front of her, and he was dazed as he said, "My defenses should have held. They should have...held!"
She held him tight as her Provenance flared and she roared!
The Collector pressed harder, and dozens more Provenance Lifeforms guttered!
Then Thalia forcefully let go of Noah’s hand and went up as she cried while looking at devastation, with Noah following her right after!
She climbed into the torn air in her soaked robe, and she hung between the Collector and her bleeding father, and she spread her arms!

"You came for what is yours!"Her voice carried across the whole dying Elseworld. "It was promised to you by this lineage, and this lineage does not break its word! Look at me, O Collector. I am the debt. I am standing in the open. Take the one who was promised, and leave the ones who only kept the promise!"
He knew she was trying to buy time as...
’My Provenance, please, what can we do?!’
She sent him a mental message thst showed her desperation!
The face in the sky considered her.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR looks at the daughter.|
|You fucking whore. Damaged goods should only feel the pain before they are torn apart soon after. Wait your turn, harlot.|
The pressure resumed. Half the lineage of Provenance Lifeforms was gone now!
Aurelius sagged in his wife’s arms, and Noah looked at all of this with eyes of profound defiance!
He stopped thinking about power.

He had known. He had known the owner of that Provenance would come, and he had spent the intervening time Dual Cultivating and learning to build Elsedimensions and reading about Gu and being taught the difference between depth and magnitude by a dead man, and he had made no plan for this whatsoever because of many assumptions and things he had been told!
It was a horrendous oversight as he assumed and took the word of Aurelius that the could keep an Immense One at bay, and that he knew how an Immense One would react.
They were horribly wrong.
He continued reaching into an obsidian journal and he drove his Provenance into it, hard, into the page of the porch and the two cups, and he called.
A demand for a debt owed, not a request.
"You said I could reach you. I am reaching. I am calling the favor. Intervene in the Vasiliou Elseworld where THE UNPAID COLLECTOR is rampaging now for him to cease animosity against us!"
He sent the message.
And...
The page did not answer.
Above the Elseworld, the pressure found what was left of the golden tower and leaned on it, and the tower fell.
Multiple Vasiliou Provenance Lifeforms continued to rise and circle Aurelius and Rosalia as if they wanted to ensure their leaders did not die, and many of them turned into crimson gold mist!
Noah’s existence seethed as he sent his Provenance into the page again.
Nothing came. No response!
The book stayed shut in his hands while people who had done nothing but keep a promise died in every direction, and Noah, at this moment, truly felt powerless.
Completely!
He had the dead construct of a genius on his Existence and he was traversing THE Chrysalis that some didn’t even know existed, but so what?
Power was power, and his certainly did not match up at this time.
As he gazed at the devastation, a second eye finally opened in the sky.
It bloomed beside the face of the Collector, heavy-lidded, gold, and the dusk that came with it settled over the burning Elseworld and stopped the light from dying any further!
THE REMINISCING WIDOW.

She did not look at Noah as she looked at the Collector, and the Collector looked at her, and the gaze he turned on her was cold enough that the thinning halted on its own, the pressure pausing mid-act while two strands of Immense Ones considered each other across a sky that belonged to neither of them.
They spoke.
Nobody heard any of it, not even Noah.
It moved above him in a register that did not need his hearing, and what came through was the shape of it and not the words.

She said something brief. He said something briefer. She said something that took longer, and the dusk deepened while she said it, and at the end of it the Collector was silent for a moment that the whole Elseworld held its breath inside!
Then the Collector harrumphed.
|THE UNPAID COLLECTOR looks down upon the Vasiliou.|
|A lineage of lamps. Thousands of candles calling themselves a fire, and half of them snuffed by an afternoon of his displeasure. He is embarrassed to have been owed anything by them at all.|
The eye turned. It found Noah and Thalia, and it held both of them at once.
|I am not done with you.|
|Live in fear and doubt. At an undetermined time in the future, I may appear at any moment you hold her, and rip her in half.|
|Any...moment.|
HUUUM!
And in an instant, the face in the sky was gone.

The violet dome came back, torn in a way that would not heal for a long while, and the moss-stone arcs found their gravities again and settled, and across the Elseworld the thinning had stopped, and what it had already taken did not come back.
The second eye lingered.
It looked down at Noah through the dusk, and he could see it clearly, every line of it, and the words came without any halo to carry them, quiet, from everywhere for all those here to see.
|The favor has been paid, O Human Dreamer.|
Then she was gone as well, and the evening she had brought went with her.
Noah did not move for a moment.
Then Thalia came down out of the air past him and went to her parents. Rosalia had lowered Aurelius to a moss-stone arc.
His blood had stopped and his Provenance was gone entirely, not guttering but gone. Fractured. Decimated!
His daughter knelt and put her forehead against his shoulder, and he lifted one shaking hand and set it on her hair.
"Its...okay. Such is existence, my daughter. Such is existence. I am just glad to have protected you from a being like that..."
Aurelius said such words, but Rosalia gazed at Noah hatefully!
Around them, the lineage counted itself, and came up short.
Noah looked at the devastation of Provenance Lifeforms.
The Provenances forever disintegrated while he had been...
Powerless. That was the word, and it was not the same word as outmatched or outnumbered. He had faced things above his weight before and found an angle.
There had been no angle. There had been a wall, and a book that would not open, and seconds!

And when the help had come, it had come in its own time, which was never his. The Widow had arrived when she arrived, spoken as long as she chose, and left when the debt was square by her own accounting, and every second between his call and her eye had been paid for by the lives of many Provenance Lifeforms.
That was what relying on another meant. They came in their own time. They did things in their own way. The bill for the difference went to whoever was standing closest, and today it had gone to many!
He had assumed far too many things that turned out to be wrong.
He needed to do things differently. He needed to question everything he heard or thought he knew as there were no absolutes.

Noah stood in the decimated centerpoint of The Vasiliou Lineage as he stood tall while many accusing faces picked each other out of the rubble, their distate and hatred showing clearly whenever they glanced at him!

There was no tyranny to show or speech to give as this...was merely a glimpse of the power of Immense Ones and a heavy defeat that let it be known clearly...whatever rules others believed, Immense Ones did not have to abide by them.
