chapters.title: Chapter 5709: Sonder I
paragraphs: Noah looked at the devastation, and the devastation looked back through a hundred grieving faces.

Aurelius sat on the moss-stone arc with his wife’s arms around him and his daughter’s forehead against his shoulder, and his blood had dried on all three of them, and his Vanguard was gone in a manner that Noah suspected would not return in a lifetime.
He lifted his head. He found Noah across the wreckage of his own city, and then he gave one heavy nod.

"I did not know you had the pull that you showed,"Aurelius said. His voice had lost the steadiness it wore in the sky, and he did not try to put it back. "Thank you. For spending a favor of an Immense One to end this."
Noah said nothing. There was nothing to say that would not sound like taking credit for a rescue that had cost this man half his lineage.

"It was I who made the deal, ages ago, to give my daughter away."Aurelius looked down at Thalia’s radiant hair under his hand. "So I cannot lay this at your feet. Your intrusion took a choice out of my hands. The choice of cowardice, which I could never make myself take, because I was afraid of exactly this, the extermination of everything that carries my name. You forced us to the place I had spent an Age avoiding. A price was paid for it. But I..."
His voice trailed. He looked out at the pale places in the air where his Elders had been.
"But I..."
The words did not finish.
And Noah’s eyes flashed with the brilliant light of infinity, and everything went grey and still.
He had not frozen them. He could not have frozen most of them; a great many of the Provenance Lifeforms in this ruined city were his betters in every number that could be measured.

He had only stretched his own perception toward infinity, so that a single instant opened out and out, an instant with no far wall, and he stood inside it alone with a failure that was not going anywhere.
His eyes pulsed.
He entered the reverie, that unique state where boundless epiphanies bloomed in every direction at once and a thought could be turned over ten thousand times before the next instant arrived.
And his eyes, which existence had learned to read as tyranny, held something else in the grey stillness.
Sadness.
It was only human.

Because in the stretched instant he was thinking of Eon. Of how he had taken her as his woman, and how her home and her people had been destroyed, and how that had become one more weaving in the great wake he dragged behind himself. And now Thalia. He had taken her too, this woman who had crossed time itself to reach him, who had torn her own Provenance to arrive, who had sat in his spring and named every danger ahead of them in careful order.
She had warned him. She had done nothing but warn him and help him and love him, and here was her home, and here were her people, thinning into the air while she knelt in the blood of her father.
He could argue that he had made no promises. It would even be true. He had promised the Vasiliou nothing except an errand and a bargain.
He still felt he had broken something. He still felt he had let them down. The technicality did not reach the feeling.
He rarely felt this way. His whole identity was pitched at one weaving, and the weaving was tyranny. Majesty!
He spoke the same to Provenance Lifeforms who could unmake him as he spoke to the frightened and the small. He had stood before Immense Ones and not bent a word of himself.
He was fearful, and he was fearless, both at once, and he had built an entire existence on the certainty that this was enough.
None of it had done a single thing today. In the end he had been reduced to hammering on a book and begging another to do what he could not.

He looked at the faces. Thalia’s, hollowed out. Rosalia’s, turned on him with a hatred that had earned every degree of itself. Aurelius’s, solemn and unfinished. And his existence buzzed, and a realization came up out of the grey stillness and would not go back down.
He was the protagonist.

He had named himself that. He had spoken the Letter and taken the Aura and built an edge over existence out of the claim that the story bent toward him. And it was true, and it had served him, and it had also let him believe, in a place beneath thought, that the other figures in his eras were figures. Extras. Supporting shapes. Weight and texture in his story.
They were not!
Every one of them was the protagonist of a story that had been running long before Noah Osmont arrived in it.

Aurelius carried an Age of history in which Noah was one recent Chapter, and not the first hard one. The people going out like lamps around him had each held a whole existence, vivid and detailed and entirely their own, in which they were the center and he was the stranger who arrived one afternoon and changed everything and would leave.
He wanted to be grand. He wanted to be immense. He had never once questioned thr cost!

But it should not be built on the ruin of existences that had done nothing to him. He had his life, and the ones he had chosen to protect. They had theirs. Every form of existence was exactly as complex as his own, as full, as central to itself, and he had been walking through all of it as scenery.
HUUM!

The light in his eyes grew, and it did not lose the sorrow, and deep in his existence THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer cried out with a solemnity he had never heard from it and surged like a vast sea rising past its shore.
Existence was vast and complex.
And every single lifeform within it was equally vast, and equally complex, and equally the center of its own turning.
|A fundamental change has occurred within THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer.|
|You have long dreamed. You believed you were the one who dreams. Today you have understood that you dream among decillions who dream as vividly as you.|
|THE DREAM STATE OF SONDER has been attained.|

|SONDER: the sudden realization that every stranger you pass is living a life as vivid, complex, and detailed as your own. It is the moment you understand that you may not be the main character of existence, but a background figure in decillions of other stories unfolding around you.|

He found Noah across the wreckage of his own city, and then he gave one heavy nod.

His voice had lost the steadiness it wore in the sky, and he did not try to put it back.
"Thank you.
For spending a favor of an Immense One to end this."
Noah said nothing.
There was nothing to say that would not sound like taking credit for a rescue that had cost this man half his lineage.
"It was I who made the deal, ages ago, to give my daughter away."Aurelius looked down at Thalia’s radiant hair under his hand.
"So I cannot lay this at your feet.
Your intrusion took a choice out of my hands.
The choice of cowardice, which I could never make myself take, because I was afraid of exactly this, the extermination of everything that carries my name.
You forced us to the place I had spent an Age avoiding.
A price was paid for it.
But I..."
His voice trailed.
He looked out at the pale places in the air where his Elders had been.
"But I..."
The words did not finish.
And Noah’s eyes flashed with the brilliant light of infinity, and everything went grey and still.
He had not frozen them.
He could not have frozen most of them; a great many of the Provenance Lifeforms in this ruined city were his betters in every number that could be measured.

He had only stretched his own perception toward infinity, so that a single instant opened out and out, an instant with no far wall, and he stood inside it alone with a failure that was not going anywhere.
His eyes pulsed.
He entered the reverie, that unique state where boundless epiphanies bloomed in every direction at once and a thought could be turned over ten thousand times before the next instant arrived.
And his eyes, which existence had learned to read as tyranny, held something else in the grey stillness.
Sadness.
It was only human.
Because in the stretched instant he was thinking of Eon.
Of how he had taken her as his woman, and how her home and her people had been destroyed, and how that had become one more weaving in the great wake he dragged behind himself.
And now Thalia.
He had taken her too, this woman who had crossed time itself to reach him, who had torn her own Provenance to arrive, who had sat in his spring and named every danger ahead of them in careful order.
She had warned him.
She had done nothing but warn him and help him and love him, and here was her home, and here were her people, thinning into the air while she knelt in the blood of her father.
He could argue that he had made no promises.
It would even be true.
He had promised the Vasiliou nothing except an errand and a bargain.
He still felt he had broken something.
He still felt he had let them down.
The technicality did not reach the feeling.
He rarely felt this way.
His whole identity was pitched at one weaving, and the weaving was tyranny.
Majesty!
He spoke the same to Provenance Lifeforms who could unmake him as he spoke to the frightened and the small.
He had stood before Immense Ones and not bent a word of himself.
He was fearful, and he was fearless, both at once, and he had built an entire existence on the certainty that this was enough.
None of it had done a single thing today.
In the end he had been reduced to hammering on a book and begging another to do what he could not.
He looked at the faces.
Thalia’s, hollowed out.
Rosalia’s, turned on him with a hatred that had earned every degree of itself.
Aurelius’s, solemn and unfinished.
And his existence buzzed, and a realization came up out of the grey stillness and would not go back down.
He was the protagonist.
He had named himself that.
He had spoken the Letter and taken the Aura and built an edge over existence out of the claim that the story bent toward him.
And it was true, and it had served him, and it had also let him believe, in a place beneath thought, that the other figures in his eras were figures.
Extras.
Supporting shapes.
Weight and texture in his story.
They were not!
Every one of them was the protagonist of a story that had been running long before Noah Osmont arrived in it.
Aurelius carried an Age of history in which Noah was one recent Chapter, and not the first hard one.

The people going out like lamps around him had each held a whole existence, vivid and detailed and entirely their own, in which they were the center and he was the stranger who arrived one afternoon and changed everything and would leave.
He wanted to be grand.
He wanted to be immense.
He had never once questioned thr cost!
But it should not be built on the ruin of existences that had done nothing to him.
He had his life, and the ones he had chosen to protect.
They had theirs.
Every form of existence was exactly as complex as his own, as full, as central to itself, and he had been walking through all of it as scenery.
HUUM!

The light in his eyes grew, and it did not lose the sorrow, and deep in his existence THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer cried out with a solemnity he had never heard from it and surged like a vast sea rising past its shore.
Existence was vast and complex.
And every single lifeform within it was equally vast, and equally complex, and equally the center of its own turning.
|A fundamental change has occurred within THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer.|
|You have long dreamed.
You believed you were the one who dreams.
Today you have understood that you dream among decillions who dream as vividly as you.|
|THE DREAM STATE OF SONDER has been attained.|
|SONDER: the sudden realization that every stranger you pass is living a life as vivid, complex, and detailed as your own.
It is the moment you understand that you may not be the main character of existence, but a background figure in decillions of other stories unfolding around you.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5710: Sonder II
paragraphs: |THE Dream State of Sonder elevates the Mantle of THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist. It grants a gaze of empathy and understanding: you perceive the dreams and the hopes of those you look upon. You are the Human Dreamer. You are not the only one who dreams in existence. You may now perceive and draw not only from your own dreams, but from the dreams of all who dream around you.|
|PROVENANCE has crossed the 100 threshold, passing into THE SEAM, into THE INEFFABLE VERSE, and arrived at 110.|
|VERITAS has advanced to 105.|
|PONDUS has advanced to 101.|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI has advanced to 125.|
Noah stood in the greying instant with his existence remade a little, and his eyes shone with endless blue and gold, and the shine remained a solemn thing.

He had dreams. Others had dreams too. As THE Human Dreamer he could dream grandly enough for himself and everyone he loved, and he could do it without grinding the dreams of the uninvolved to dust beneath him. That was possible.
And if he met a being who meant to spend its dream on the destruction of his, then of course he would answer it without mercy, because protecting what was his had never once required apology.
His hand closed into a fist.
He looked up, and the brilliance in his eyes grew brighter.

Then he looked at the lineage around him, the Provenance Lifeforms who had lost everything, drifting through the ruin of a city that had stood since before the current arrangement of things, and he wanted to offer them somewhere.

Somewhere an Immense One could not reach. He had a Realm, and a first Elsedimension folded into it, built with no authority an architect could ride, and he wanted to open it and say come, be safe, no strand of the Weave will ever touch you here.
He was not sure he could say it truthfully.

Because an Immense One had just reached into the Vasiliou Elsedimension and expressed his full power inside a place that was supposed to blunt him, and Noah did not know how. If a strand of THE Immense One could bypass one Elsedimension, could it bypass his? Could it walk into the Realm and do to his mother and his son and his people what the Collector had just done here?
He did not know!

And ever since he had built his first Elsedimension, he had given THE Infiniverse the order to begin turning the whole of herself into one, an Elsedimension entire, a home no other existence could enter. He had believed that made his people safe. He had believed it as firmly as he had believed Aurelius could hold an Immense One at bay.
Assumptions had killed today. He would ask Atlas, because he could not afford one more thing he merely hoped was true.
He drew a breath in the stretched grey instant, and he let THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer open the whole of the way, and Sonder woke behind his eyes.
The grey filled with gold.

Around every single being in the ruined city, a swirling cloud of golden dream turned slowly, one for each of them, and no two were alike, and the whole devastated Elseworld became a sky of quiet private dreaming.
He looked at Thalia.
|THALIA VASILIOU dreams: to be believed, once, by the one she crossed time to reach. To not be a warning he resents. To sit at a table that is set for the living. To protect and to prosper.|
Noah’s chest tightened, and he made himself keep looking.
He looked at Aurelius, and at Rosalia holding him.
|AURELIUS and ROSALIA VASILIOU dream: that the name survives them. That the daughter they bargained away was worth the wound it cost to let her go.|
|Note: any weaving you contribute to the dreams of those you perceive feeds back into THE Human Dream. The grander the dream you help carry, the grander the return to your own.|
Noah looked at them all, one at a time, through the gold, and he inscribed the afternoon into his existence.
He had made no promises. He would hold to that, since it was true.

But he could move differently. He could carry his Dreams and his Infinity across existence without leaving only apocalypse behind him, without decimating every story he happened to walk through on his way to being grand.
The grey released.
Color and sound crashed back into the ruined Elseworld, and Aurelius, mid-sentence, found the end of it at last.
"But I...am glad," the old man said quietly, "that my daughter is alive."
Noah finally spoke.
"I should have made precautions much earlier."He looked at the old man across the ruin. "I am sorry."

Aurelius only smiled at that, sadly, and looked around at the pale places in the air and the fallen tower and the survivors moving through the rubble counting the ones who were not moving through it with them. He did not argue the apology and he did not accept it.
Noah looked at Thalia.
She was tending her father, her Provenance flowing into him in a steady warm current, and her face had changed. The hollowness was gone out of it. What had replaced it was firm!
Before he could call out to her, she spoke.

"An Immense One wanted my Provenance." She did not look up from her father as she said it. "One of them looked across all of existence and decided that what runs in a Vasiliou was worth crossing a sky to take."
Her hand pressed flat against Aurelius’s chest, and her Provenance sank deeper into him.

"So I will use it. I will use it to change the Provenance of my lineage." Her eyes came up now, and they burned. "I will make them all into Elselifeforms, and I will understand, down to the root, exactly why a being like that wanted this badly enough to burn my home for it. If we are worth taking, then we are worth becoming something that cannot be taken."
Noah gave a light nod at that.
"I cannot make any promises right now," he said.

"But I am looking into a bastion. A domain that something like THE UNPAID COLLECTOR should not be able to reach into. As soon as I have confirmation, real confirmation, I will tell you. It should be possible to move the whole of the Vasiliou Elsedimension somewhere safer."

Thalia looked at him, and her eyes shone with a sudden immense brilliance, because she knew exactly what place he meant. She had walked its blue-gold hills. She had asked him, once, to take her to see his mother in it!
She simply nodded, and turned back to her father, and let her Provenance flow.
Noah’s existence pulsed.
And far away, in a place outside the weavings of time, another of his bodies stopped walking.

chapters.title: Chapter 5711: Questions and Answers
paragraphs: <THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering>

The silk fell around him and the kaleidoscopic nebulas turned in the vastness, and Noah stood alone in the deep drift of THE Chrysalis with dreamy light burning bright behind his eyes, brighter than it had ever burned.
An infinite dream filled with boundless complexities seemed to be waking!
He had questions. Today had bought them at a terrible price, and he intended to spend every single one as his mind calculated the bloody ruins of the Vasiliou Elsemountain.
"How could an Immense One exert their power inside an Elsedimension?"
He spoke the words into the illusory ring resting against his finger.
|-0.1 PROVENANCE ESSENCE|

"They are built to reject the authority of such beings,"Noah continued. "That was the entire point of their architecture, you told me so yourself. And yet I just watched one reach into the Vasiliou Elsedimension and impose himself without the slightest trouble. Lifeforms of higher Dimensionality than mine were ended with a tap, inside a place that was supposed to blunt him. I only survived because he wanted to save me and my love for last, as cruelty. Had he chosen to kill instead of to torment, that body of mine would have collapsed, or worse. So I need to understand clearly. What parameters actually make an Elsedimension keep an Immense One out?"
The illusory band warmed against his flesh.
The voice rolled out from the records-cluster, carrying that sharp, familiar arrogance that refused to bend to anything in the continuum.

|The largest protection an Elsedimension offers is not a wall. It is that the place cannot easily be found by an Immense One simply deciding to look for it. They are strands of the Weave. Their sight runs along the cloth, and a strand cannot look at what is woven into a seam it does not know about.|
|Unless.|

|Unless that strand has been there before. If an Immense One was ever inside an Elsedimension, if it was ever invited, ever allowed to cross the threshold even once, then it left seeds of its own weavings behind. They always do. They cannot help it, any more than you can walk through wet sand without leaving prints. An Elsedimension that has admitted an Immense One is a useless Elsedimension. The authority has already permeated it. The door was opened from the inside and it does not close again.|
|So. That Collector had been to the Vasiliou Elsedimension before, or something of his had, or the lineage let something in they should not have. Ask them.|

|There are no absolutes. But a properly designed Elsedimension, one that has never once let an architect past its door, will do its job. Yours has never admitted one. Keep it that way and it is the safest ground in existence for a being of your fold.|
The answer came as he thought about it, and them he set it aside to confirm with his own eyes before he built a single plan on it.
"The Elsedimension Ring," Noah said, letting another thread of authority bleed into the band. "The first thing you are guiding me to build. What is it actually capable of?"
|-0.1 PROVENANCE ESSENCE|
"Because I am thinking about survival at this moment."Noah went on, his pupils reflecting the falling silk.
"Survival, against things tremendously stronger than me. Will this ring let me do that?"
|Now you are thinking like a man who intends to live long enough to become dangerous.|
The records pulsed with clear, steady warmth as Atlas continued.

|What I engineered, and what I can teach you to engineer, does a great many things. An Elsedimension Ring, designed well, can be set to sense the incoming animosity of a specific enemy, an Immense One you have marked, and the instant it feels that intent turn toward you, it warps your entire existence into an Elsedimension elsewhere before the blow arrives. You are simply not where the strike falls. You were never there.|

|You can build in other functions besides. A masking so that certain sights slide off you. A warning that wakes before the danger does. A store of ground you can retreat into and seal. A ring is not one tool, O Human Dreamer. And a ring is only one of many things.|
The dreamy light of Sonder turned behind Noah’s eyes as he listened, absorbing the mechanics without distraction.

|A weaker existence can move across an existence full of stronger ones and not die. It is done. It has always been done. It is perilous, and it is adversity without end, and it is possible. There are ways.|

|The first is to not be found. Depth over magnitude. Walk and hide where the great strands do not think to look, and let the mighty thunder past overhead while you go quietly about becoming. Most who hunt you cannot strike what they cannot perceive.|

|The second is to not be worth it. Make yourself a poor bargain. Be difficult, be defended, be the kind of prize that costs more to take than it returns, and a great many predators will decide you are not worth the afternoon. The Collector came for the Vasiliou because they were cheap. Do not be cheap.|

|The third is to not be reachable. Build the ground I am teaching you to build, and keep it clean of every seed, and when the sky turns against you, be elsewhere before it finishes turning. A being that cannot be cornered cannot be killed at leisure, and leisure is how the mighty prefer to kill.|
|Use all three at once and you will cross the whole of existence with monsters on every side and arrive at the far end still breathing.|

The nebulas turned overhead as the silk fell across Noah’s bare shoulders. He took the three principles into himself, weighing each against the brutality he had witnessed, and he did not let a single one become an absolute.
|And here is the last of it, Dreamer, and then I will let you get back to nearly being eaten by insects.|
The voice slowed slightly, carrying the unhurried weight of an ancient memory.

|You will not hide forever. That is not what any of this is for. You hide from a thing today so that you can grow, and you grow so that tomorrow you hide from something a fold higher, and one day you look back and find that the being you fled from an Age ago is a being you can now look in the eyes and feel nothing at all. No pressure. No fear. Just a strand, standing there, no larger to you than you once were to it.|
|Anything is possible in existence. I have watched it happen. I made some of it happen. And then... I stopped being able to, which is a story for a course you are not ready for.|
|Now. Go find a Common Gu that does not run, and let us build you a workshop for your finger.|
Noah stood a moment longer in the falling silk.

The light of dreams burned brighter in his eyes, Sonder and defiance and a cold new patience all at once, and he turned, moving deeper into THE Chrysalis to build the thing that would keep the people he loved out of a sky’s reach.

chapters.title: Chapter 5712: A Clash of Dreams! I
paragraphs: Noah traversed in silence for a while as he continued to think of many things, and after a few minutes, he finally came across a Gu Lifeform in this region of predominant weavings of Dreams.
The Common Dream Gu was the type that did not even run.

It hung in a pocket of still silk where three strands had tangled into a kind of nest, moon-small at this range, its translucent body heaving slow, dream-weather drifting golden through its interior. Its many eyes were half-lidded. It was not fleeing and it was not feeding. It was simply there, doing the one thing its whole existence was made to do, and Noah stood in the drift a short distance off and looked at it with eyes in which Sonder had not once dimmed since it woke.
He saw its dream.
A single cloud of gold turned around the creature, slow, and inside the cloud was the dream, and Noah looked into it and found it so... simple.

It dreamed of warmth. It dreamed of the silk being soft. It dreamed, in the wordless way of a thing that had never held a word, of drifting somewhere the strands fell thick and the dream-weather was sweet, and being left alone to drift there. That was it!
That was the entire interior life of a lifeform that read past a hundred in every attribute a panel could measure. It wanted to be warm. It wanted to be left alone.

Noah found, standing there, that he did not want to break it. But...he would anyway. He needed a Common Gu, and this was one, and he had crossed out of the weavings of time and let himself be eaten to reach a place where he could take it.
In the end, Existence still held natural selection as one still had to do what they had to do.
It was like a human empathizing with the chicken he raised in a chicken coop. He could do it, but when he was eating that chicken soup...that soup tasted damn good.
He raised his hand, and THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer gathered behind his eyes, ready to reach into the little creature’s dream and fold it gently shut and carry it with him!
But then, his Provenance buzzed as he felt something.
"That one is ours."
The voice came down through the silk.
Noah did not turn at once. He let his hand lower, and he let the reverie in his eyes hold, and only then did he look.
They came out of the deep nebulas in a wedge.

Nine riders, titanic, each the height of a small mountain, carved of bronze and stone. Their Steeds burned, whole and blazing, First Causes pouring light through the hide of a white stag whose antlers held Observable Existences in their tines, a golden six-legged serpent, a plated beast whose every plate was a continent, a plain horse that was somehow worse than all the rest!
And dragged behind them on obsidian rope that burned with an Immense One’s borrowed power came three bound Dream Gu, their tentacles limp, their Dreams gone dark.

At the head, on the white stag, sat the largest of them. Crimson eyes in a face of old bronze. She looked down at Noah, and she looked at the little untaken Gu drifting in its nest, and her mouth curved.
"You have good eyes,"she said. "You found a Dream Gu, but we will take it off your hands."
Noah looked up at her, and then he looked at all of them, one after another.
Golden clouds of dreams gathered around each of them.
He read three of their dreams while she waited.

The leader dreamed of a nod. Not from anyone. From an Immense One. A single acknowledgment from a Father who had bred her line for exactly this and had never once looked directly at any of them, and she did what she was told so that ultimately she hoped she would finally earn her the tilt of a head she had wanted.
The Descendant on the golden serpent dreamed smaller and uglier:of the leader failing, so that he might be first to bring the catches home.

The one on the plain horse did not dream of the Father at all. It dreamed of the day the hunts would end. It did not believe the day would come. It dreamed of it anyway, quietly, and had for a very long time.
Noah took all of that in!

"You have a great many of those already," Noah said. He nodded at the three bound Gu without heat. "Three on the rope, and there are more out there in the silk than the one drifting between us. This region of the chrysalis is full of dreams. Go find another."
His voice was calm.

"I do not want a conflict with the First Borns of a Father I have no quarrel with...well, for the most part. I have had a long day. Someone I hold dear watched her home burn not long ago, and I would rather not add much more today. So take the good advice a stranger is giving you for free. Find another Gu. Leave this one, and leave me, and we both go home with what we came for."
For a moment the silk held its silence.
Then the leader laughed!
It was the laugh of a titan being lectured by a candle.

"You speak very well for a thing with no aura at all," she said."I have been looking at you since we arrived, little one, and there is nothing under your skin. No Cause. No standing that reaches me. You dress like something and weigh like nothing. Who do you even descend from? No matter."

She leaned forward over the stag’s blazing neck. "That Gu is ours because we say it is ours, and there is no one here to say otherwise but you, and you are no one. Step back into your silk. Father enjoys his dreams, and we have some more to catch before we can go."
She did not step back. None of them stepped back!
The nine titans and their burning Steeds stayed, and the little Dream Gu drifted on in its nest between the two of them, warm, wanting to be left alone.
Noah looked at their panels while she spoke,.
|FIRST BORN OF THE SLEEPLESS FIEND (×9)|
|Attribute range across the party: 101 to 130.|
|Depth: THE SEAM. Every rider a Cause-bearing Descendant of undying line.|
|PROVENANCE: 0. None among them holds a single point.|
Every one of them read higher than he did.

Several of them, in raw magnitude, could break him. And not one of them held a single point of Provenance, because they were spoken things, sentences with a bloodline, and a sentence does not generate its own aim.
They had been given everything they were. They had made none of it!
He, standing there weighing nothing, had made all of himself.
And every one of them held a dream that wanted to end his, so that a hunt could be completed and a head might tilt.

Noah felt the old thing rise in him, the tyranny, the greed, the cold amusement at the mighty taking themselves so seriously, and he did not fight it down. Sonder had not replaced it. Sonder had only aimed it.

These were not bystanders drifting through their own quiet lives.These were nine dreams that had looked at his dream and decided to grind it under, and against that, protecting what was his had never once required an apology.
Even if they were the Protagonists of their own story...he was THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist!

He wanted to see. He wanted to see his one dream, the dream of a human who had decided to be grand without leaving only ruin behind him, clash against nine older dreams that were certain of themselves, and he wanted to find out whose held!
It would be arduous. Nine titans who each outweighed him, their Steeds burning, an Immense One’s rope in their hands. He might bleed for it. He intended to persevere and come out standing anyway!

Noah let his hand rise once more, and this time THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer did not gather gently. It surged, blue and gold and vast, and the light of dreams in his eyes blazed until the nine riders and their burning mounts threw shadows across the falling silk.

"Here is where we are," Noah said. "I gave you the door. You looked at it, and you decided I was no one, and you kept your feet where they are. That was your choice, and I am a great believer in letting existences make their own choices, even the wrong ones."
The little Dream Gu, sensing at last that its warm nest had become the center of something, stirred, and began, slowly, to wake.
"You came here to catch dreams for a Father who does not look at you."Noah’s blue-gold gaze swept the wedge, and stopped on the leader, on the crimson eyes and the dream of a nod behind them.
"Let me show you what it looks like when a dream refuses to be caught."
HUUM!
The silk stopped falling.

Every strand in the tangled nest and for a great span around it halted in the air, and the golden dream-weather inside the little Gu flared, and inside Noah’s eyes decillions of dreams that were not his own began, faintly, to turn, because Sonder was awake and he was no longer the only dreamer he could reach!
The nine First Borns felt the place change, and for the first time the leader’s mouth was not a smile as she frowned.
And this insignificantly small region of THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering filled with the concepts of Dreams faced a war of dreams!
The leader did not wait. Her crimson eyes flared. The white stag’s antlers blazed, every Observable Existence turning in its tines flaring with them.
"Voss. Kara. Take this fucker from both sides," she said. "The rest, close the surrounding existence. Leave him a mouth to talk with and nothing else."
The surroundings broke into motion, and the quiet nest of dreams became a killing floor!

The Descendant on the golden serpent came in from the left, and the one on the winged silver Steed dropped from above, and the space between them was where Noah stood, and it should have been the end of a small thing with no aura!

The serpent-rider’s palm opened, and from it poured white. THE Argent Loom! One of the oldest authorities in existence came off him in a woven flood, bright thin strands lashing out to bind an enemy and hold it still for the killing!
It closed on nothing.
Because Noah was no longer there to close on.

He had begun before the leader finished her order. He had learned today, at a terrible price, what became of a man who let stronger things set the tempo, and so he had not waited to be attacked. In the Infinity of a Dreamer’s stretched instant he had closed his eyes and dreamed one thing, whole and simple.
He dreamed he could not be found.
THE PRECEPT OF THE WAKING DREAM woke!

In the dream he had no aura, no weight, no place an eye could come to rest, and because he was the Human Dreamer and the dream was his own existence, it became true before the Loom could finish closing!
The white flood passed through empty silk.
|You dream yourself unseen. To perceivers below your Dreams, you are not there. The dream holds while it is not contested by a higher sight.|
The serpent-rider, Voss, drew his Loom back, confused, and the winged Steed’s rider landed in the space where the enemy had been and found nothing there to land on.
"Where did it go..." Voss started.
Noah was already under his mount.
He crossed the region unseen, past both riders still searching the air, and came up beneath the belly of the golden six-legged serpent.

He reached into it, a hand wrapped in blue and gold, and closed his fingers around one of the First Causes seated blazing in its organs, and he distilled it. He drew the essence sideways out of true, taking the taste and leaving the fruit, and the Cause guttered!
He was very proficient in Causes, after all.
The serpent screamed and buckled at one leg as a sunrise went dark inside it!

Voss felt his mount fail under him and could not see why. He hauled on the reins and wheeled, Loom spilling uselessly from his hand, eyes raking the silk. "Hey, this fucker is invisible even though his Dimensionality should not be higher than ours! Are they actually a Gu? They could be a rare Gu!"
"No way! Spread your immensity out and do not let anything near you!"The leader snapped.
It was good advice, but till not enough!

Because Noah had crossed to the next one. He slid a dreaming hand between two continent-plates of the great plated beast and gripped the Cause beneath and drew, and a plate went cold and grey and split.

He was gone up the side of the black stone quadruped before the beast finished stumbling, and he guttered the molten Cause running down its side, and it folded onto its own legs with a groan that shook the nebulas.
Three mounts crippled. Not one Descendant had seen him do it!
They were beings of immense weight and no sight past their own dreams!
And while he worked, he understood something.
He was asking himself how he should fight with his strongest points while ensuring no time for the Descendants to even unleash their true power.
And the pieces were clicking!
He was inside their perception. He was a dream moving through the place they lived. And a dream that could move through their perception could reach the thing at the center of it.
He had read their dreams already. The leader’s nod. Voss’s small ugly hunger. The plain-horse rider’s quiet wish that the hunts would end.
He had only read them.
What if he wrote?
Noah rose out of his crouch still unseen, and let a portion of his Provenance bloom, and reached, not for a Cause this time, but for the golden cloud of dream turning slow around the leader.
He controlled his Provenance like an extension of his existence to interfere with that cloud as why shouldn’t he be able to manipulate the dreams of others?!
And he began to dream her a different dream.
|You reach into the Existential Narrative of another existence through its dream. THE Mantle of THE Meta-Fictional Protagonist stirs.|
The leader went rigid on the white stag as her high Dimensionality felt something!
She felt something reach into the oldest quiet place in her, where her hopes and dreams lived, and she felt something changing!
She wheeled the stag around, crimson eyes wide, and for the first time there was something in her face that was not contempt.
Was this fucker actually a Gu?!
Her body illuminated with Dimensionality as her Intent filled with THE Argent Loom and an ancient Tongue erupted around her like a storm!
"Get the fuck out of my Existence!"
HUUM!
"You dream of recognized," Noah said, and his voice came from everywhere.
"From a Father who has never once looked at you. I have seen it."
He tightened his grip on the dream.
"That is a sad thing to be. Let me change it for you."
He began to write. Into the cloud of her he wrote a new past, one where the recognition had already come, long ago, and meant nothing, and she had felt nothing when it did!
He wrote it backward into the records of her, so that it had always been so!
And the leader’s existence lurched, because the dream that had shaped her every action was being told it had never been true, and at the edges, her records began to disagree with themselves!
She became furious when she felt this!
"Enough."
WUUa
She reached for something!
She drew a sword!
It came off her Existence in a wash of white and crimson, long and plain and terrible, and the instant it cleared the sheath the whole region of the Chrysalis changed its weight.

The silk stopped falling. The three bound Dream Gu on the ropes went rigid. And Noah, unseen in his dream, felt his imperceptibility strain for the first time, because the thing she had drawn was searching for him with a sight that was not eyes.
|WARNING.|

|The blade carries Existential Narrative not its own. Slivers of the Narrative of THE Sleepless Fiend are woven into its edge. It perceives across folds. Your unseen dream is no longer certainly unseen.|
The leader turned the blade, and its edge caught a light that came from nowhere in this place, and her lurching existence steadied itself on the weapon like a hand on a rail.
A sliver of brilliance of an Immense One flared as all of surrounding existence shuddered and cried!
She swung, at a pocket of empty silk, at nothing that anyone could see, and yet she still found her target as... it caught Noah full across the chest!

"Kill it before it disappears again! Whether its a Gu or not doesn’t matter!" the leader roared. "It cannot hide from the blade! Move!"

Voss, whose golden Steed was crippled but whose arm was not, hurled a spear of woven Argent Loom and Dimensionality, and Noah twisted in the air as this sharp Dimensionality tore through his shoulder instead of his heart.
Others came as Noah closed his eyes and imagined a dream where dodged every threst coming towards him!
It was an an infinite dream of THE Human Dreamer as he felt like he could do it endlessly!
The old assumption tried to rise in him, the one that whispered the story bent his way, that he was the protagonist and would be fine.
He srifled it.

He caught himself against a drifting continent of dead chitin, bleeding from chest and shoulder, and he thought about the one thing that mattered, which was the thing he had felt in the instant before the sword landed.
Her records had lurched.

For one moment, before she drew an Immense One’s power, the leader’s existence had shuddered, because the dream he was writing and the records she was built of had stopped matching. He had felt a Descendant’s foundation tremble because a story it stood on had been told a different ending!
That was the solution!
|The blade will find you whenever you are perceived. You cannot out-power it. But its bearer stands on a dream, and you are the thing that writes dreams. You can fight the war you can win.|
Noah stopped trying to survive the sword.
He stopped dodging toward safety, stopped answering their tempo, and hung in the burning air, bleeding, letting them come, because the fight they thought they were in was not the fight anymore!
He spread his hand across the nine dreams turning in his Sonder-sight, and he wrote into all of them at once.
The leader’s blade came for him even as he did it, and it hit, and he let it hit, taking the wound across his ribs and keeping his hand open!
Into Voss he wrote that he had betrayed the leader long ago, been caught, and been forgiven, and that the forgiveness was the most humiliating thing that had ever happened to him!
Voss’s raging storm of Dimensionality dropped from his hand mid-throw as a shame that had never occurred crashed down through him.
Into the winged rider he wrote that its wings had always been a lie, that it had never truly flown, that every flight had been a dream it told itself, and the rider faltered in the air!

Into the plain-horse rider he wrote that the hunts had already ended, ages past, and that everything since had been a dream it was having as it died, and the rider went still and silent and stopped fighting entirely, staring at a nothing it had privately expected for a very long time.
And into the leader, into the woman with an Immense One’s power in her hand and his blood on her edge, he wrote the cruelest true thing he had found in her.

That her Father had looked at her once, directly and had given her his Recognition an Age ago, and that she had been too busy hunting to notice, and had missed the only thing she had ever wanted while it happened, and could never have it again!
He wrote it into her Dreams as a thing that had always been true.
And the Descendants of THE Sleepless Fiend roared as their Existence fought against their Dreams!

They shockingly began to come apart! The dreams Noah had written and the records they were made of could not both stand, and no existence can hold two truths at its own foundation, and the disagreement ran outward from the center of each of them, a crack finding every edge at once!
Effectively, he had fucked around with their Trueness as for beings of high Dimensionality, their Trueness was critical!
Atlas had talked about DEPTH, MAGNITUDE, and AGREEMENT when it came to the power of lifeforms.
The Depths were their Dimensionality as theirs were higher than his, and Agreement with existence was heavy, but theit MAGNITUDE...he fractured it inside out.
|You are overwriting the Existential Narrative of nine Descendants. Their dreams and their records no longer agree. An existence at war with its own story cannot hold its shape.|

Voss clutched his head and howled at a betrayal that had never happened. The winged rider forgot the lie of its wings and fell. The plain-horse rider dismounted, slowly, and sat down in the silk, certain it was already dead and merely waiting to notice.
And the leader dropped the sword.

The weapon carrying a sliver of power of an Immense One fell through the silk and its terrible song went quiet, because the hand that held it no longer knew whether it had ever wanted the thing it was fighting for!
She clutched at her own chest and found there the memory Noah had written, of having had it, of having missed it, and her crimson eyes went wide and wet and utterly lost!
"I just wanted him to look at me...did I really miss it? Did I truly?!"

A crack ran up through the old bronze of her body. The white stag beneath her screamed as its rider’s Narrative tore, and the whole wedge was breaking now, nine titans going mad as their records ripped away from one another, madness blooming in a place made of the very concept of dreams.
Storms of Argent Loom and typhoons of Dimensionality began to rage around them as weaker Lifeforms would be shredded if they came nearby!
Noah hung above them, bleeding from three wounds as he did not derive any pleasure from this!

A day ago he might have enjoyed it. Today, with Sonder awake in him, he saw each of the nine fully as he unmade them, saw the whole vivid interior of nine existences that had each stood at the center of a long story, and he broke them anyway!
Because they had opposed his grsnd and infinite dream, and he had promised himself he would come out standing.
But even now, his eyes flashed coldly as he thought about everything.
It was about their Father.
These were the First Borns of THE Sleepless Fiend, one of Those Who Remain. They could see many things.
He could not leave the broken dreams of nine of the Fiend’s children lying in the Chrysalis for anything to find.
"Against terrifying enemies, I have to be careful," Noah said quietly, to the falling silk, to himself.

"I put my hand heavily into an Immense One’s bloodline today as I have been doing recently, altering their Curses or Sentences. That leaves marks and clues. And I cannot afford to leave clues to such cruel beings."
He looked at the nine, mad and splitting, their dreams hanging around them in torn golden clouds, and he made a grand decision.
"So there will be no evidence."
He opened THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer, and for the first time in his existence, he... devoured dreams.

He bypassed the Dimensional storms and drew the torn golden clouds off the nine dying Descendants and into himself, every hope and every dream these nine had ever carried, and he took them in and shut them behind his eyes where nothing that looked at the Chrysalis afterward would ever find them!

Emptied of the dreams their existences had been at war with, the Descendants went quiet. Then they went still. Then, one by one, with nothing left at their foundations to hold a shape, they simply ceased, and their whole burning Steeds ceased with them, and the region went dark and cold!
|You have devoured the Existential Narrative of nine Descendants and Steeds of THE Sleepless Fiend. No dream remains for any perceiver to read. In them, the event did not happen.|
|THE Provenance of THE Human Dreamer deepens. You have learned to take what you long only borrowed. +5 PROVENANCE, +3 VERITAS, +3 PONDUS|
Noah hung in the silence, bleeding, full of dead dreams, and he did not feel grand.
He felt careful!

He looked down. The three bound Dream Gu drifted free of their fallen ropes now that their captors were gone, and the little Common Dream Gu he had first come for still hung in its nest, awake, its many eyes on him, its small dream of warmth turning around it untouched by any of it. Four Gu!
His gains from this were grand, grander by far than what he had come for!
He didn’t sit and dawdle!

He debated taking the vibrant binding ropes or the sword filled with slivers of an Immense One as he was not foolish enough to carry things holding the marker and power of an Immense One! But could they be seamlessly devoured and broken down? He formed a bubble of blue gold dreams to wrap around them as he tried to analyze and devour even them rapidly.

He formed his Provenance of THE Human Dreamer into chains that wrapped around the Gu and drew the four of them to him, and golden jaws of an endless dream erupted out as they began to chew on the corpses of Descendants and Steeds that floated listlessly!
And...
Caution said do not linger. Caution said a place where you have just done something this large is a place to be gone from before anything arrives to read it!

For once, Noah did not argue with caution as he turned into a streak of light shooting in the distance, every step taking him Gigaparsecs away as he even intended to leave the region of Dreams of THE Chrysalis entirely!

Noah streaked across the vast reaches of THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering, each stride carrying him across gigaparsecs of falling multicolored silk and turning nebulas as dreamy light swirled steadily around his frame. Floating beside him, encased in a shimmering sphere of blue-gold dreams, drifted the spoils of the First Borns.
The obsidian rope and the pale crimson-white sword.
As his perception probed the sealed sphere, information surfaced in his consciousness, revealing the dark history woven into the very structure of the relics.
|THE UNSLEEPING BINDINGS|
|Classification: Immense One Relic (Defective Echo).|

|An obsidian rope braided from the harvested Causes of ten primeval Steeds who failed to bear the harness of THE Sleepless Fiend. It carries the unfinished cadence of his binding-sentence, burning through the unspent potential of captured existences to enforce an unyielding stillness.|
|THE FIRST BORN’S TOOTH|
|Classification: Immense One Relic (Severed Gaze).|

|One of nine blades carved from a crystallized fragment of THE Sleepless Fiend’s own peripheral sight. Forged so his eldest progeny could observe across the Folds of existence on his behalf, it perceives across THE SEAM and severs lifeforms. It has never been drawn by its creator.|
Noah kept moving, his eyes analyzing the dark script drifting within the blue-gold bubble.

"What happens if I devour the Narrative of an Immense One?"Noah asked, directing his thought into the illusory ring resting against his finger. "Consuming the Existential Narrative of nine Descendants granted an increase of Provenance and deepened my standing across multiple metrics. What would a weapon carrying the sliver of an architect yield?"
The ring took its toll, drawing a fraction of his authority.
|-0.1 PROVENANCE ESSENCE|
The records-cluster within the illusory band vibrated with sharp, derisive amusement.
|It yields an early burial, O Chance of Chances.|
Atlas’s words arrived flat and dry, stripped of any theatrical warmth.

|Do not confuse a sentence with the mouth that spoke it. Those nine First Borns were Descendants. They carried blood, instructions, and borrowed weight, but their Existential Narrative belonged to them alone. When you ate their dreams, you consumed a branch. It made you heavier, and because their depth was within your reach, you could digest that shit without choking.|

|These relics are entirely different. They carry fragments of the Weave itself. The Dimensionality of an Immense One is not a higher tier of what you hold, it is a completely separate cloth. If you attempt to swallow a sliver of the Fiend’s actual Narrative, your Provenance will not absorb it. You cannot digest it. The conceptual mass will sit inside your foundation as a jagged wedge of iron, tearing through your inner architecture while it radiates across every fold of existence.|

|It is poison that glows in the dark. It paints your entire presence in blinding phosphorescence, shouting to him as he is listening across the expanse: hey, I am right here. Trash them as quickly as possible. Drop them into the silk and keep moving.|
Noah thought for a moment before he sighed.
With a single flick of his will, the blue-gold dream bubble dissolved.

The obsidian bindings and the pale crimson blade fell away, tumbling into the endless cascade of falling silk. They drifted down into the deep, turbulent nebulas of the Chrysalis, their lingering weight swallowed by the timeless expanse as Noah accelerated away without looking back once.

He continued to move for minutes, crossing unmeasured expanses of the conceptual domain. Caution was not cowardice, it was simply the prerequisite for continuing to exist! He had been far too tyrannical for his own good recently as he...was Quintessential, but he was not invincible!
As he traversed the thinning drift of silk, his chest resonated. THE Dreamer’s Scale hummed with a quiet, steady frequency, attuning his perception to the subtle shifts in the surrounding medium.
Ahead, resting beneath the shade of a petrified conceptual bough, another soft luminescence caught his eye.
It was another Common Dream Gu.

This one was slightly smaller, translucent azure ripples pulsing through its rounded shell as it lazily filtered the ambient concept of dreams. Sensing the resonance of THE Dreamer’s Scale, the small creature did not scatter. It simply drifted, regarding him with calm, multifaceted eyes.

Noah reached out, letting a strand of blue-gold dream essence curl around the creature. It nestled against his palm, accepting the warmth, and he drew it into his internal realm alongside the four others.
Most of them truly seemed to exist with nature as they showed no aggression. These insects were wondrous things!
At this time, the architecture of THE Chrysalis began to shift.

The falling silk thinned until it vanished entirely. The dry nebulas of the Dream region receded into the distance, replaced by a sudden, overwhelming moisture that was not water, but liquid starlight.
The surroundings opened into a vast cosmic ocean.

Waves of deep violet and shimmering silver rolled across millions of Gigaparsecs, surging with the heavy concepts of Weight and Memory. Immense phosphorescent currents drifted through the depths, illuminating vast oceanic trenches carved from crystallized epochs. It was an aquatic expanse of raw stellar essence, where the pressure of ancient records pressed down with the weight of uncounted stars.

In the distance, suspended within a slow-moving whirlpool of golden light, floated a colossal mountain-reef. It stretched for thousands of miles, built from petrified stellar coral, calcified bone of forgotten leviathans, and dense mineral crusts that absorbed the rolling currents.

Noah descended through the shimmering waves without causing a ripple, diving deep into the interior of the floating reef. He slipped into a cavernous hollow shielded by thick layers of fossilized coral and crystalline stone.
He exhaled, the tension that had gripped his body since the descent of THE Unpaid Collector finally receding into a cold, steady equilibrium.

Inside his Provenance Realm, five Common Dream Gu hovered in a gentle spiral around the central river of light. Their soft luminescence mingled with the blue-gold hills, their small dreams of warmth and peace adding a subtle, stabilizing tranquility to the sovereign domain.
He summoned his status.
|VERITAS: 108|
|PROVENANCE: 115|
|POTENTIA: INFINITE|
|PONDUS: 104|
|OSMONTIAN MOIRAI: 135|
His attributes held firm in the Seam, anchored by the weight of nine devoured Narratives and the unspent Causes he had claimed.
The illusory band on his finger pulsed with renewed clarity, the presence of Atlas resonating within the quiet sanctuary of the reef.

|This place should be THE Tide,|Atlas said, his tone carrying the calm assurance of someone stepping into his own forge. |Weight and Memory govern this water. It blunts stray perceptions and dampens the tremors of the outside continuum. Nothing should interrupt us here.|
Noah looked down at his palm, where the very first Common Dream Gu he had found, the clean one that dreamed only of being left alone in the warmth, manifested in a soft coil of blue-gold light.
|Take the little one,| Atlas said, the records-cluster humming with anticipation. |The one that wished for warmth. We are going to teach it how to be an Elseengine heart.|
WAA!
Noah looked at the small lifeform resting quietly against his skin. It had simple Dreams. He would incorporate it into his grand and Infinite Dream!

Noah looked down at his palm, where the very first Common Dream Gu he had found, the clean one that dreamed only of being left alone in the warmth, manifested in a soft coil of blue-gold light.
|Take the little one,| Atlas said, the records-cluster humming with anticipation. |The one that wished for warmth.
We are going to teach it how to be an Elseengine heart.|
WAA!
Noah looked at the small lifeform resting quietly against his skin.
It had simple Dreams.
He would incorporate it into his grand and Infinite Dream!

chapters.title: Chapter 5714: Sleepless! I
paragraphs: <THE SLEEPLESS FIEND>
In the quiet spaces of a closed room, lifeforms placed behind curved glass will always establish a routine.

They wake, they swim along the transparent perimeter, they consume whatever flakes of nourishment drift down from the ceiling, and they believe the curved boundary of their water is the edge of all reality.

They engage in tiny, frantic conflicts over an inch of sand. They breed their progeny to believe that the illumination above them is an eternal constant, never realizing that the hand turning the light on and off belongs to something standing outside their sky.
It is a predictable cycle, observed with detached curiosity by anyone standing tall enough to peer through the glass.
In this vast, silent chamber, there were hundreds of such vessels.

They did not hold minnows or aquatic insects. Each floating enclosure was a self-contained Dimension, carefully anchored against the surrounding dark, with more than half engineered as hidden Elsedimensions folded away from the standard patterns of the continuum.

And the creatures moving inside them were Descendants, entities standing at THE SEAM or towering even higher, lifeforms whose bloodlines carried uncounted eras of unbroken authority, pacing along the transparent boundaries of their artificial skies without ever perceiving the room they occupied.
They even thought they left their Dimension to cross endless darkness and enter other Dimensions...but they did not know they only ever remained in one enclosure.
At the center of these floating glass domains sat a hazy, colossal humanoid figure.

He did not possess a body of mortal clay or dense bone. The silhouette was composed of constantly pulsing strands of brilliance, undulating threads of the Weave that twisted with quiet, immense authority.
This was THE SLEEPLESS FIEND.
Before him rested a wide, shallow dish carved from crystallized void.
Within the dish, pinned down by needles of solid law, writhed a chimeric lifeform!

It was an unnatural synthesis, woven from the boundless currents of Infinity, the raw genesis of THE Primordial Source, and the rigid geometric threads of THE Argent Loom. The creature had no unified identity, only an agony of incompatible foundations, its Dimensionality surging outward in violent, miniature typhoons that broke uselessly against the lip of the petri dish.
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND held a slender needle between two fingers of woven brilliance. At the needle’s tip clung a single drop of pitch-black ink, dense with the weight of sovereign records.

With cold, surgical precision, he pressed the needle into the chimera’s heaving flank. Sentences of pure intent flowed from the ink into the creature’s marrow, carving order into the chaotic blend of authorities.
"This is merely the integration of measly small authorities,"the Fiend murmured.

"A little Infinity to stretch the boundaries, a drop of the Source to fuel the combustion, and the Loom to ensure the structure remembers its place. With enough Narrative and a few Causes to bind the seams, you will be stabilized. Cease your noise. An existence that cannot endure a little editing has no right to step outside the glass."

The chimeric beast twisted, its conceptual shrieks rippling through the dish, but the Fiend did not press harder or withdraw. He simply held the needle steady until the ink settled into the flesh, watching the authorities cease their violent rejection of one another.

He did not hate the things he molded. Hatred was an unnecessary expenditure of kinetic energy, and an architect who had outlasted epochs had no use for pointless heat. Existence was an unfinished architecture, full of loose threads and unstable foundations, and someone had to sit in the dark and test which joints could bear the weight of what was to come.
He lifted the needle, letting the chimera rest in its newly stitched skin.
Then, the strands of brilliance that formed his visage shifted.
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND blinked!

His luminous eyes closed, the endless pulse of his form steadying for a fraction of an instant. Within the vast expanse of his awareness, a faint vibration ceased. It was not a physical sound, but the sudden absence of nine particular frequencies atop other 9 that had been tethered to his lineage!
"Curious," he said softly to the quiet room.
He opened his eyes, tilting his head slightly.
"Thpse sent out to gather weavings in the silk...their sentences have ended."
He sat in contemplation, tracing the faint echoes along the Weave.
"Not crushed by superior mass, and not broken by another architect. Not a scrap of their Existential Narrative remains for the cloth to remember. Who did they encounter in the dark?"
He tapped the uninked end of the needle against the rim of the dish.

"THE Chrysalis is a bit scary with those things left behind by that monster watching everything, so I cannot do too much. But... a little punishment across a tiny region where they died should be fine."
He set the needle down upon the table of void.
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND did not summon a weapon. He did not gather energy or prepare an incantation.
At the tier of Those Who Remain, power was not an accumulation of kinetic force. It was the absolute imposition of one’s Existential Narrative upon the fabric of reality.

He was THE SLEEPLESS FIEND. His entire existence was defined by an unbroken, eternal vigil, an identity that had forgotten how to close its eyes since before the First Sundering. His Narrative was an endless, suffocating weight of wakefulness, exhaustion denied, and consciousness forced to witness every passing epoch without reprieve.
He raised a single finger of woven brilliance and touched the empty air.

He did not look into THE Chrysalis. He simply selected the coordinates where the threads of his nine Descendants had vanished, and he wrote a short paragraph of his own existence directly into the localized Seam.
A mandate of pure, incurable insomnia.

The concept parted from his fingertip, slipping seamlessly through the dimensions, bypassing the physical folds of space, and anchoring itself into the conceptual bedrock of the distant region of the Chrysalis.
Having delivered the sentence, he did not wait to observe the execution.
THE SLEEPLESS FIEND stretched his luminous arms and let out a long, slow yawn, the strands of his jaw parting in weary indifference!
He turned his gaze toward another floating glass sphere, where thousands of young Descendants moved across pale cities, entirely unaware of their father’s presence.
"Now I have to send more out,"he murmured, the light of his eyes dimming slightly in boredom. "Dreams are the one thing that always leave a good taste on a sleepless existence."
Countless gigaparsecs away, within the boundless folds of THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering, the silence broke in unfathomably small corners of this place.

If one could pull their perception backward, looking across the vast expanse that encompassed the falling silk of the Dream region, the neighboring boundary of THE Tide with its rolling seas of stellar light, and the drifting continental fragments between them, the change appeared as an instantaneous infection of the continuum.
The mandate of THE SLEEPLESS FIEND descended!
It fell across millions of cubic gigaparsecs as a suffocating blight of pure conceptual rot!
The phenomenon struck directly at the living concepts inhabiting the region.
In an instant, billions of years of accumulated sleeplessness crashed into every entity drifting through the expanse!

The Dream Gu, creatures born to drift in gentle, half-lidded reverie, suddenly found their interior golden weather turning ash-grey. Their multifaceted eyes were forced wide open by an inescapable, agonizing alertness. They could not dream. They could not rest. An epoch of ceaseless, exhausting consciousness flooded their simple existences within a fraction of a second!

Their translucent bodies shriveled, the soft curves of their carapaces cracking into dry, brittle husks. From within the endless falling silk, thousands of Gu began to emit shrill, soundless shrieks of conceptual agony, their Trueness fracturing under the weight of an exhaustion their foundations were never engineered to bear.
In the adjacent reaches of THE Tide, the stellar water turned dark and turbid.

Aquatic Gu, ancient leviathans of petrified coral, and floating colonies of conceptual organisms writhed in sudden torment. Diseases of existence broke across their forms, lesions of corrupt memory and rotted weight festering in their carapaces. Entire ecosystems of living law withered in moments, collapsing into stagnant detritus!
It was a quiet extinction, executed by an architect who had not even bothered to watch where his finger fell.

And deep within the outer reefs of THE Tide, inside a hollow cavern of fossilized coral, Noah sat with a single Common Dream Gu resting upon his open palm, his mind focused on guiding its gentle pulse into the heart of an Elseengine, when the sudden tremor of an unraveling sky crashed down upon the sea!

chapters.title: Chapter 5715: Sleepless! II
paragraphs: <THE Chrysalis of THE First Sundering>
The fossilized coral cavern was quiet, shielded beneath thousands of leagues of dense, petrified reef as the deep currents of THE Tide rolled steadily overhead.

In the center of the hollow, Noah sat with his legs crossed upon a slab of compressed starlight. Resting upon his open palm, the Common Dream Gu pulsed with a soft, golden rhythm. Its translucent shell breathed in slow intervals, radiating a quiet reverie of warmth and gentle drift that soothed the surrounding air.
Floating within Noah’s internal realm, eight foundational elements hummed in alignment, waiting for the spark that would bind them to a living center.
Atlas’s voice echoed through the illusory ring, calm and instructive.

|The process requires absolute precision, O Chance of Chances. You are not killing the insect. You are not hollowing out its consciousness. You are extending your Provenance into its core, aligning its native law with the Elseengine until its small dream becomes the heartbeat of the domain. It must trust the warmth you offer, or the vessel will reject the weld.|

Noah drew upon a thread of blue-gold dream essence, letting it wrap around the small Gu in a protective mantle. The creature leaned into the contact, its multifaceted eyes softening as it prepared to surrender its concept to the architecture of the ring.
Then, at such a pivotal juncture, the ocean stopped moving.

The rolling currents of THE Tide froze in mid-drift. The deep hum of the fossilized reef cut out entirely, replaced by a sudden, total vacuum of sound that made the conceptual marrow of Noah’s bones ache with instant tension!
Above the reef, through the thousands of leagues of stellar water and across the distant expanse of the Chrysalis, something fell!

The descent carried no kinetic weight and no shower of falling meteors, arriving instead as an instantaneous infection of the continuum, a cold and suffocating decree that sank straight through the Seam and struck the bedrock of the region!
HUUM!
The water of THE Tide turned turbid and grey, festering with an unnatural, sickening stillness.
CRACK!
The Common Dream Gu upon Noah’s palm went rigid.

Its soft, golden interior weather vanished in a fraction of an instant, replaced by an ash-grey pallor. Its multifaceted eyes snapped wide open, dilating until they nearly tore through its translucent carapace. A shrill, soundless shriek ripped from the creature’s existence as its small, rounded body shriveled, cracking down the center until it was turned to a dry, brittle husk.
Before Noah could withdraw his authority, the decree reached into the cavern and gripped his own existence!
|WARNING.|
|The localized continuum has been infected by an Immense One’s sentence.|
|Existential Mandate: ETERNAL INSOMNIA.|
|Slumber is revoked. Reverie is severed. Consciousness is forced into an unbroken, infinite vigil across all folds.|
Existence vanished behind a blinding, jagged haze of absolute lucidity.
The attack was flooding his existence with a terrifying, suffocating rush of pure, forced wakefulness that crashed straight into the core of his soul.
Billions of years of accumulated purposefully made exhaustive sleeplessness poured into his mind in a single microsecond!
Billions of years!
He had only been alive for decades!

His eyes, already bright with the light of Sonder, flared with an incandescent, agonizing glare that threatened to incinerate his retinas. The concepts of rest, stillness, recovery, and quiet surrender were violently stripped from his consciousness, burned away by a relentless, crushing pressure that forced every perception, every thought, and every memory to stand at absolute attention amplified with exhaustion. The feeling of being so tired and hoping to give up and face endless darkness, but you couldnt!

Epochs of exhausting, ceaseless consciousness hammered against his sanity. His thoughts accelerated beyond control, grinding against one another with the heat of colliding Dimensions, unable to cycle down, unable to drift, unable to find a single moment of shade in an endless, blistering desert of awareness.
For THE Human Dreamer, whose very power was rooted in the fluid, boundless architecture of his humanity, the mandate struck at his foundational root.
His dream state fractured.

The gentle, undulating rivers of light within his Provenance Realm began to boil, turning into turbulent currents of jagged light. The blue-gold hills cracked open, bleeding pale steam as the concept of the Waking Dream was violently rejected by the suffocating insomnia choking the surroundings.
Noah fell to his knees against the coral slab.

Blood, thick and shimmering with stellar gold, dripped from his nostrils and the corners of his eyes, hissing as it struck the petrified stone. His fingers dug into the rock, gouging deep trenches into the calcified crust as his body trembled violently under the strain!

He could not breathe out. He could not find the rhythm of his own heart. Every nerve in his frame felt pulled taut across the surface of a dying star, stretched until the fibers groaned beneath the weight of an exhaustive eternity without sleep!

The decree was never aimed at him in particular, arriving merely as a casual flick of a distant finger, a minor punishment tossed out, yet it carried enough conceptual gravity to tear his Trueness apart from the inside out.
Within the illusory ring, an engineer vibrated violently, the voice of Atlas cutting through the deafening roar of Noah’s forced consciousness.
|Hold on to your foundation.|

|Do not fight the wakefulness by trying to sleep. You cannot sleep beneath the sentence of THE SLEEPLESS FIEND. He has forgotten how to close his eyes since before Existence was divided, and his mandate will crush any existence that tries to curl into a ball.|
Noah gritted his teeth. The pain inside his skull was absolute, an iron spike driven white-hot through the center of his thoughts, preventing even a microsecond of peace.

|A lifeform that has never broken believes it is made of solid stone. A lifeform that has had its marrow fractured, its thoughts burned, and its foundation hammered against the anvil of an architect knows the exact pressure the sky can exert before it bends. Pain is not an ending, O Chance of Chances. Pain is the continuum informing you of where your edges end.|
The ancient engineer’s words crashed into Noah’s suffering as an undeniable structural truth!

|Those who break beneath the friction are swept into the dust of forgotten folds. But those who can hold their shape while the heat strips their skin force the continuum to make room for them. Persevere, Dreamer. Persevere, and show this dead sky that a human does not need permission to exist.|
Persevere.
The word echoed in the depths of Noah’s burning mind, carrying the distant memory of an obsidian journal and the unyielding stubbornness of mortals who had dared to walk among giants.
He was THE True Human Emperor. He was THE Human Dreamer. He had cast out borrowed authorities, forged his own Provenance from nothing, and declared himself the protagonist of his own endless journey.
He would not be snuffed out by a thing that he had not even seen!
Noah raised his head, his pupils burning through the blinding haze of exhaustive insomnia with a cold, terrifying ferocity.
If the mandate demanded exhaustive eternal wakefulness, he would not cower and beg for sleep.
He would be awake.
He would take the ceaseless, agonizing consciousness that threatened to shatter his mind, and he would harness it to drive his own immensity!
HUUM!
Within his core, THE Telos of Adversity roared to life, burning with his Provenance!

The concept of struggle, the immutable law that pressure must forge density, erupted through his Existence. Alongside it, THE Telos of Existence and THE Telos of Tyranny aligned, locking together within his chest.
Noah opened the gates of his Provenance.
Instead of shielding himself from the Fiend’s mandate, he dragged the suffocating insomnia directly into his Telos of Adversity, feeding the conceptual rot into the furnace of his own sovereign laws.

The agony reached an unimaginable peak. His conceptual flesh tore, his veins blackened with the phantom exhaustion of billions of years, and the sheer trauma of the ordeal etched jagged, irreversible scars into the core of his foundation!
He paid for every second in raw, agonizing friction, his Veritas and Pondus groaning beneath the immense burden!
Yet, as the fire burned through his impurities, his foundation did not collapse.
It hardened.
|THE Telos of Adversity consumes the sovereign pressure of an Immense One’s sentence.|
|Your Provenance absorbs the trauma of ETERNAL INSOMNIA while never touching any semblance of the Narrative of an Immense One.|

|The concept of reverie is tempered in the forge of absolute wakefulness. Your Provenance is tempered in the wake of this exhaustion. If you can Dream even in this state, your dreams will be unfathomably grand ones.|
|VERITAS: 110 (+2)|
|PROVENANCE: 116 (+1)|
The blinding white haze gradually receded from his sight, leaving behind a cold, crystalline clarity that settled into the depths of his eyes.
The pain remained, a deep, phantom ache throbbing in the core of his thoughts, a permanent scar marking the day an architect tried to erase his right to dream. But Noah remained on his feet.
He slowly rose from the stone slab.

Around him, the hollow cavern bore the horrific evidence of the descent. The surrounding reef was drained of color, the fossilized coral brittle and crumbling, while outside in the depths of THE Tide, millions of leagues of stellar water festered in dark, diseased stillness. The mandate was still active, radiating across the Chrysalis, an active poison in the water!
Yet within the hollow, Noah stood upright.
His pristine body was marked by lines of dried golden blood, his dark hair disheveled, but his presence radiated an immovable weight that defied the rot pressing against the stone walls.
Atlas fell silent for a long moment, the illusory ring pulsing with a rare, quiet reverence.
|The mandate will linger in this region for cycles before the Chrysalis washes it clean. We must depart for a deeper fold. To engineer here while the air is poisoned will not be ideal.|
Noah looked down at his palm.

The Common Dream Gu lay curled in a tight, brittle ball, its carapace cracked, trembling violently beneath the ambient pressure of the insomnia that still choked the cavern. It was moments away from complete conceptual collapse.

Noah gently lowered his hand, his scarred, unyielding dream essence flowing outward, wrapping the small insect in a fortress of tempered warmth. Under his sovereign shelter, the Gu’s frantic trembling slowed, its fractured shell stabilizing beneath his absolute care.
Noah looked toward the dark, festering waters of THE Tide, his gaze steady and devoid of fear.
"The pressure here is heavy. The adversity is real. That makes it... the perfect forge."
He placed the stabilized Dream Gu back into the center of his palm, his blue-gold pupils locking onto the small lifeform.
"In the midst of this adversity, I will complete my first Engineering!"
HUUM!
