A single tear slipped from beneath the golden veil.
It fell through the amber light of the endless dusk, catching the faint glint of the setting sun, and landed with a soft, tiny splash into the cold, dark liquid of the untouched cup.
|I am sorry,| she whispered, her voice finally breaking into an open, ragged sob. |For the mountain.
For the silence.
For leaving you alone in the dark.
For how everything unfolded back then...
I am so... sorry, Atlas.|
The ring did not pulse.
The dark spikes along its curve remained rigid, sharp, and indifferent against the weathered grain of the table.
Atlas’s voice came through the iron one last time.
|What was done was done,|Atlas said quietly into the dusk. |But existence will be bathed in immense blood for what was done.
Existence remembers.|
HUUM!
Existence Remembers!
The Widow sat with her hands folded in her lap, her veiled face turned toward the dark iron.
She was thinking about many things when...
Then, the boundary of her sanctuary stirred.
It was not a physical vibration, but a cold, invasive tremor that rippled across the conceptual perimeter of her domain.
The slow rotation of the two golden halos behind her head froze instantly, their light snapping into a tight, defensive alignment.
Her gaze changed.
The sorrow that had broken across her voice moments before vanished, replaced by an absolute, diagnostic stillness.
She did not hesitate as her pale hand moved across the timber, lifting the spiked mobius ring from the table and drawing it into the deep folds of her private existence.
She wove layers of her own Narrative over the metal, burying the relic beneath sovereign obscurity until not a single trace of its weld could leak into the surroundings.

The fabric of the pocket dimension offered no resistance, yielding smoothly before an authority that did not bother to knock.

THE SLEEPLESS FIEND stepped onto the boards.

His arrival brought no violent shockwave, but the air turned instantly thin and suffocating, the steam from the warm cup flattening against the porcelain under the weight of an eternal, sleepless vigil.
His luminous visage turned slowly, his gaze sweeping across the quiet porch before settling upon the woman seated at the table.

The Fiend walked forward, his form shimmering with restless threads of the Weave as he stopped beside the wooden table.
He looked down at the two cups, his eyes lingering for a fraction of an instant on the cold one.

"Tell me.
Has your past lover made any moves?"
WAA!

chapters.title: Chapter 5721: Reflections I
paragraphs: The fine grey ash rested in a small, solitary heap upon the starlight slab, undisturbed by the slow currents of liquid luminescence that filtered through the cracks of the petrified reef as the heavy concepts of Weight and Memory pressed against the outer stone.
Noah sat cross-legged before the remains, his left forearm resting upon his knee as his breathing remained measured and steady.

The skin of his limb was whole once more, gleaming with a smooth, unblemished clarity as the boundless vitality of Infinite Sanguine Mana finished knitting the scorched pathways and shattered meridians back into seamless alignment.
Yet Noah did not immediately reach into his existence for the third Common Dream Gu.
He did not rush. He wanted to understand the reason for the failure.

He turned his perception inward, reviewing the sequence through the lens of his Infinite Provenance Baryogenesis and the foundational behavior of his Sanguine arts as the pathways of his meridians hummed with absolute vitality.

The Osmontian Tongue was his imperial dialect. The letter PROTAGONIST did not merely occupy space; it asserted an absolute, unyielding thematic supremacy over every concept it touched. It was a sovereign word that demanded the absolute center of the stage.
The Common Dream Gu, by contrast, was a fragile, unadorned creature. Its entire existence was built upon a simple, wordless reverie of warmth, soft silk, and being left alone to drift!

When Noah forced the terrifying weight of PROTAGONIST into its core, the insect possessed none of the conceptual tensile strength required to anchor the sentence. The carrier had cracked, dried, and dissolved into cinders within a microsecond, leaving the unleashed narrative with nowhere to ground itself except the meat of his own arm.
"It is letter that was too heavy for the insect,"Noah said.

|Mmm, it was too heavy,| Atlas replied through the metal. |A common insect carries the weight of a common life. If you want to write an absolute decree, you either find a rare existence that has the spine to bear it, or you learn how to whisper before you scream. Frugality, Dreamer. You do not burn an entire forest to cook one fish.|
Noah nodded faintly.
Then, his focus shifted across the continuum.
While his main body remained anchored upon the starlight slab in the depths of THE Tide of THE Chrysalis, Noah sent his consciousness to another body that was receiving a confirmation.
<The Vasiliou Elseworld>
The sky above Vasileia remained choked with pale, drifting debris as the shattered remnants of the mountain drifted listlessly through the void.

The magnificent golden terraces were reduced to broken mounds and tumbled pillars, the air thick with the stench of ruptured Provenances as the survivors huddled in the shadows of their fallen splendor.

Aurelius Vasiliou sat upon the broken pedestal of what had once been the lineage’s central archive. The stoic patriarch was bowed, his golden hair matted with dried blood, coughing violently as fractions of his damaged Provenance evaporated from his chest in pale mist.
Beside him, Thalia Vasiliou knelt amidst the rubble of the twelfth stand, her hands glowing with faint, desperate light as she tried to stabilize him!
Her face was pale, the graceful composure she usually maintained strained to its absolute limit as the weight of an unpayable debt pressed down upon her shoulders.
Noah stepped forward, his eyes scanning the shattered horizon before turning toward the wounded patriarch.
He offered no comfort and spoke no words of false sympathy, stepping directly before Aurelius as his voice cut through the weeping of the lineage with cold clarity.
"Did THE UNPAID COLLECTOR enter the Vasiliou Elsedimension before?"
The question dropped onto the broken stone like an iron weight.
Thalia froze, her hands pausing above the elder’s chest as she looked up at Noah.
Aurelius stopped coughing. The patriarch slowly raised his head.
Then, Aurelius let out a ragged, bitter breath.

"He did," Aurelius said, his voice scraping like stones grinding in the dark. "Eons ago. When the agreement regarding Thalia was made to secure his backing. The lineage signed the pact, and to seal the records, THE UNPAID COLLECTOR was allowed here. He stood upon our central terrace for less than an hour, drank our wine, praised the design of our mountain, and departed."
Aurelius lowered his trembling hands, his knuckles turning white.
"We thought the transaction was concluded. We believed the walls of an Elsedimension were absolute."
"They are absolute,"Noah replied, "Unless you invite the butcher through the front gate."
The patriarch offered no defense. He looked down at the shattered terrace beneath his boots, the horrifying realization of his lineage’s complicity in their own slaughter settling around him.
The Vasiliou had purchased their own doom the moment they invited an architect past their boundary, rendering any outside siege entirely unnecessary.
Noah did not linger to watch the patriarch drown in his regret.
With a single thought, he took his focus back to the depths of THE Tide.
Noah opened his eyes in the cavern of petrified coral.
The seed was real. Atlas’s answer held true.

An Elsedimension was not flawed by its inherent design; it was compromised only when its master allowed an outside architect to leave tracks in the marrow of its foundation. A domain that had never admitted an architect, a space completely untainted by the weavings of Those Who Remain, was genuinely unfindable and impregnable.
His grand design for his people was structurally sound.
Noah closed his eyes and turned his intent inward, reaching across the dimensional folds straight into the core of THE Infiniverse.
’Finish the layers of different realms of Elsedimension,’Noah commanded, his voice echoing across the boundless conceptual expanse of his origin. ’And prepare to receive... Provenance Lifeforms.’
The response from THE Infiniverse arrived immediately.
|Yes, Master.|
THE Infiniverse spoke within his existence.

|Also, I’ve locked down weavings of Laestrygonians and have begun pulling them as apart from Damodred, many more will soon be with us. THE Tide That Owes Nothing has continued to accumulate its boons as I am using it slowly.|
Noah listened to the report, feeling the immense, silent momentum of his home expanding beneath the surface of reality as his Infinite Sanguine Mana cycled with steady brilliance!

chapters.title: Chapter 5722: Reflections II
paragraphs: <THE Infiniverse>

Beyond the observable horizons of ordinary reality, deep within the private heart of an empire that existed outside the sight of many things, a sea of endless blue-gold light stretched across infinite leagues.
It was an ocean of pure dream-weather and sovereign potential, moving without waves or tides, reflecting a sky filled with trillions of turning constellations.
Infinite!
Standing upon the calm surface of this boundless sea were two figures in human form.

The first was THE Infiniverse. Her manifestation was breathtaking and terrifying in equal measure, her cascading hair composed of woven domains and crystalline void, her eyes holding the birth, expansion, and quiet collapse of uncounted civilizations.
She wore robes woven from overlapping dimensional lattices, her pale hands moving through the air with the absolute precision of a master architect at work.

Floating directly behind her were dozens of miniaturized Observable Existences, each one compressed to the size of a polished pearl, turning slowly in orbital rings. From these tiny wonders, thin golden threads were drawn continuously, dripping pure Distilled Cause Essence into wide, crystalline conduits that descended into the depths of the sea.
Beside those golden conduits ran eight radiant rivers of elemental matter.

Hydrogen, Helium, Lithium, Beryllium, Boron, Europium, Strontium, and Neodymium flowed in torrential ribbons of raw, purified light, looping around the pearl-like existences before merging into the grand design.
Above them both flowed a colossal cataract of blue-gold authority. It was the direct link to their Master’s Provenance.
THE Infiniverse took these streams, and with a sweeping gesture of her slender arms, she directed them across the expanse.

Across hundreds of realms spanning millions of gigaparsecs, the fabric of space and concept bowed. Entire clusters of Wheels of Existence and star systems, vast planetary sectors, and dimensional planes were being lifted away from the standard coordinates of reality.

The eight elements wrapped around their perimeters, Distilled Cause Essence sealed their seams, and the mantle of Provenance folded them deeply inward, transforming hundreds of realms into pristine, autonomous Elsedimensions.
No architect had ever walked their soil. No sentence from Those Who Remain had ever touched their skies. They were completely untainted, sterile to outside sight, and utterly unfindable!
Beside her stood Ruination.

Her manifestation was clothed in deep crimson silk, her hair burning like quiet supernovas as red-gold embers drifted from her shoulders. Her crimson eyes watched the folding of a Elsedimensions with tranquil appreciation, her arms folded beneath her chest as she leaned slightly toward her sister.

"Since Sonder awoke in him," Ruination said, "Master has become very reflective of others. He has been looking outward, thinking about giving those who walked beside him a chance through a single endless Dream."
THE Infiniverse did not cease her weaving, her fingers twisting a river of Europium around an entire realm of three thousand star systems as she listened.

"He has thought about his son," Ruination continued softly, her gaze drifting across the blue-gold sea. "He has thought about his daughter, his mother, the Queens of THE Infiniverse, and all those who helped him when his footsteps were still small. He knows they had their own grand dreams of brilliance before his shadow grew so immense that it covered their sky. He does not want them to merely survive in a golden cage. He wants to put them into an endless Provenance Dream of their own, letting them live their true dreams without the limitations of their origin."
Ruination smiled faintly, watching a miniature Observable Existence condense under her sister’s palm.

"Those who can endure the longest in their dreams, those who attain tremendous power from within their own reveries, will wake to find themselves far grander than they are today. Erikson, Titano, Ul’moreth, Eon, Kazuhiko... all of them were once the heroes of their own legends. If they do not wake from their dreams in a single day, they may step directly into THE Transfinite Verse when their eyes open. If they do not wake for weeks, an entire epoch of years will have passed within their Provenance Dream, and they might open their eyes to find themselves standing in THE INEFFABLE VERSE. Perhaps they will inherit and advance the Infinite Scales he cast out. Perhaps he will impart knowledge of sovereign engineering to their souls to see what they can build. He simply wants to give them a chance."
Sonder.
The realization that every lifeform drifting past possessed an interior existence as rich, complicated, and desperate as one’s own.

THE Infiniverse drew a massive band of Neodymium into her palms, compressing the perimeter of another forty realms until their spatial signatures vanished completely from the surrounding dark. Her expression remained cool, composed, and imperial!

"I understand Sonder," THE Infiniverse replied."I have observed how it operates in his eyes, and I recognize the mechanical elegance of allowing other narratives to mature. But I am not the biggest fan of it."
Ruination glanced sideways at her sister, an amused tilt touching her lips. "You find fault with his compassion?"
"It is not about fault,"THE Infiniverse said evenly, guiding a flood of Distilled Cause Essence into the foundation of a newborn Elsedimension.

"It is about geometry. To me, Master is the singular, absolute center of existence. He is THE True Human Emperor, THE Human Dreamer, the only point of origin that matters in any continuum. When he looks at others and sees the fullness of their lives, his vision spreads outward. I do not wish for his gaze to be diluted by the small concerns of mortals who could not keep pace with his stride. I want him to look upon reality as an author looks upon a clean sheet of paper, with himself as the only hand holding the pen."
HUUM!
She turned her starlit eyes toward Ruination, her expression devoid of malice, filled only with the cold, immovable devotion of an empire built in his name.

"Sonder makes him hesitate to crush what is weak. It makes him empathize with chickens before he drinks the soup. I would prefer him to be an absolute, unyielding tyrant who steps across existence without once asking the dirt if it minded his boots."
Ruination let out a soft, melodic laugh that sent gentle ripples across the blue-gold surface beneath their feet.
"That is why you are who you are, Sister, and I am the blood,"Ruination murmured, her crimson eyes softening as she watched the distant light of their Master’s Provenance pulse above them.

"You want him to be an engine. But that is why I love Sonder. It enriches his humanity. It prevents him from degenerating into a hollow equation like Those Who Remain. The architects who view living beings as mere sentences to be edited, Descendants as cattle to be slaughtered, and existence as an empty stage. They are miserable, sleepless monsters who feel nothing because they believe only they exist."
Ruination reached out, catching a stray spark of crimson-gold mana in her palm and letting it dance across her fingertips.

"Master is different because he remembers the weight of a single life. He knows the people who stood beside him were not scenery. They were the ground he walked on to reach the sky, and because he remembers, he will not discard them when the climb becomes steep. That humanity does not make him fragile, Sister. It gives his tyranny a purpose."
Ruination turned her gaze back to the endless blue-gold horizon, her voice dropping into a quiet, tender murmur.
"We also have dreams, do we not, Sister? Even if our dreams are to always lift him up..."

THE Infiniverse remained silent for several breaths. Her hands continued their flawless, rhythmic weaving, guiding the eight primordial elements into place as dozens more realms folded away into sovereign pockets of isolation.
She did not argue further, but a fraction of the coldness in her starlit eyes softened, acknowledging the truth in her sister’s words.
Together, the two manifestations continued their work in absolute harmony.
Across existence, nobody had had any conception of what was quietly growing in the dark.

Hidden beneath layers of absolute unfindability, THE Infiniverse was expanding at an unimaginable rate. Already, her engineered expanse held the conceptual weight and territorial immensity of several hundred complete Dimensions, folded so deeply into the bedrock of reality that if an Immense One looked directly at her coordinates, they would perceive only empty, undisturbed void!

chapters.title: Chapter 5723: Wonder!
paragraphs: In THE Chrysalis, Noah’s eyes focused upon eight microscopic particles hovering above his outstretched palm.
Hydrogen, Helium, Lithium, Beryllium, Boron, Europium, Strontium, and Neodymium.

They did not behave like ordinary physical matter. They turned in disciplined, concentric orbits, each particle emitting a faint, distinct frequency that subtly bent the surrounding light of the cavern.
Noah studied their rotation as his thoughts traced the architecture of THE Enduring Gu Elsedimension Ring resting upon his middle finger.

"Out of every mineral, metal, and authority drifting across Existence" Noah spoke into the quiet cavern, "why do these exact eight govern the boundary of an Elseengine? Why not stellar iron, refined gold, or crystallized void?"
From the illusory band beside his ring, a faint pulse of light stirred as Atlas manifested his translucent form.
The old engineer looked at the hovering particles with a flat, half-lidded gaze, crossing his arms over his chest.

|You think you are looking at mortal chemistry,|Atlas said. |You look at the names and your mind wanders to dirt and glass tubes of worlds with no authority, only playing with chemistry. These are not common rocks, Dreamer. When the First Sundering tore Existence apart, the grander Immense Ones did not simply leave a tidy path behind. They exceeded the Weave. They broke through the cloth, and the immense friction of their departure burned away their non-essential mass. What you hold on your palm are remnants of the eight primordial weights left in their wake. The physical ashes of those who exceeded that were scattered across existence.|
BOOM!
|Even lifeforms with no authority don’t know they harvest and utilize elements that could make unfathomable things when manipulated the right way...|
Atlas pointed a translucent finger toward the spinning orbits.

|Hydrogen sets the boundary of combustion, the original spark of expansion. Helium cools the flame into a stable, slow-burning mantle. Lithium provides the crystalline skeleton so the vessel does not wobble. Beryllium carves the internal channels to direct the flow of intent. Boron absorbs stray conceptual heat, buffering the interior so the expansion does not shatter the shell. Europium coats the perimeter, rendering the domain opaque to outside observation. Strontium lends geometric memory, ensuring the vessel remembers its shape after taking a blow.|
The old man’s finger shifted, locking onto the final, dense particle spinning at the center of the ring.

|And Neodymium. The inward pull. It acts as the sovereign magnetic anchor of the entire lattice. Without it, the other seven layers would simply drift apart into empty space. Neodymium draws the surrounding conceptual volume inward, folding leagues of space into an indivisible point. That is why an Elsedimension can hold an ocean while resting comfortably on your knuckle.|
Noah observed the microscopic pull of the Neodymium particle, watching how the local light bent slightly toward its core.
The mechanics were sound, but mechanics alone were only half of the equation.
Noah closed his eyes, turning his perception inward to dissect the structure of THE Osmontian Tongue.

Language, at this level, was not merely sound; it was existential geometry. The letters he had unlocked, I AM, OSMONT, QUINTESSENTIAL, HUMAN, and PROTAGONIST, were complete, self-contained monuments of narrative weight. To force PROTAGONIST into a Common Dream Gu was to drop a mountain onto a moth.
Yet every language possessed morphology.
Noah analyzed the anatomy of his words, realizing that a sovereign letter could be partitioned into its underlying phonetic radices.
The letter I AM carried the core radix of BEING, which provided stability, presence, and rootedness in reality.

The letter PROTAGONIST, when stripped of its crushing imperial supremacy, held the foundational radix of AGENCY. It was the pure, unadorned concept of self-direction, the will to move forward under one’s own power without demanding that the rest of existence bow in subservience.
A Common Dream Gu could never bear the title of an emperor. But it could understand the concept of being, and it could harbor the quiet agency to dream its own dream without interference.
Noah opened his eyes.
He did not immediately reach for the second Gu. Instead, he raised his right hand and summoned a thread of Infinite Sanguine Mana.
The crimson-gold energy did not erupt with its usual destructive brilliance. Under Noah’s absolute control, the mana thinned until it became a hair-thin filament, scarcely wider than a single quark.
He guided the thread downward, weaving it directly into the surface of the starlight slab.
Next, Noah called upon his Telos of Adversity. He introduced a fraction of linguistic stress.
The coral groaned, microscopic cracks threatening to split the slab as the concept resisted the medium.
Noah did not force it. He directed the filament of Sanguine Mana to wrap around the fracture.

The crimson-gold vitality flowed into the fissure, acting not merely as glue, but as an alchemical flux. It cooled the friction between the heavy concept and the brittle stone, cushioning the impact and distributing the narrative pressure evenly across the rock.
A sudden clarity settled in Noah’s mind.
He summoned a single droplet of Distilled Cause Essence from his internal void, letting it hover beside the filament of blood.
With a precise command of his will, Noah drove the two substances together.
The Infinite Sanguine Mana and the Distilled Cause Essence merged, swirling into an iridescent, deep-crimson fluid that pulsed with a slow, heavy heartbeat.
|Infinite Sanguine Cause Mortar has been forged for the first time.|

It possessed the fluid malleability of living blood and the eternal, structural permanence of a First Cause. It was a customized alchemical buffer, designed specifically to serve as a shock absorber between his sovereign tongue and a fragile carrier!
It was his own engineering and design not brought forth by Atlas!
Atlas watched the crimson fluid hover in the air, his translucent brows twitching slightly.
The old man remained silent, withholding any overt praise, but the lines around his eyes tightened as he recalculated his assessment of Noah.
Atlas cleared his throat, leaning against his illusory staff.

|Do not get arrogant,| Atlas said. |You made a decent mortar. That does not mean you know how to build a temple. Long before the First Sundering, the ancient First Lifeforms were so enamored with the sound of their own authority that they attempted to speak before they had grown teeth. They tried to shout commands at the sky, and in their haste, they bit their own tongues completely off, bleeding to death on the very soil they sought to rule.|
Atlas pointed toward the hovering crimson mortar.
|That is the Rule of being humble. Humility is knowing the capacity of your vessel. A mortal body must learn how to hold a whisper before it tries to roar an imperial mandate...|
The old man had begun to ramble on and on!
Noah carefully arranged his materials across the starlight slab in strict, methodical order.
From his internal realm, he drew the second Common Dream Gu, letting it rest gently within a protective dome of blue-gold dream essence.
Beside it, he placed nine droplets of Distilled Cause Essence, each one coated in a fine sheen of Infinite Sanguine Cause Mortar.
Surrounding them both, the eight primordial elements settled into their precise orbital distances: Hydrogen, Helium, Lithium, Beryllium, Boron, Europium, Strontium, and Neodymium.
Noah sat back, his breathing slow and rhythmic as he observed the assembly.
He would not carve his flesh right away. He would conduct a complete, theoretical dry run across the stone, testing everything until the margin of error reached absolute zero!
For the first time, he felt engrossed in a project that he wasn’t able to complete right away!

chapters.title: Chapter 5724: Foundational!
paragraphs: The theoretical alignments across the starlight slab concluded, dissolving the simulated fractures into calm ribbons of blue-gold light as Noah turned his full attention back to his own flesh.
He reached into his internal realm and drew out the second of his remaining three Common Dream Gu.

The creature rested quietly upon his knee, its translucent azure shell pulsing with a simple, unhurried reverie. It was small and fragile, breathing in slow rhythms that carried the faint scent of undisturbed silk, completely oblivious to the currents churning outside the coral cavern.
Noah looked down at it, his pupils reflecting the tiny insect as he prepared the strokes of THE Osmontian Tongue.

This time, he did not summon the raw, unmitigated weight of an imperial conqueror to crush the carrier. He drew upon the clarity granted by Sonder, understanding the interiority of the small existence before him!
The Common Dream Gu dreamed of enduring the cold, drifting endlessly through the dark while searching for a tiny pocket of warmth.
Noah did not seek to overwrite that dream. He met it.
He broke the Osmontian Tongue down into its fundamental grammatical strokes, taking I AM and fusing it directly to the core of THE PROTAGONIST.

It was not an assertion of tyrannical supremacy that demanded the sky bow down. It was the tempered essence of agency: the quiet, unbreakable declaration that an existence possessed the right to stand at the center of its own journey, to endure the frost, and to find the warmth that made survival meaningful.
HUUM!
From his fingertips, threads of Infinite Sanguine Mana emerged.

The crimson-gold energy narrowed until it split into millions of microscopic needles, so fine they bypassed ordinary physical dimensions entirely. Noah guided these needles forward, pricking the carapaces of the eight stabilizing elements spinning in their orbits.
Hydrogen, Helium, Lithium, Beryllium, Boron, Europium, Strontium, and Neodymium were simultaneously coated in a shimmering layer of Infinite Sanguine Cause Mortar.
Beside them, the nine droplets of Distilled Cause Essence were drawn into the formation.

Because the elements were shielded in the sanguine mortar, they did not clash with the pure potential of the Causes. The mortar acted as a perfect alchemical buffer, absorbing every stray vibration and cooling the conceptual friction that had detonated his previous attempt.
The nine droplets fused seamlessly into the elemental lattice, and the entire structure collapsed gently around the Common Dream Gu.
There was no shriek of terror!

The insect did not blacken, and its shell did not crack. Enveloped by the warmth of Noah’s tempered agency, the Common Dream Gu exhaled a soft breath of pure golden light, willingly surrendering its concept into the structural weave of the newborn Elseengine.
The lattice clicked into place without a single tremor.
The second attempt was at hand!

Noah brought his mind back to the golden anatomical diagram Atlas had projected, the intricate lines of the ancient engineer’s crowning achievement etching themselves across his thoughts with absolute clarity. Every channel, every anchor, and every elemental node along the Inscription was verified in a fraction of a microsecond.
Noah raised his right hand, pressing his fingertips firmly against the skin of his left forearm.
He guided the living Elseengine lattice inward.

The eight elements sank through the surface of his flesh: Hydrogen, Helium, Lithium, Beryllium, Boron, Europium, Strontium, and Neodymium. They wrapped around the radius and ulna, locking tightly into the marrow like an interlocking sleeve of starlight!
HUUUM!
Then, the script ignited.
Deep within the core of his bone, the Osmontian letters I AM THE PROTAGONIST blazed into existence!
BOOM!
The agony returned instantly.

It was not the chaotic, tearing detonation of a failed weld, but the deep, agonizing structural ache of living bone being permanently re-engineered into a sovereign relic. Two hundred decillion quarks groaned beneath the sudden, immense narrative density pouring into the limb, the sheer weight of an absolute identity pressing down onto the subatomic architecture.
Noah did not flinch. He did not let his arm tremble by a hair’s breadth!

His Teloi roared to life, locking with the unyielding supremacy of Quintessence to turn the crushing friction into fuel for the weld. The sovereign fire burned away the agony, tempering the marrow and forcing every letter of the inscription to seat itself permanently into his anatomy.
Light flared through the skin of his arm, turning the limb entirely translucent as the golden script took root.
Then, the blinding radiance snapped inward.
Crisp, magnificent prompts ignited across Noah’s sight!

|Limb Anchored: Left Forearm.|
|Carrier: Common Dream Gu (Refined Elseengine Core).|
|Attribute Boons: +50 PROVENANCE, +50 VERITAS, +50 PONDUS, +50 OSMONTIAN MOIRAI.|

|Permanent Effect: FOUNDATIONAL ACCELERATION. The rate at which the user processes, integrates, and purifies authorities and attributes is permanently increased by 100%. The Quality of your Provenance is permanently increased by 100%.|

The weight of Existence is drawn down onto every Provenance Telos Quark at a constant trickle, in every state: waking, dreaming, fighting, bleeding. He clenched his fist.
The air inside the hollow cavern warped slightly, the starlight slab beneath him vibrating under the quiet, immovable density settling into his arm.
It felt completely immovable!
IMMOVABLE!
<THE Boundary of THE Chrysalis>
A silent armada of three hundred silver vessels sliced across the perimeter of THE Chrysalis.
These were merely some of the hunting groups dispatched from the Dimensions of Immense Ones, a mobilization of Descendants carrying the absolute will of their Fathers and Mothers!
Standing at the head was Kaelen-Tor, a high-ranking Descendant born of the direct bloodline of THE SPINDLE OF UNENDING WEAVE.

Her skin was the color of unpolished alabaster, her hair pulled tight in braids woven with strands of refined argent wire, and her garments were cut away at the chest to expose a terrifying marvel of stolen architecture.
Etched directly across her sternum, pulsing beneath translucent flesh, was a massive Narrative Inscription.

It did not belong to the old mortal frameworks, nor was it a crude imitation of forgotten blueprints. The inscription swirled with an unnatural, forced harmony between THE Primordial Source and THE Argent Loom, lines of primordial origin twisting around silver threads of absolute subjugation. It flared with immense Dimensionality, radiating a heavy, suffocating pressure that made the void around her buckle and moan.

Those Who Remain had not remained idle after breaking the Great Engineer upon the mountain. They had taken his blueprints, dissected his corpses, and integrated his stolen syntax into their own lineages, breeding Descendants who carried engineered sentences within their very bones!
Now that weavings of that Engineer returned, they unleashed them!
Crouched beside her boots were seven Argent Loom Hounds.

They were horrific, skinless quadrupedal monstrosities bred exclusively from the flesh of failed Descendants, their ribs exposed like the bared frames of a mechanical loom. In place of eyes and snouts, their heads were shaped like heavy iron shuttles, clicking and snapping as their jaws parted to reveal rows of silver needles instead of teeth.
They did not hunt by sight, nor did they track blood.

They existed solely to taste the subtle, forbidden vibration of unauthorized Elsedimensions and the microscopic friction generated whenever an unregistered lifeform attempted to engineer something from the fabric of existence.
Across the vastness of the existence, hundreds of similar groups were advancing in interlocking nets, carrying out the directives of a dozen different Immense Ones.

They were a force sent to exterminate any spark of sovereign engineering before it could ignite a fire. Some were spread across Observable Existences and Dimensions and endless darkness and Narratives of Existence others didn’t even know...and also places like THE Chrysalis!

Though of course, any group given a directive and access to a place like this...was unfathomably more powerful that a group that could be passing through Observable Existences, or inside a certain Dimensional Provenance Train.
Before Kaelen-Tor’s eyes, the existential command of Those Who Remain burned with cold, radiant brilliance.
|DIRECTIVE: PURGE.|
|Some coordinates within THE Chrysalis demonstrate anomalous frequencies of existence.|
|Execute total unraveling of all unknown weavings, foreign lifeforms, and isolated folds.|
|Zero verification required. Zero survivors permitted. If you meet a powerful anomaly, instantly call for help.|
Kaelen-Tor’s eyes were devoid of cruelty or wrath. She carried only the sterile indifference of an exterminator tending to an overgrown cellar.
Her armada did not carry crude physical ballistas or basic elemental cannons. The vanguards practiced the refined butchery ofArgent Loom Engineering.

Racked along the decks of each galleon were tens of thousands of slender argent needles, forged from the calcified marrow of conquered First Lifeforms. When the hunting parties caught anomalous prey, they did not simply cut their throats; they drove these sovereign spikes directly through their existence and causes of their captives, pinning down their Depth, draining their Trueness, and unraveling their historical records to learn.
Ahead of the lead vessel, drifting peacefully in a hollow formed of petrified dream-silk, lay a small settlement of Primeval Ones.

They were an ancient, peaceful tribe who had inhabited this pocket of THE Chrysalis for Ages, their bodies carved from porous volcanic starlight as they quietly tended to a small nursery of Common Moss Gu.
They possessed no weapons, held no imperial ambitions, and asked nothing of the sky beyond being permitted to watch the slow drift of the centuries.
As the silver of Kaelen-Tor’s vessels entered their hollow, the tribal elders emerged, raising their hands in peaceful greeting.
Kaelen-Tor did not even look at their faces.
She did not ask for their names, she did not demand their lineage records, and she did not give them a single instant to speak.
HUUM!
Kaelen-Tor raised her right hand and tapped the center of her chest.
The Narrative Inscription across her sternum blazed with blinding, chaotic brilliance!

The Primordial Source roared to life, feeding pure originating heat into the silver threads of THE Argent Loom. A web of razor-thin silver light exploded outward from her ribs, expanding across thousands of leagues in less than a microsecond.
It was not an explosion of heat; it was an act of existential deconstruction!

The silver threads swept through the settlement, slicing cleanly through the porous stone dwellings, the nursery of Moss Gu, and the bodies of the Primeval Ones. The moment the threads made contact with an existence, they seized its narrative weight and pulled.
CRACK!
In the span of a single breath, the entire tribe unraveled.
Their homes collapsed into sterile grey powder. The Moss Gu shriveled into black ash, their tiny reveries snuffed out before they could register fear!

The Primeval Ones screamed without sound as their skin, muscle, and memories were stripped away layer by layer, reduced to spools of raw, inert conceptual fiber that were dragged instantly into the hungry hull of the Vessel.
Ten seconds after the armada arrived, the entire settlement had ceased to exist. Not even a ghost remained to haunt the hollow.
Kaelen-Tor lowered her hand, the inscription on her chest settling back into a slow, menacing pulse as the Vessel continued its forward glide.
Then, at her feet, the lead Argent Loom Hound went completely rigid.
Its shuttle-shaped head snapped upward. It drew in a deep, desperate inhalation, its needle-teeth chattering as it caught a faint, lingering current drifting across the spatial medium.
It was a scent that made every hound in the pack shudder with violent excitement.
It was the faint, phantom trace of a sovereign weavings carried by existence. Maybe a sign of Engineering!
The lead hound threw its shuttle-head back and released a harsh, metallic bay that rang like an iron bell across the silent fleet.
CLANG!

The beast lowered its iron snout, locking its trajectory straight toward the south, pointing past the boundaries of the petrified silk and directly into the deep, turbulent, starlight ocean of THE Tide.
Kaelen-Tor’s eyes narrowed.
"Alright, lets go see," she murmured, her voice flat and devoid of emotion.
She raised her hand toward the dark waters ahead, and with a single motion of her fingers her massive vessel advanced!

chapters.title: Chapter 5725: Existence and Time! I
paragraphs: <Pocket of Narrative Existence: THE Endless Dusk>
The spilled tea had soaked into the boards where she knelt.

The cold of the Fiend’s visit still hung in the air, and her throat still ached where his fingers had held it. She could feel the words he had pressed into her, sitting at the back of her jaw like a bruise. He had walked into her home and out again without once slowing his stride.
She had spent an age keeping still!

That had been the whole of her strategy. Stay quiet, hold what she had lost on the Mountain of Gu without stirring it, and maybe the currents would pass her porch by. She had told herself the stillness was a kind of strength. That keeping the past intact and undisturbed was itself a way of enduring.
The Fiend had taken ten seconds to show her what it actually was.

Staying still in front of Those Who Remain did not hide you from them. It only made you easy. An architect did not respect a thing that would not defend its own door. He looked at it and saw something that had saved him the walk.
The Widow got up off the timber.
The silk was wet at her knees. She did not look down at it. She straightened, and her spine came up out of the stoop it had held for Ages.
Behind her veil, the two halos stopped.

For as long as she could remember, since the sky over the mountain had gone grey, they had turned one way and pulled her grief inward, holding her still. Now they hung motionless for a breath.Then they turned the other way.
The grief she had been storing all that time stopped going in. It started coming out and hardening along the edge of her porch.
She reached into the deepest fold of herself, where she had buried it, and drew out the mobius ring.

She set it on the table, between the upright cup and the broken one, and pressed her fingertip to the spikes along its curve. She fed a thread of her own Trueness into the metal. The ring took it, and the line opened, running to Atlas past every thread.

"What are you planning, Atlas?"Her voice was level. "What do you want to do? I...will not do it the way I did it last time. I will give you my power now, and whatever else you need. I do not know if you meant this, leaving your ring with me. But I am going to try to believe in possibilities."
WAA!
The porch was quiet for a long moment.
The mist beyond the timber did not move, as if the dusk were waiting to hear whether the dead answered.
Then something turned over inside the iron and the metal warmed under her hand.

"Existence is full of things that do not care how safe you feel," Atlas said. "Everyone thinks they are untouchable. They sit up high, they build their little fences, they decide the sky owes them a favor. I thought so too, once. Grand workshops, a crowd of bright fools carving to my drawings, and I was sure my blueprints were law. I was wrong. I was loud and careless, and it cost me my hands."
The ring pulsed, keeping time with the reversed turn of her halos.

"I am quieter now, humble..." he went on. "Quieter, and meaner about it. When you have no hands left to swing a hammer, you learn fast which joint to tap to bring the whole ceiling down. You were grand once yourself, you know. Before you made a headstone of your porch, you walked the folds without flinching, and even Those Who Remain gave your perimeter room. What you did just now is a start. Hold your footing this time and you might...end up larger than you ever were. Maybe. Maybe..."
The records in the band turned with a dry click.
"So. There is work to be done. I have the first move already. An inscription. I want to take the eyes off them, off Those Who Remain. If they cannot see or hear...things become just a bit fairer."
<THE True Human Emperor>
Noah held his wrist up and looked at it for a while.

Under the skin, the inscription ran gold along the bone, keeping time with his pulse. He could feel the rest of it too, though there was nothing to see. The weight of existence coming down on every quark in a slow, steady drip, without him doing anything at all.
His arm just kept getting heavier and truer while he sat there, and he did not have to lift a finger to make it happen.
He flexed the hand once. The water near the slab pulled back from it.

Atlas flickered up out of the ring beside THE Enduring Gu Elsedimension Ring, leaning on a staff, squinting at the light under Noah’s skin like a man inspecting an engineering he half expected to find crooked.

|A clean Engineering,| Atlas said. |What I designed for you is not a static stamp. It is a living foundational inscription. Right now, it is at Tier 1, Incipient, because you fed it a common Gu. But its framework was engineered with open joints. The moment you harvest a Rare Gu that resonates with its grammar, or the moment your own foundation undergoes an existential elevation, you can feed it again. The inscription will drink the higher concept, widen its channels, and elevate its tier.|
Atlas tapped his staff against the starlight slab, producing a dull, resonant clack that echoed through the cavern.

|More importantly, it is an inscription bound to your very existence. Mortal blacksmiths forge armor that gets stripped away when the chest is cracked open. Weak sovereigns carve runes into their skin, and the moment their flesh is turned to ash, they become naked again. What you have carved into that arm is woven into your narrative continuity. Even if an architect descends and cleaves you into countless microscopic fragments, scattering your meat across ten thousand dead dimensions, your existence will still remember the Engineering. The moment your blood knits back together, the inscription will be there, holding its full power.|
Noah lowered his arm to his knee and looked at the old man.
"What about you?"
Atlas paused.

"You spent an age designing this," Noah said."You had the full set. Nine of these across your own bones, engines, all of it. And you still fell on the mountain. So which is it. Do you still have any of that, or are you just...an old man in a ring?"

He had walked into her home and out again without once slowing his stride.
She had spent an age keeping still!
That had been the whole of her strategy.
Stay quiet, hold what she had lost on the Mountain of Gu without stirring it, and maybe the currents would pass her porch by.
She had told herself the stillness was a kind of strength.
That keeping the past intact and undisturbed was itself a way of enduring.
The Fiend had taken ten seconds to show her what it actually was.
Staying still in front of Those Who Remain did not hide you from them.
It only made you easy.
An architect did not respect a thing that would not defend its own door.
He looked at it and saw something that had saved him the walk.
The Widow got up off the timber.
The silk was wet at her knees.
She did not look down at it.
She straightened, and her spine came up out of the stoop it had held for Ages.
Behind her veil, the two halos stopped.
For as long as she could remember, since the sky over the mountain had gone grey, they had turned one way and pulled her grief inward, holding her still.
Now they hung motionless for a breath.Then they turned the other way.
The grief she had been storing all that time stopped going in.
It started coming out and hardening along the edge of her porch.
She reached into the deepest fold of herself, where she had buried it, and drew out the mobius ring.
She set it on the table, between the upright cup and the broken one, and pressed her fingertip to the spikes along its curve.
She fed a thread of her own Trueness into the metal.
The ring took it, and the line opened, running to Atlas past every thread.
"What are you planning, Atlas?"Her voice was level.
"What do you want to do?
I...will not do it the way I did it last time.
I will give you my power now, and whatever else you need.
I do not know if you meant this, leaving your ring with me.
But I am going to try to believe in possibilities."
WAA!
The porch was quiet for a long moment.
The mist beyond the timber did not move, as if the dusk were waiting to hear whether the dead answered.
Then something turned over inside the iron and the metal warmed under her hand.
"Existence is full of things that do not care how safe you feel," Atlas said.
"Everyone thinks they are untouchable.
They sit up high, they build their little fences, they decide the sky owes them a favor.
I thought so too, once.
Grand workshops, a crowd of bright fools carving to my drawings, and I was sure my blueprints were law.
I was wrong.
I was loud and careless, and it cost me my hands."
The ring pulsed, keeping time with the reversed turn of her halos.
"I am quieter now, humble..." he went on.
"Quieter, and meaner about it.
When you have no hands left to swing a hammer, you learn fast which joint to tap to bring the whole ceiling down.
You were grand once yourself, you know.
Before you made a headstone of your porch, you walked the folds without flinching, and even Those Who Remain gave your perimeter room.
What you did just now is a start.
Hold your footing this time and you might...end up larger than you ever were.
Maybe.
Maybe..."
The records in the band turned with a dry click.
"So.
There is work to be done.
I have the first move already.
An inscription.
I want to take the eyes off them, off Those Who Remain.
If they cannot see or hear...things become just a bit fairer."
<THE True Human Emperor>
Noah held his wrist up and looked at it for a while.
Under the skin, the inscription ran gold along the bone, keeping time with his pulse.
He could feel the rest of it too, though there was nothing to see.
The weight of existence coming down on every quark in a slow, steady drip, without him doing anything at all.
His arm just kept getting heavier and truer while he sat there, and he did not have to lift a finger to make it happen.
He flexed the hand once.
The water near the slab pulled back from it.

Atlas flickered up out of the ring beside THE Enduring Gu Elsedimension Ring, leaning on a staff, squinting at the light under Noah’s skin like a man inspecting an engineering he half expected to find crooked.
|A clean Engineering,| Atlas said. |What I designed for you is not a static stamp.
It is a living foundational inscription.
Right now, it is at Tier 1, Incipient, because you fed it a common Gu.
But its framework was engineered with open joints.
The moment you harvest a Rare Gu that resonates with its grammar, or the moment your own foundation undergoes an existential elevation, you can feed it again.
The inscription will drink the higher concept, widen its channels, and elevate its tier.|
Atlas tapped his staff against the starlight slab, producing a dull, resonant clack that echoed through the cavern.
|More importantly, it is an inscription bound to your very existence.
Mortal blacksmiths forge armor that gets stripped away when the chest is cracked open.
Weak sovereigns carve runes into their skin, and the moment their flesh is turned to ash, they become naked again.
What you have carved into that arm is woven into your narrative continuity.
Even if an architect descends and cleaves you into countless microscopic fragments, scattering your meat across ten thousand dead dimensions, your existence will still remember the Engineering.
The moment your blood knits back together, the inscription will be there, holding its full power.|
Noah lowered his arm to his knee and looked at the old man.
"What about you?"
Atlas paused.
"You spent an age designing this," Noah said."You had the full set.
Nine of these across your own bones, engines, all of it.
And you still fell on the mountain.
So which is it.
Do you still have any of that, or are you just...an old man in a ring?"

chapters.title: Chapter 5726: Existence and Time! II
paragraphs: For a second Atlas said nothing. Then his chest shook and a cracked laugh came out of him, loud enough to bounce around the fissures.
"Haha. The balls on you, Dreamer. I like you."
He wiped at nothing under his eye and settled back onto the staff, still grinning, though the grin thinned out as he went.

|Yes, I was grand. And existence is full of things that do not care how grand you are.|He shrugged. |When they came for me it was not a duel. Many of them pooled everything they had just to get through, and even that was not enough to break the foundation. They had to use IT.|
BOOOM!
The word dropped!

|IT is a strange thing,| Atlas said. |The ones in the high seats cannot even hold it. They try to weave it in and their hands blister and their weavings come apart. I could hold it. There have only ever been a handful of us who could. That was the whole problem. They turned the one thing I could carry and they could not into the thing that broke my weavings.|
He looked away, off through the wall of the cavern toward somewhere Noah could not see.

|I am not going to tell you the rest of it here. Say the wrong detail out loud in a place like this and you invite eyes you do not want. But ask yourself how I am talking to you at all. A spirit does not survive its own body being taken apart. I am still here because of what I was, and I am not sitting idle either. Me waking up has already started things moving.|
He pointed the staff at Noah’s chest.

|Which is your problem, by the way. They are already moving. Descendants and authorities of Those Who Remain, the whole lot, out across the folds sniffing for anything that smells like engineering. They were nervous before I ever stirred. A few things happened recently to make them even moreso.|

|Someone reached for IT. Vakochev. He built himself scales, tried to stand against them, and they came together and ground him into nothing. The blood from that was barely dry when my old weavings started humming as they felt it. They know there is a hammer of engineering out there again.|
His face soured.

|So they did what frightened things do. They built a taller tower and unleashed...a Ruling of Existence. All those Mantles and rulings and systems you have been running into out there, that is not existence growing up on its own. It is a watchtower. They are spreading their gazes to ensure that they easily observe...more of existence.|
HUUM!
Noah sat still.
The Ruling, THE Provenance of Existence! They were a net, and the moment anyone worked outside it, the net twitched and the hounds came!
"A net," he said.

|A net,| Atlas agreed, pleased with him. |I have my own aims in all this, and things I will keep to myself for now. I teach you because you did something with odds that should be impossible, and you might end up bending them further than I ever did. The bending and curving of Probability around your existence is key. But do not mistake that for me serving you. I am still arrogant. I still have my Elsedimensions tucked in folds you cannot picture yet, I still have my engineering, and I still have myself.|
He crossed his arms.
|Enough about me. Are you going to tell me anything about yourself, Dreamer, or do I have to go poking around your edges to find out what you are made of?|
Noah’s mouth moved.
His gaze drifted somewhere past Atlas and the coral, and when he spoke his voice was unique as if he was a man reading off something he had watched from a distance.

"In the beginning, I was always born human," he said. "No inherent authority, no noble lineage, no spark. I had nothing but my ability to think, and even that, some in my early days might have judged as lower than average. But I was stubborn. When the world pressed down I did not break, and when obstacles appeared I persevered through them. I had nothing to my name. I rose from and forged everything I hold now, propelled forward by Infinity, Quintessence, and Tyranny. And, looking back on the journey, a healthy amount of luck."
The water barely stirred in front of him.

"The one major change came the moment I stepped beyond my original Observable Existence. Once I crossed into the different dimensions, where space and time no longer obey flat geometry, I stopped living in linear time."
He turned his hand over and watched the gold pulse under the skin.

"To everyday lifeforms, a life runs in a straight line. Yesterday, today, tomorrow. From this elevation, from the moment my Provenance fully awoke, moments do not follow one another like beads on a string. They exist at once. In one fold a body of mine sits in the brass corridors of a moving train, in a dimensional cabin. In another I stand on the shattered terraces of a golden mountain, looking down at a weeping patriarch whose home was decimated. Deep in my empire an ocean of blue and gold turns quietly while two sisters weave wonders into sovereign Elsedimensions. And here, in this cold hollow of petrified coral, I sit on a slab speaking to a man who died an Age before I was born."
He was quiet a moment.

"After I attained Sonder, I started looking at the people who walk beside me with different eyes. They are not scenery, and they are not instruments in my ascent. They are the protagonists of their own weavings of existence. I find myself wondering how their stories are progressing, and how much time has passed for them. Because for all of us, and for all these higher powers that rule the folds, time does not move in a straight line. We sit in this cavern where the hours seem ordinary, and in another pocket weeks or months could already have slipped away. It is all a matter of...time..."
HUUM!
Something slowed in his eyes.
"Time. Time, time."
He said it four times, the last of them trailing, like a clock heard through a wall in an empty room. The mobius ring on his finger buzzed against the word!
Atlas watched him for several seconds, and the cynical smile went out of his face.

|Yes,| he said, softer than usual. |Time is a terrifying and pivotal weaving of existence. Even I spent cycles trying to harness it for myself. Because with enough time, theoretically, anything is possible. A common stone can be pressed into a diamond. A mortal can build a bridge to the sky. An empire can learn how to bleed an architect.|
His staff caught a pale white light.

|I was going to teach you time much later as it has its drawbacks. Among the grand inscriptions that harness the different pillars of existence, the one tied to the flow of hours is among the most volatile. Too many possibilities. We could sit on this rock all day trading philosophies. But as you so eloquently pointed out, there is no... time.|
He paused, then broke into a loud, self-amused cackle.
|Haha. You see what I did there? Ah, being dead this long may have made me completely crazy.|
He shook his head, and his tone sharpened back into the focus of a craftsman adjusting his drawings on the fly.
|But your little speech shifted my plans, Dreamer. If your perception is already drifting off the line, we should not fight the current. Your next inscription will not be a shield.|
|We will make it about... time.|

chapters.title: Chapter 5727: Existence and Time! III
paragraphs: They would make it about time, Atlas had said, and the word was still sitting in Noah’s head when he tapped his left forearm against the edge of the starlight slab.

A dull thud went through the stone. No vibration ran up the bone. The skin did not redden. Under the pale surface the gold script sat there like iron driven into granite, steady and rooted, as if the arm belonged to a statue instead of a living man.
Then the water carried something through the stone. A thin scrape, faint, like needles dragged across glass, coming down from the upper shelf of the reef.
The band on his middle finger warmed. Atlas came up over his staff with a scowl.
|Stop admiring your arm,| he said, glancing at the ceiling. |We have company coming down the shelf. A pack of Descendants just entered the Tide.|
Noah did not move. "Did they track the ring?"

|Either that, your Existential Engineering, or the stink of the Gu you burned to ash earlier.| Atlas scratched his beard. |Doesn’t matter now. Those Who Remain still have working ears everywhere. I am building a way to deafen them, but for the moment their scouts are doing their rounds.|
"How much can they report back?"

|One pulse through Existence is enough. If a Descendant gets nervous and snaps a signal, no architect will bother sailing down. They will drop an anvil on the whole trench from above and wipe everything clean. Similar to what THE SLEEPLESS FIEND did here not long ago...|
Noah stood.
His fingers twitched once. In his chest, Tyranny pulled at him. He wanted to see what the arm could actually do against someone potentially powerful.
He set it aside.
Killing and battles was easy. Keeping the death quiet was the job.
"I wont fight them in the open," he said. "I will... build a room."
He walked to the mouth of the cavern. The water outside hung heavy and blue, lit in patches by glowing coral.

He raised his right hand, and instead of blasting mana out he drew it into threads no thicker than spider silk, coating each one in Infinite Sanguine Cause Mortar. The red fluid clung to the line, dull and sticky, smelling faintly of copper and old stone.
He cast the lines across the seabed. They drifted down and settled into the silt, weaving between the coral ridges like tripwires.

Then the eight elemental seeds. An engine compresses them into a ring to fold a pocket inward. Noah reversed the order and threw them outward. Neodymium into the far corners of the trench, its pull set to hold the edges shut. Europium along the ridges to swallow light and any scrying needle that came looking. Boron through the middle, to eat heat and shock before either could reach the surface.
Inside ten minutes the floor of the canyon was rigged as he used his Provenance, Distilled Cause Essence, and pivotal Elements to essentially make a trap of....an Elsedimension!

Above the reef the blue light faded. The water went murky silver. Long shadows dragged across the coral as the first vessels drifted into view, moving without a wake. Three hundred of them slid into the trench and spaced out in a wedge that closed off the open water overhead.

Noah stepped out of the hollow, climbed a broken coral spine, and stopped. His robes drifted around his knees, dark against the pale rock. No weapon drawn, no aura up. To the fleet above he looked like a wanderer who had drifted too deep!
At the prow of the lead ship, Kaelen-Tor looked down.

Her skin was chalk-pale, her braids tied off with silver wire. Her chest was bared to the sternum, and across the ribs ran a jagged scar where silver thread and dark red fire had been sewn together. It looked ugly, two metals beaten into each other before either was hot enough to melt, but it hummed hard enough to turn the water around her to glass.

Seven hounds paced the deck at her boots, no skin and no eyes, only pale muscle stretched over bone with iron shuttles for heads. Their jaws snapped, needle teeth clicking as they caught the scent off the seabed.
She did not waste breath on demands. To a Descendant with an order to purge, anything alive in an unregistered fold was trash to be cleared.
She looked down at him and lifted two fingers!
"Pin him," she said. "Take his records and memories"
WAA!

The silver hulls clicked together. From the bottom of three hundred vessels a lattice of silver light dropped like an iron grate, an Argent Loom array built to freeze a man’s legs, choke his mana, and hold him still while the needles worked!
It slammed down into the trench and hit the seabed with a dull crump!
Noah did not dodge. He stood under the falling light and watched the silver threads strike the ground.
The moment it came near him and touched the coral, the Infinite Sanguine Cause Mortar took the blow. The red sludge soaked up the force, darkened, and held!
Noah closed his left hand into a fist.

The perimeter snapped shut. Along the edges of the trench the eight nodes flared, Neodymium pulling inward, Europium turning the water black as ink to anything looking in, and the trench folded into itself with a dry snap.
The water did not shake. To anything swimming the Tide a league off, the canyon was an empty, blighted gully and nothing more.
Inside, the light died as an Elsedimension light years vast bloomed!
On the deck of the lead ship, Kaelen-Tor felt it go. She reached for the spindle at her wrist and tapped the connection that tied her to the Spindle of Unending Weave, and...
Nothing.
The thread did not glow. The line to her father was gone, cut as clean as if someone had taken shears to it!

She looked down over the railing. Through the dark water the wanderer on the coral spine had not moved. But the skin of his left arm had gone clear, and the gold script under it was bright enough now to throw light on the cracks in her own deck.
Haha. Had she actually found something critical?

She walked to the tip of the beakhead, boots clicking on the deck, and looked down through the dark water at Noah. Behind her the seven shuttle-headed hounds strained on their wires, iron jaws clicking in fast, nervous bursts.
She tilted her head, the silver wire in her braids clinking.

"Who are you? Are you connected to the weavings of Vakochev? Atlas? Or did you dig up an old bone in the mud and think it made you something? Before this becomes a mess of authorities, tell me. Are you a talker?"
Noah did not answer. He stood on the broken coral, arms loose, watching the silver plating of her vessel.
Her details resolved for him in clean lines.
|KAELEN-TOR - DESCENDANT OF THE SPINDLE|
|VERITAS: 212|
|POTENTIA: 218|
|PROVENANCE: 0|
|PONDUS: 206|
|INSCRIPTION: UNSTABLE PRIMORDIAL-ARGENT GRAFT (TIER 2)|
Kaelen-Tor took his silence for an answer. "A quiet one. Good. Saves time for me."
